### S2C 0x5B — PlayerRoomBalloonSet

*server → client* · key `0x5B` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **missing** · length: 24 (4+2+1+17) when the uid is found; only 4 bytes consumed when it is not. Always send all 24.

Locations: `0x004576C3` handler block start (primary switch); `0x004576D8` GetDataFromPacket u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8) into stack [esp+0x1B4]: uid; `0x004576EC` FUN_004189f0 entity lookup by uid (uid 0 means null); `0x004576F5` TEST ESI,ESI then JZ 0x44D7AD: break if not found

```
u32 uid
if(find_entity_by_uid(uid) != null) {
  u16 room_no
  u8 room_type
  str[17] room_title
} else {
  stop
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | UID of the player whose room balloon is being set. uid 0 or an unknown uid means nothing more is read. | stack local [esp+0x1B4], used only as the lookup key |
| `room_no` | u16 | Room number the player is in. 0 = none (no balloon, not clickable). 0x81 = cash-shop marker (the same value S2C 0x75 writes): draws sprite 0x168 with no title and the click prompt is 'Enter the cash shop?'. Any other non-zero value draws a room balloon, and c… | entity+0xE2 |
| `room_type` | u8 | Room kind. Below 4 = arena ('Enter the arena?', sprite 0x87). 4 = play/chat room ('Would you enter the play room?', sprite 0x19C, coloured title). Above 4 = battle ('Will you subscribe to join the battle?', sprite 0x87). Read even when room_no == 0. | entity+0xE1 |
| `room_title` | str[17] | Room title drawn in the balloon and used in the '[%s] %s' join prompt. Exactly 17 raw bytes with no NUL forced, followed directly in memory by +0xE1/+0xE2. Send at most 16 characters, NUL-padded. Read even when room_no == 0. | entity+0xD0..+0xE0 |

**Semantics.** Looks up the player by uid. If not found, processing ends. Otherwise it overwrites the player's room info: u16 room number (+0xE2), u8 room type (+0xE1) and a 17-byte title (+0xD0). All three are read unconditionally, unlike the spawn record, which skips type and title when the room number is 0. With room_no != 0 the client draws a room balloon over that player, and clicking the player offers to join that room (dialog 0x133 gets the room number and type). Send room_no=0 to clear the balloon. There is no UI refresh, no sound and no reply.

**Trigger.** Broadcast to clients in the same field when a player creates, enters or leaves an arena room, play room or battle room, so others see or lose the balloon and can click to join. 0x07 can carry the same state at spawn.

**Expected response.** none directly. If a viewer confirms dialog 0x133, the client sends a join request (not traced here).

**Gates / hazards.** No in-world gate. Scene must exist when uid != 0 (FUN_004189f0 dereferences scene+0x0C). An unknown uid is silently ignored. The title is used as a C string (sprintf_s '[%s] %s' at 0x44C968, Draw_Text at 0x431945); if all 17 bytes are non-NUL it runs into the room_type/room_no bytes, so always NUL-terminate. The balloon only draws when [game_state+0x4D8]+0x70 == 0 and g_ui_root+0x40 != 0. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C40, pvp_arena#25): a 0x5B carrying the RECEIVER'S OWN uid does draw the balloon over the local player (verified with a "Duel Room" balloon above the local character, cleared again by 0x5C). The server must therefore decide deliberately whether the room owner gets their own balloon.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 @0x4576D8), lookup FUN_004189f0 @0x4576EC with TEST/JZ break @0x4576F3/0x4576F5, then u16 into +0xE2 (IAT 0x4A4090 @0x45770F), u8 into +0xE1 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457729) and char[0x11] into +0xD0 (IAT 0x4A4098, PUSH 0x11 @0x45773C, call @0x457745), then JMP break. There is no condition between the three reads. They differ only in how the DSL writes it: A 'if(found){...} else {stop}' versus B 'if(null){stop} ...'. Both put the same 24 bytes in the same order, so neither is wrong. I chose A's explicit if/else form. B's extra facts are verified: S2C 0x75 writes +0xE2=0x81 at 0x457FD3; type/title are read unconditionally here but only when +0xE2 != 0 in the spawn record (0x44F03C JZ 0x44F07C); and the render gates at 0x4317B3..0x4317CD. A's render and click details are verified at 0x4317DA..0x4318F2 and 0x44C8C5..0x44C9AE. Other references: memory note project_local_player_spawn.md calls +0xE2 'marriage'; the binary shows it is the room number/balloon, though that note's read order matches. Not present in PySlayer server_packets or the KR Hex-Rays excerpt. Our server has no builder.

**Open questions.**
- Exact numbering of room_type values 0..3 (arena sub-modes) and values above 4 (battle kinds) is not resolved.
- The C2S join request sent after confirming dialog 0x133 was not traced.
- [RESOLVED by live verification pvp_arena#25, 2026-09-17] Live: yes - 0x5B for the receiver's own uid draws the balloon above the local player and 0x5C removes it, so sending it to the owner is a deliberate server choice, not a no-op. Original question: "Whether the owning player also needs 0x5B (their own balloon is drawn from the same entity fields) or only observers."

| `room_type` | u8 | must be 4 (play/chat room). The renderer builds the row text only when type==4; any other value draws stale text. The join path stores it into [game+0x4CC]+0xF70 and sends it in C2S 0x1A. | room+0x17 |
| `map_id` | u16 | map/stage id of the play room. Filter control 0x17 of window 0x478 shows only rooms with map_id==0x26AF (9903). The client's play-room create (C2S 0x18) hardcodes 0x26AF; arena create sends 0x264B/0x264C. This field is read BEFORE has_password on the wire. | room+0x22 |
| `has_password` | bool | locked room: lock sprite 0x7D; joining opens password window 0x4A | room+0x20 |

**Semantics.** Starts a new Play&Chat room list (window 0x478). Prologue at 0x455A2A: RemoveHead + free every room in the list at game+0x450 (head +0x454, count +0x45C); if window 0x478 exists, clear its UI rows; set label control 0x14 to '0'; FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) dismisses message box 0x16. It then parses rows like 0xA0: every row goes to the head of the list at game+0x450 and of window 0x478's UI list (FUN_00489a80 with param 1). There is no type check, no can-enter check and no filter, so rows appear in reverse arrival order. Afterwards label 0x14 = sprintf('%u', count[game+0x45C]) and FUN_00489c50(0x478,1).

**Trigger.** Send when the player opens the P-key 'Play&Chat Room' list; the client opens window 0x478 itself and sends C2S 0x74 with no payload. C2S 0x75 is sent when it closes.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** No player-object dereference, so it is safe outside the world. room_type must be 4, or the row renders with garbage/stale text. Rows are not de-duplicated. Name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes.

**References.** PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0xA1.py uses the same layout (name17, u16 1, u8 8 maxuser, u8 4 curruser, u8 3, u8 4, u16 1, u8 IsLocked); PySlayer's '??' bytes are room_level, room_type=4 and map_id. PySlayer sends 0xA1 for C2S 0x2C code 4; the EN client instead requests this list with C2S 0x74 (no payload). Not in our server.

**Open questions.**
- What map 9903 (0x26AF) is and whether other map_ids are valid for play rooms
- Side effects of FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) when no message box is pending

### C2S 0x2F — MessengerFriendListRequest

*client → server* · key `0x44EF4F/0x2F` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 0

Locations: `0x44E38F` S2C 0x03 handler entry (character/world info + map load); the send is at its tail; `0x44E52F` calls FUN_0046f860(messenger), which resets messenger state and sets messenger+0x74 = g_s…; `0x46F934` MOV [messenger+0x74], g_sock_game; only if messenger+0x70 (ui root), messenger+0x68 (app)…; `0x46F709` CMessenger ctor sets +0x74 = 0

```
(empty payload)
```

**Semantics.** Opcode-only request from the messenger (friend list) subsystem. Earlier in the same S2C 0x03 handler, FUN_0046f860 re-initializes CMessenger: it clears the friend-list state and copies the local name from player+0x48+0x1BE and fields +0x1D8/+0x1CF. At the end of the handler, after the map is loaded, the UI is refreshed and timers 6 (240000 ms) and 0xB (7000 ms) are armed, the client sends a bare 0x2F on the messenger's socket (the game socket). Nothing is Added before or after the opcode. The only other Add(0x2F) in the binary is this one. It is fire-and-forget: the client does not wait for a reply before continuing to the 0x63 send.

**Trigger.** Automatic, at the end of every S2C 0x03 (world/map info) handler, i.e. after each map load, both on entering the world and on map change. Always immediately followed by C2S 0x63.

**Expected response.** Probably S2C 0x0B friend list, handled in SubHandler3 on the messenger object and read through messenger+0x74: u8 unk (messenger+0xD1), u8 count, repeat(count){ str[17] name, u8 unk, u32 unk, u8 state }. The client does not require a reply.

**Gates / hazards.** Sent only if [app+0x4E4]+0x74 != 0, i.e. FUN_0046f860 found a UI root, an app pointer and g_sock_game. app+0x4E4 itself is dereferenced without a null check here and at 0x44E52F, so it must exist (allocated at app init). Because this runs on every 0x03, a server that answers 0x2F with a friend list resends that list on every map change.

**References.** The live capture shows 0x2F with 0 bytes sent right after a map loads, which agrees. windslayer_server.py _dispatch consumes 0x2F with the log 'arena query — ignoring'. That label is WRONG: the packet comes from CMessenger (friend list), not the arena. The arena room list is C2S 0x2C/0x2D. PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x2F.py is an unrelated S2C 0x2F (the same number means something else in the other direction); PySlayer has no C2S 0x2F parser. Our server comment 'no heartbeats arrived after 0x2F+0x63' matches the send order.

**Open questions.**
- Name is inferred from the owning object (CMessenger, whose S2C handlers 0x0B-0x10/0x60-0x62/0x78/0x7A-0x7E carry friend-list, 1:1 chat and mentor strings); no UI string names 0x2F directly. Friend list vs. full messenger sync (friends + mentor) is not proven.
- Whether the original server answered with 0x0B, and whether other messenger packets (e.g. 0x7B mentor info) also followed, is unknown.

```
u32 friend_id
str[17] friend_name
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `friend_id` | u32 | Server id of the friend to remove, echoed exactly as the server gave it. The same field is used by C2S 0x33 chat invite and matched by S2C 0x60 status updates. | Dialog 0x17A +0x134. Written at 0x472B46 from friend_node+0x18, the friend_id the server sent in S2C 0x0B (friend list)… |
| `friend_name` | str[17] | Character name of the friend to remove, NUL-terminated and zero-padded to 17 bytes. Stale bytes are not possible on the normal path because the buffer is memset first. | Text buffer (+0x50) of control 4 of dialog 0x17A. FUN_004838c0 at 0x472B56 zeroes 0x81 bytes, then copies friend_node+0… |

**Semantics.** Asks the server to remove a friend from the player's friend list. The client changes nothing locally when it sends: the list node, the count (messenger+0xD0) and the '(count/capacity)' label only change when S2C 0x0E arrives. The body is fixed at 22 bytes: 0x32, u32 friend_id (LE), 17 name bytes. There is no ResetBuffer call; the packet is built with Add calls and flushed with Send(1), like the other messenger sends (0x30/0x31/0x33/0x34/0x5C). Flow: the player selects a row in the friend list window 0x176 and clicks button 9. The UI script opens confirm dialog 0x17A; the code copies the selected node's friend_id into dialog+0x134 and its name into control 4. Clicking button 2 (OK) of dialog 0x17A sends this packet and closes the dialog.

**Trigger.** Friend list window 0x176 ('My Friends'): select a friend, click button 9 (Delete). Then click button 2 (OK/Yes) in confirm dialog 0x17A, which probably uses UILng 8001 'Would you like to delete the character from your Friend List?' and 8002 'Name of Friend's' (inferred). This is the only trigger: FUN_0046ffe0 has one caller (0x47303D), and window id 0x17A appears only in FUN_00472900.

**Expected response.** S2C 0x0E FriendDeleteResult (handler 0x470D35): u8 success, str[17] name. If success != 0: popup '<name> is deleted from friend list.', then FUN_004721e0 unlinks every friend node whose name exactly matches (strcmp) and redraws window 0x176 and the (count/capacity) label. If success == 0: popup 'Deleting <name> from your friend list failed. Please again in a few minutes.' The server should echo friend_name byte-exactly, because removal is by name, not by friend_id.

**Gates / hazards.** Send-time gates, in order: (1) dialog 0x17A must be found in the ui_root+0x5C0 window list; otherwise 'Please select a character name. ' and no send. (2) messenger+0x74 must be non-NULL; it is NULL until the first S2C 0x03. (3) Control 4 of dialog 0x17A must exist (EDI != NULL). If (2) or (3) fails, nothing is sent and there is no message, but the dialog still closes. Nothing checks that friend_id is non-zero or that the name is still in the list. Open-time gates (button 9 of 0x176): a row must be selected (+0xEC != 0), otherwise the message is shown and 0x17A is closed. HAZARD: if FUN_00459fd0 returns NULL or dialog 0x17A is not found, +0x134 and control 4 are not refreshed, so OK would send whatever an earlier use left there. The code does not reset them. In the mentor tab (FUN_00470270 else-branch), buttons 8 and 9 of window 0x176 are put in state 3 (FUN_00489320(0x176,9,3)), which probably disables them, so deletion should only be reachable from the friend tab.

**References.** PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x0B/0x0C (friend_id source) and S2C 0x0E (FriendDeleteResult: 'Reply to C2S 0x32 (delete friend: u32 friend_id, str[17] name), sent from the delete-confirm dialog 0x17A'), which matches this derivation. Sibling messenger sends in the same class with the same register convention: 0x46FF17/0x30 FriendAddRequest, 0x470224/0x31, 0x470084/0x33, 0x47025F/0x34, 0x46FFD8/0x5C (FUN_0046ff70, the function right before, ESI/EDI convention). Missing from protocol_spec.json because the Ghidra scout only annotated plain CALL [0x4A4108] sites and this one is a tail JMP. PySlayer: server_packets/__init__.py imports opcode_0x32 inside try/except but the file does not exist; there is no C2S parser. Our server (windslayer_server.py, wsproto.py) has no 0x32 handling and no friend system. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C43, social_friend#06): captured live byte for byte - payload 21 B "02 00 00 00 42 6F 62 00*14" = u32 friend_id (2) followed by str[17] "Bob", exactly the grammar above. (This spec was missing from the earlier protocol_spec.json snapshot that the verification matrix was written against; it is present and correct in this corpus.)

**Open questions.**
- Whether the original server keyed the deletion on friend_id or friend_name (the client sends both; the S2C 0x0E reply removes by name only).
- The mapping of window 0x17A and button 9 to UILng strings 8001/8002 ('delete from Friend List') is inferred from lng ordering (0x17C->8006, 0x17D->8007) and the S2C 0x0E strings, not from a parsed UI definition file.
- Whether FUN_00489320 state 3 really disables button 9 in the mentor tab. If not, a selected mentor record (+0x18/+0x00) would be sent in the same 0x32 layout.
- Whether the other 0x17A buttons (cancel/close) are handled only by the UI script: FUN_00472900 ignores every param_3 except 2 for window 0x17A.

S2C 0x0F results: 2 = ?, 3 = refused personal chat, 4 = rejecting chatting, 5 = room full, 6 = in conversation with another player, 8 = not online. EN lng 2729 'Ruquest#to#Conversate'. PySlayer has no C2S parser. Our server has no handler.

**Open questions.**

```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text_len` | u8 | Length of the chat text in bytes. It is the low byte of the strlen the caller passes (param_2); Add(uchar) pushes EBX, so only BL is sent. | caller's strlen of the text. From FUN_00444a30 it is strlen(CIME+0x104). From FUN_0043db00 it is strlen of the macro sl… |
| `text` | str[text_len] | Chat text for the messenger chat room. Exactly text_len raw bytes with no terminator (Add(char*,N) with N = movzx BL at 0x470177). | CIME result string (DAT_0070e708+0x104) or the macro text slot |

**Semantics.** Sends one line of chat into the messenger/friend conversation room the player is currently in (room id held at CMessenger+0xcc). The client does NOT show its own line locally. It waits for the server's S2C 0x61 relay, which prints "<name> : " and " text" in window 0x177. The line is colored 0xffc766a6 when the name equals the player's own name (CMessenger+0x7c), otherwise 0xff3277cc.

**Trigger.** The player presses Enter with text in the messenger chat window (UI 0x177, 'Messenger Window'), or presses a chat-macro hotkey while window 0x177 is the focused window (g_ui_root+8 == 0x177) and that window's state (+0x3c) != 1. Otherwise the macro goes to normal chat through FUN_00444a90.

**Expected response.** S2C 0x61 to every member of the room, the sender included: str[17] sender_name, u8 len, str[len] text. It is only processed while CMessenger+0xcc (room_id) != 0.

**Gates / hazards.** No send when: CMessenger socket (+0x74) is NULL, the text pointer is NULL, or CMessenger+0xcc (room_id, set by S2C 0x0F result=1) == 0. Also no send when ENGINE.DLL Curse_Engine_Clean(text) returns false; the client then prints 'No cursing please' (color 0xfffdf34c) to the chat log. After the IME path the client calls CIME::ResetResultString and memsets player+0x14d8 (0x3d bytes). HAZARD for the relay: the S2C 0x61 handler reads len bytes into a 64-byte stack buffer and then sprintf_s(" %s") into a 0x3d (61) byte buffer. The server must relay len <= 58, otherwise sprintf_s hits the invalid-parameter handler (client abort), and len >= 64 also leaves the text unterminated.

**References.** Same shape as the normal chat C2S 0x03 capture ("02 68 69" = u8 len + text), but scoped to the messenger room. PySlayer has no C2S parser for 0x35. Our server's _dispatch has no 0x35 branch. The UI string 2675 'Messenger Window' names window 0x177.

**Open questions.**
- What maximum length does the IME impose on the 0x177 input box? The client-side buffer at player+0x14d8 is 0x3d bytes, which suggests <= 60 chars, but this was not verified.
- Does the server echo S2C 0x61 back to the sender? The client never echoes locally, so it must, or the sender never sees their own line.

```

**Semantics.** Tells the server that the local player left the messenger chatting room. The packet is only the opcode. When window 0x177 (the chatting-room window) changes to state 1 (hidden), the client frees that window's two local lists: chat lines at +0xB0 and participants at +0xC0, whose count at +0xC8 is checked against 10 in 'The chatting room is full'. It then zeroes CMessenger+0xCC, the room id that S2C 0x0F wrote at 0x470E60 when result==1, and sends 0x36. No room id goes on the wire, so the server has to track which room the session is in. The packet is sent even if the player never joined a room, because only the window's visibility matters. The server must accept 0x36 from a player who is in no room.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts found the same wire format: the opcode byte only, built by FUN_00472790 with Add(u8 0x36) at 0x4728DA and Send(1) at 0x4728E5 on CMessenger+0x74. The only disagreement was notation: A wrote the grammar as '(empty - opcode byte only)' and B wrote 'stop'. The asm shows no other Add between the window lookup and Send, and no ResetBuffer or AddToHead. The caller path is confirmed: state switch table 0x44B848 entry 1 is 0x4466DF, then EBX==0x177 leads to 0x446925 and the call at 0x446930. Both are right on content. B's 'stop' is used because it is valid DSL for a zero-byte body. A's extra detail is also verified: S2C 0x0F stores a u32 room id at +0xCC (0x470E58/0x470E60), and this packet zeroes it. The packet is not in PySlayer client_packets, the windslayer_server.py _dispatch, or the captures.

**Open questions.**
- Which S2C (if any) a server should broadcast to the remaining room members on leave; 0x61/0x62 are room-gated handlers but were not decoded here.

**Semantics.** Buys more friend-list slots at the Frenaiga NPC service window 0x47B. On OK (ctrl 2) the client checks gold >= 50,000 and friend capacity (CMessenger+0xD1) < 50, then sends the bare opcode. It does not deduct gold or raise capacity locally; the server must do both and report back with S2C 0x9D. No amount or slot count is sent, so the server decides the increment and the price. CMessenger+0xD0 is the current friend count and +0xD1 the capacity; S2C 0x0B fills capacity first.

CMessenger+0x74 is not NULL-checked on this path, so the client crashes if the messenger was never initialised (S2C 0x03). The 50000 check is only a minimum-gold gate; the actual cost comes from the server through the u64 gold in 0x9D.

The difference was notation only ('(empty...)' vs 'stop'). The asm shows no Add on this path between the capacity gate at 0x47367C and the Send tail. The shared tail at 0x4736FE only reloads ECX=[EBX+0x74] before Send, so the u32/str[17] Adds of the 0x6D branch (0x4736C9-0x4736F6) are not on the 0x73 path. The naive scout wrongly merged the two branches. EDI is still 1: it is set at 0x472928 and not written on the route 0x47292D -> 0x472DC1 -> 0x47320A -> 0x473615 -> 0x47363E. On the expected response A is right and B's 'not identified' is superseded: S2C 0x9D at 0x471F07 reads u8 result, then u8 into CMessenger+0xD1 (0x471F33/0x471F3A) and u64 into info+0x228 (0x471F56), and prints '(%u/%u)' from +0xD0/+0xD1. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.

**Open questions.**

- The 0x9D success text is the generic 'You added him/her on your friend list' string; whether another S2C was intended for expansion is unknown, but 0x9D is the only handler that writes +0xD1 besides init/0x0B.

| `name` | str[17] | Friend character name (NUL-padded). The node is zeroed first (0x28 bytes), so a name using all 17 bytes is still terminated. | new friend node (operator new 0x28) +0x00 |

| `status` | u8 | Online status, zero-extended to u32. 1 = offline: drawn grayed, sorted after online friends, and a chat invite shows "is not on line.". 0 = online (0x60 prints "has logged in. (Friend)"). 4 = online on a channel (0x60 prints the channel number). Any other val… | node+0x20 (node+0x24 byte forced to 0) |

**Semantics.** Replaces the whole friend list. The handler frees every existing node, stores the capacity at messenger+0xD1, then builds one zeroed 0x28-byte node per entry (name +0x00, channel +0x14, friend_id +0x18, status +0x20, +0x24=0) and appends it to the CPList at messenger+0x04. Last, FUN_00470270 copies the list count into messenger+0xD0, redraws friend window 0x176 (entries with status != 1 are added first, then status == 1) and sets the "(count/capacity)" label. No reply is sent. Returns 1 (handled). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50/C52, social_friend#00): EN labels - window 0x176 is captioned "My Friends" with the header "(count/capacity)"; its ctrl 7 is "Converse" (not "Invite") and tab 0x1A is labelled "Mento". The window is opened from HUD window 3 ctrl 2 (the bottom-right "Avatar" button, tooltip "Character Information"), which opens menu 0x1CE (Quick Slot, My Friends, Card Deck, Map, Quest, Skill, Equip, Bag, Status); item 2 "My Friends" toggles window 0x176.

**Trigger.** Send after S2C 0x03 (login/enter world and every map change). The 0x03 handler (0x44E52F -> FUN_0046f860) unconditionally clears the friend list, sets capacity and count to 0 and resets the chat room id. Without a later 0x0B the client shows an empty "(0/0)" list and cannot add friends.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler3 returns 0 (the packet is silently dropped by the rest of the chain) if messenger+0x68 (app) or messenger+0x70 (g_ui_root) is NULL. Both are set in the CMessenger constructor 0x46F670 at startup, so in practice this always passes. messenger+0x74 (the CSNSocket used as `this` for reads) stays NULL until the first S2C 0x03. Sending 0x0B before 0x03 calls GetDataFromPacket with this=NULL; whether that works depends on Fireway and is untested. Nothing checks friend_count against capacity. No de-duplication, but the list is cleared first.

**References.** PySlayer has no S2C 0x0B (server_packets only imports it in a try/except and the file is missing). reference_opcode_atlas.md calls sub3 0x0B "BUY"; that is the C2S meaning (C2S 0x0B = buy item), and the S2C meaning is the friend list. Our server never sends S2C 0x0B. Strings: "(%u/%u)" @0x6F808C and "Can't be add.\r\n\r\nVisit Frenaiga." (FUN_0046fe30).

**Open questions.**
- Status values other than 0, 1 and 4 (e.g. 2 or 3) render as online. Their intended meaning is unknown.
- Which C2S request (if any) made the original server send 0x0B, or whether it was pushed right after 0x03, cannot be determined statically.

On failure it formats the matching message into a 128-byte buffer and opens popup window 0x16 (FUN_00489da0). No packet is sent back. The text is garbage and the strcpy into the 0x3E9-byte dialog buffer could over-read. Only send 1, 2-7, 0x0B or 0x15. On success the list count can go past capacity, and duplicate names are not checked. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C42, social_friend#02): the 24-byte SUCCESS form (result 1 + str[17] name + u8 channel + u32 friend_id + u8 status) is accepted and renders correctly - the grammar here is right; the wsproto encoder was building the 18-byte failure layout for result 1. Failure codes render as MODAL POPUPS; only result 1 / 0x0B produce the green floating notice.

**References.** No PySlayer builder. Our server's 0x0C is the C2S SELL handler, and it never sends S2C 0x0C. The atlas does not name S2C 0x0C. The client-side add flow is FUN_0046fe30 (C2S 0x30, "Requesting <name> to be a friend").

**Open questions.**
- What was the real server-side difference between result 1 and 0x0B? The client handles them the same.
- Is result 7 (no empty slots in YOUR list) sent to the requester while 5 goes about the target? Presumed from the strings.

} else {

}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | 0x65 = error, target is a novice ('<name>is a novice. Only a class-upgraded player can become a mentor.'). 0x66 = error, not found ('<name>can not be found.'). 0x64 = success, mentor online on YOUR channel: the node channel is taken from CMessenger+0x90 and s… | stack esp0+0x13; on success -> node+0x14 (replaced by CMessenger+0x90 if 0x64) |
| `mentor_name` | str[17] | Mentor character name, NUL-padded. Printed via "<%s>%s" into a 0x80 buffer. On success its 17 bytes are copied into the node. | stack esp0+0x20 (not pre-zeroed); success -> node+0x00..+0x10 |
| `mentor_uid` | u32 | Mentor's character uid. Present only on success. Later S2C 0x7D mentor status updates (FUN_00470780) match on node+0x18. | node+0x18 |

**Semantics.** The client first reads result (u8) and mentor_name[17]. For result 0x65 or 0x66 it prints a red (0xFFFD4C87) main-chat line built from "<%s>%s" with the name and the error text, returns 1 and reads nothing else. For any other result it does the following in order. It prints the green (0xFF00C800) line '<name>is registered as your mentor.' and allocates a zeroed 0x28-byte node. It copies the 17 name bytes to node+0x00 and reads the u32 mentor_uid into node+0x18. It sets node+0x14 = result. If result == 0x64 it overwrites node+0x14 with CMessenger+0x90 (own channel) and sets status node+0x20 = 0; otherwise it sets status = 4. It sets node+0x24 = 1, appends the node to the mentor list at CMessenger+0x14 (FUN_00459df0) and refreshes the messenger UI (FUN_00470270). There is no duplicate check.

**Trigger.** Server reply to C2S 0x5C {str[17] mentor_name}, sent by FUN_0046ff70 from the name-entry dialog. The client blocks registering yourself, and FUN_00472900 only lets a novice register ('Only a novice can register a mentor.'). Send 0x65 if the target has not class-upgraded, 0x66 if they don't exist or are offline, and 0x64 or the channel number on success.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Sub3 entry gate: CMessenger+0x68 and +0x70 must be non-zero. No chat-room gate. Reads use CMessenger+0x74 (g_sock_game), which FUN_0046f860 sets from the S2C 0x03 handler, so send this only after S2C 0x03. mentor_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes: the local is not pre-zeroed and is formatted into a 0x80-byte buffer with _sprintf_s, where an overrun triggers the CRT invalid-parameter handler. Success appends a new node every time with no duplicate check, so don't send success twice, or after S2C 0x03 already delivered a mentor. FUN_00470780 only inspects the list head. On a same-channel success, send 0x64 rather than the numeric channel: a numeric value equal to your own channel is still stored with status 4 ('other channel'). This differs from the 0x03 block, which compares against the own channel. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C42, social_friend#17): the 22-byte success form (result 0x64 + str[17] name + u32 mentor_uid) is accepted live - the grammar is right; the wsproto encoder dropped mentor_uid because of a hex-literal comparison bug.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: The two analysts agree on every read and its order. The structural difference is only that B spells out the terminating branch. A gave 'u8 result; str[17] mentor_name; if(result != 0x65 && result != 0x66) { u32 mentor_uid }' and B gave the same with an explicit 'else { stop }'. The asm confirms both paths. At 0x4715CD, call [0x4A4094] reads the u8 into esp0+0x13. At 0x4715DC/0x4715E3, PUSH 0x11 then call [0x4A4098] reads 17 bytes into esp0+0x20. At 0x4715E9..0x4715FA, MOVZX result, SUB 0x65 JZ 0x471742, SUB 1 JZ 0x4716F2. Both error blocks (0x4716F2..0x47173F and 0x471742..0x47178F) contain only _sprintf_s, FUN_004817d0 and RET 0x10, with no GetDataFromPacket. The success fall-through does its single extra read at 0x471690 (call [0x4A40C8], u32 into node+0x18). So B's explicit form, with 'else { stop }', is the canonical grammar and A's is equivalent. One side point: A said the matching mentor sub-block lives in S2C 0x07 at 0x44E5BA and that the client needs 0x07 first. That is wrong. 0x44E5BA is inside the S2C 0x03 handler (asm marker for 0x03 precedes it; FUN_0046f860 is called there at 0x44E52F and sets +0x74/+0x90 and clears +0xCC), as B said. windslayer_server.py _build_pyslayer_opcode_03 emits that mentor gate u32 = 0, which confirms it. Node layout, colours and status values (0x64 -> own channel, status 0; other -> status 4) were verified at 0x4716A1..0x4716C7 and match FUN_00470780 (S2C 0x7D). There is no PySlayer builder for 0x7A, and it is not implemented in windslayer_server.py.

**Open questions.**
- Server-side rule for when 0x65 applies (the class-upgrade check happens on the server) is not visible in the client.
- Whether a channel value of 0 or a value >= 0x67 is ever used in practice. The client accepts any non-0x65/0x66 value as success.
- CMessenger+0x90 is copied from byte [[CMessenger+0x6C]+0x1CF] in FUN_0046f860. Its identity as the local channel number comes from its use as the 'same channel' value (0x7A, FUN_00470780), not from a direct write of the channel.

| `manner_delta` | i32 | signed manner-point change (can be negative) | entity+0x15D8 += delta; if local player also scene+0xEE0 += delta |

**Semantics.** Silent manner-point delta. Looks up the uid in the scene entity list (ignored if absent), adds delta to entity+0x15D8, and if the uid is the local player's session uid also adds it to the local character manner points (scene+0xEE0) and refreshes the manner number (window 0x1B control 1, red when negative). No message or dialog.

**Trigger.** Server-driven manner change without a compliment message: e.g. penalties, report outcomes, or the GM chat command '/manner <name> <amount>' (C2S 0x06 sub 0x0A: str[17] name, i32 amount, FUN_00444A90 @0x444C0C). Also usable to update bystanders' copy of a player's manner points.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler3 in-world gate. Entity must exist in scene list or the packet (including the local update) is ignored. Delta is additive; to set an absolute value the server must track the client's current value. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C52, social_friend#26): manner_delta is confirmed live to be a SIGNED i32 DELTA, not an absolute value (a -5 packet moved the Status window Manner field down by 5 and turned the name tag red once the total went negative).

**References.** No PySlayer implementation. Not in windslayer_server.py. Same offsets as 0x96 minus the name/message.

**Open questions.**
- Exact retail triggers for 0x97 are not proven statically (GM /manner command response is a plausible one).

### C2S 0x42 — ItemMallCloseStorageCommit

*client → server* · key `0x45F0D0/0x42` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 9 + 4*(to_storage_count + to_character_count)

Locations: `0x44B80E` caller chain: UI dispatcher FUN_00446300 calls FUN_0045f2e0(main+0x700, control, notifica…; `0x45F394` FUN_0045f2e0 case control 0x1CF, notification 3 calls FUN_0045ed30(this=main+0x700); `0x45ED7E` loop 1: collects records in the live cash-storage vector (+0x28, begin +0x2C) whose u32 k…; `0x45EE94` loop 2: collects records in the live character cash-item vector (+0x4, begin +0x8) whose …

```
u8 storage_deleted_flag
i32 to_storage_count
i32 to_character_count
repeat(to_storage_count) { u32 item_serial }
repeat(to_character_count) { u32 item_serial }
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `storage_deleted_flag` | u8 | 0 or 1. It is 1 if at least one cash-storage item was deleted (S2C 0x6E success) since the Item Mall was last opened (S2C 0x6A resets it to 0). | main+0x700 +0x5B8 (u32 field; low byte sent via MOVZX byte @0x45F01E) |
| `to_storage_count` | i32 | Number of records now in the account cash storage list that were not there when the mall was opened. These were moved from the character, bought via 0x6C, or received as gifts via 0x79. | size of temp vector A (ESP+0x30 object; (last-first)>>2) |
| `to_character_count` | i32 | Number of records now in the character cash-item list that were not there when the mall was opened (moved out of storage onto the character). | size of temp vector B (ESP+0x20 object) |
| `item_serial (list A)` | u32 | Unique serial of a cash item that is now in storage. This is the first u32 of the 28-byte cash-item record, the same key S2C 0x6E uses to delete. | *(u32*)record, record from main+0x700+0x28 vector, in live-list order |
| `item_serial (list B)` | u32 | Unique serial of a cash item that is now on the character (first u32 of the 28-byte record) | *(u32*)record, record from main+0x700+0x4 vector, in live-list order |

**Semantics.** Sent when the Item Mall (cash shop) main window, control 0x1CF, receives notification 3. This is almost certainly its close/exit button. The client first hides all Item Mall sub-windows (FUN_0045cc20). It then reports the net result of the session's item moves between two lists of 28-byte cash-item records. List 1 is account cash storage (main+0x700+0x28), filled by S2C 0x6A and appended to by S2C 0x6C purchases and 0x79 gifts. List 2 is the character's cash-item inventory (main+0x700+0x4), filled at login by S2C 0x6F entries with flag==0. S2C 0x6A (mall open) snapshots both lists (+0x48 and +0x58). While the window is open the player moves records between the lists: storage->character via control 0x1FC notification 0xCA, which checks per-category slot limits ('You have no more slots for the item.') and duplicates ('The item is already in your inventory. You can't store it any more.'); character->storage via control 0x1FD notification 0xC9. On close the client sends each list's additions compared to its snapshot, keyed by record+0x00 (u32 serial). Removals are never sent explicitly. The server should treat each list-A serial as 'now in storage' (moved off the character, or a no-op for items bought or gifted this session) and each list-B serial as 'now on character' (moved out of storage). Record layout as the client uses it: +0x00 u32 serial, +0x04 u16 item id, +0x06 u8 kind (0/1/2), +0x08 u16, +0x0A u16, +0x1A u8 (3 = event item). Only the serial goes on the wire.

**Trigger.** The player closes the Item Mall window (control 0x1CF, notification 3). The windows hide even if the socket is null.

**Expected response.** None awaited: no waiting dialog and no state change that depends on a reply. The temporary vectors are freed right after Send.

**Gates / hazards.** Built only if [main+0x700+0x20] != NULL. FUN_0045ae40 sets it during the S2C 0x5A key/login-start handler. SubHandler4 also ignores mall packets unless +0x14 and +0x18 are set there. The opcode Add is inside the null-check, so nothing is appended to the buffer when the socket is null. The snapshots +0x48/+0x58 are rebuilt ONLY by S2C 0x6A, and neither the snapshots nor the live lists are updated after this send. If the window is reopened without a fresh 0x6A and closed again, the same serials are re-sent, so the server must make applying them idempotent. Items bought (0x6C) or gifted (0x79) during the session appear in list A even though they never left storage. A deletion (0x6E) removes a record only from the live storage list, so it produces no serial; only the flag reports it. Counts are i32 while the elements are u32; element pointers are never NULL, so the counts always equal the number of u32 entries that follow.

**References.** PySlayer has no C2S 0x42 parser. PySlayer's server_packets/opcode_0x42.py is an unrelated S2C builder for the KR build (u32,u32,u16), and S2C 0x42 is not C2S 0x42. Not handled by our windslayer_server.py _dispatch (no 0x42 branch). The Item Mall meaning comes from strings used in FUN_0045f2e0/SubHandler4: 'Item is added to your wish-list.', 'You have no more slots for the item.', 'You failed to delete the item.', 'You are short of cash.', 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash...'.

**Open questions.**
- Notification 3 on control 0x1CF is inferred to be the close/exit button, because it hides all mall windows; there is no UI layout file to confirm it
- What the server is supposed to do with storage_deleted_flag (possibly a resync hint); it is only set by S2C 0x6E and cleared by 0x6A
- Which C2S request opens the mall and makes the server send S2C 0x6A (not in this batch). The correctness of the diff depends on 0x6A being sent on every open.
- Which window shows which list (0x1FC vs 0x1FD) does not affect the wire format. List A = account storage (+0x28, from 0x6A) and list B = character cash items (+0x4, from 0x6F flag 0) are inferred from the slot-limit and 'already in your inventory' checks on the storage->character move.

Until a 0x70 arrives, every control-0xA8 event sends another 0x46. If the player never presses charge-cash, control 0xA8 does nothing. There are no dialogs and no 'waiting' UI. Pressing charge-cash minimizes the game window and opens a dead Yahoo KR URL in the browser.

**References.** Not in PySlayer (no parse_0x46 and no S2C 0x70 builder). Not handled by windslayer_server.py _dispatch (it falls through to 'Unhandled opcode'). There are no memory notes on the cash shop. S2C 0x70 layout was taken from the handler asm at 0x4624DE-0x462541.

**Open questions.**
- Which on-screen button in window 0x1CF has control id 0xA8 (probably a 'Refresh'/'Check cash' button)? The id comes from UI resource data (probably the encrypted .hsi files), not from code. No code path pushes (0x1CF, 0xA8) literally.

After sending, the dialog closes and a 'Waiting for the server to response.' box shows, so the server must answer with 0x71. Hazards: message_len is strlen truncated to u8 (256+ chars would wrap). The message is strcpy'd into a 100-byte stack buffer and the name into a 17-byte buffer, so the edit controls' max lengths are all that prevent overflow.

**References.** Not in PySlayer or our server. Related finding: S2C 0x80 is really the password-check result (u8 ok==1, then u32 dialog_id; 0x1F9 opens the gift dialog, anything else goes to FUN_00483430(id); ok!=1 -> 'Invalid password.'). **Open questions.**
- The second byte (constant 0) is assumed to line up with the 0x43 pay_with_mileage flag; the client alone can't confirm the server-side meaning.
- Max lengths of edit controls 9 and 0xB were not traced, so the real message_len range is unknown (probably under 91 given the zeroed buffer).

**Semantics.** Asks the server to broadcast a megaphone message using a megaphone cash item from the inventory. The item id tells the server whether it is a Super Megaphone (whole world) or a normal Megaphone (whole channel). After sending, the client closes the megaphone window straight away and shows no waiting dialog, so it does not need a direct reply. The server should check that the player owns the item, use up one charge, broadcast the message, and update the item count.

If the control allows 61 or more characters the text is not NUL-terminated inside the 61 bytes sent (and the stack overflows). No ResetBuffer is called; the buffer is assumed empty after the previous Send. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all.

**References.** No match in PySlayer (no parse_0x4C). Not handled in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. Item names come from data/en/items_en.json and the PySlayer gamedef items table (Type 5 cash items).

Region codes by region slot 0..9 (table 0x70B9AE): 1 The Beginning of the Adventure, 2 Popola Village, 4 Ozzi Village, 7 Balderan, 5 Amakusa, 8 Mining Settlement, 6 Atajokuna, 9 Serien the City of … | (window 0x471 +0x40) % 10000. **Semantics.** Asks the server to teleport the player to the chosen map, using one charge of a Region Warp Stone. The client packs the region-window slot (v/10000) and the map id (v%10000) into one int, but only the map id goes on the wire. After OK the client clears the item id on that region window and closes it. It shows no waiting dialog.

**Trigger.** The player uses a Region Warp Stone, opens a region on the world map, clicks a destination (only allowed while the region window's +0x134 item id is not 0), then clicks OK (control 6) in confirmation window 0x471.

**Expected response.** Most likely S2C 0x9A: u8 result; if ==1: u32 inventory_entry_id (item count -1); otherwise 'You are unable to transfer\r\nto the area.' The map change itself probably follows through the normal map-change packets (not verified).

**Gates / hazards.** No packet is sent if the u16 item_id is 0 or dest_map_id <= 0; the region window is still reset and closed when v/10000 >= 1. Region windows opened without a warp stone have +0x134 == 0, so confirmation window 0x471 never opens (0x44B6BB). The encoding assumes map suffix < 100; a control value >= 100 would change v/10000 and the map id. The server must validate that dest_map_id is a real, allowed destination.

**References.** Not in PySlayer or in windslayer_server.py. The scout guess (0x70 + u16 + i32) matches. Region names come from pointer table 0x70B8B8. The region code tables at 0x70B9AE and 0x70D04C are identical, and DAT_00709298[i+1] == DAT_0070BA1C[i] (same window ids).

**Open questions.**
- Confirm that S2C 0x9A is the reply to C2S 0x70 (inferred from its error string).
- Which packets perform the warp after success (probably the usual 0x08 + map replay)?
- It is not verified that every region-window destination control's +0x28 is below 100 (FUN_0042c450 strongly suggests map_id%100).

**Semantics.** Enter the cash shop. (1) game_state+0x1534 = 0 (clears the wait/fade flag FUN_0043d560 sets). (2) Free box list mall+0x28; read cash -> +0x588, mileage -> +0x58C, box_count, then box_count 28-byte records into +0x28. (3) Rebuild snapshot lists: +0x48 = deep copy of +0x28, +0x58 = deep copy of owned list +0x04 (filled by 0x6F). (4) mall+0x5B8 = 0; FUN_0045af00 initializes the shop UI. (5) FUN_0045c470 swaps the world scene for ./hs/preview99_01.hmi ('Could not load Preview MAP.' on failure), creates a 0x15F0 preview avatar from the local character's appearance (alive byte=3, HP=100, uid=char+0x1D8, fixed position constants), calls RegisterLocalPlayer and sets [game_state+0x4CC](scene)+0xF00 = 4 (opening window 0x15 first if it was 5). (6) Opens windows 0x1CF, 0x1FB, 0x1FC, 0x1FD, and 0x3F3 only the first time (mall+0x5B4). (7) If byte mall+0x00 != 0 shows 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash. 500 mileage has reserved...' and clears it. (8) FUN_0045e260. Returns 1.

**Trigger.** Reply to the client's request to enter the cash shop (the 'Enter the cash shop?' dialog 0x133 for type 0x81 in FUN_0044c4b0, confirmed in FUN_00446300 at 0x446CF8, which re-dispatches as id 3 / control 1). The C2S request opcode was not traced.

**Expected response.** none directly; the client then uses the shop C2S commands in FUN_0045f2e0 (0x43, 0x45, 0x48, 0x49, 0x4B, 0x51, 0x70, 0x71, ...)

**Gates / hazards.** Only the SubHandler4 entry gate ([mall+0x14], [mall+0x18] non-NULL). No other pre-read gate. HAZARD: unconditionally unloads the current world map, loads the preview map and registers a preview avatar as local player; sending it outside the shop flow pulls the client out of the world. The server must restore the world with the normal map-change sequence on exit. Send 0x6F first, because list +0x04 is snapshotted here. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, premium_cash#13/#30): live - the mall renders fully, but NO exit control works from inside it (three attempts produced 0 packets), so the client cannot leave on its own and C2S 0x42 could not even be produced. RECOVERY: the server must push the world back with the map-enter sequence (S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07); otherwise the client must be restarted.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: A and B agree exactly on the read sequence: u32 at 0x461C25 into +0x588, u32 at 0x461C3B into +0x58C, i32 at 0x461C4F, then a loop of single 28-byte reads (PUSH 0x1c at 0x461C8F, call at 0x461C96). The only difference is the record tail: A has u8 origin + u8 unk_1b, B has u16 unk_1a. The wire bytes are identical, but the client reads +0x1A as a single byte (CMP byte ptr [ECX+0x1a],DL at 0x45FB4F on box records found by FUN_0045e6f0 in list +0x28; CMP byte ptr [EDX+0x1a],3 at 0x462322). No reader of +0x1B exists, so A's layout is the precise one. On a minor semantic detail B was right and A was not: the +0xF00 = 4 write in FUN_0045c470 (0x45C6CB/0x45C6E2) goes to [game_state+0x4CC], which is the scene, not the character. Winner for the grammar: A. PySlayer has no opcode_0x6A.py. Our server does not implement 0x6A, but the comment on its disabled 0x6F sender (windslayer_server.py ~L789) actually describes this block. Strings: 0x6F5840 'Enter the cash shop?', 0x6F7F70 './hs/preview99_01.hmi', 0x6F4610 first-purchase message.

**Open questions.**
- Which C2S opcode requests shop entry and which one requests exit (a 0-byte C2S 0x46 sent from the shop UI at 0x463D7C, guarded by mall+0x5AC, is an unverified candidate).
- Where byte mall+0x00 (first-purchase flag) is set.

```

**Semantics.** No payload is read (the 'stop' is at the start: the handler has no read calls, so any trailing bytes are ignored). (1) FUN_00463a10 writes the cash shop wish list (vector mall+0x20C, first u32 of each entry, up to 12) to the registry under the character name at [game_state+0x4CC]+0x206 as Wish0..Wish11 (zeroing them first). (2) FUN_00489320(3,6,3) on the UI root sets window 3 / control 6 to state 3. FUN_00483470 makes the same call when restoring the HUD, so this probably re-enables the HUD cash shop button. (3) FUN_00465290 rebuilds the inventory UI. Returns 1. It does not unload the preview map or restore the world scene.

**Expected response.** none

Harmless outside the shop apart from the registry write and the HUD control state. The world map must be restored separately with the normal map-change packets. LIVE: writes the Wish0 registry value (e.g. 4235) and leaves the client on the black preview screen - it does not return to the world by itself; follow with a full map load.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree that the block reads nothing. A wrote 'stop' and B an empty grammar, which mean the same thing. The asm block 0x462027-0x462062 is PUSH EBX / CALL 0x463A10 / PUSH 3,6,3 / CALL 0x489320 / CALL 0x465290 / MOV EAX,1 / return, with no IAT GetDataFromPacket call. 'stop' is kept as the canonical DSL form. On semantics A is more precise: FUN_00489320 walks the UI root window list for id 3, steps to control 6 and stores param_4=3 in the control's +0x18 state, not a 'simulated activation'. FUN_00465290 is the inventory window builder (bag +0x380 etc.), not a generic HUD refresh. Winner: tie on grammar, A on details. PySlayer has no opcode_0x6B.py. Our server: not implemented.

**Open questions.**

- Which C2S exit request precedes 0x6B.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | 1 = purchase OK. 0x0E = popup "You are short of cash.". Any other value = popup "You failed to buy the item.\r\n\r\nPlease try again in a few minutes.". Nothing more is read on failure. | stack local [esp+0x13] |
| `cash_balance` | u32 | New absolute cash balance | cash-shop manager (game_state+0x700) +0x588; shown in UI label 0x67 |
| `mileage_balance` | u32 | New absolute mileage balance. If it is higher than the old value (unsigned compare), the client shows "50% bonus mileage has been deposited." | local, then mgr+0x58C; shown in UI label 0x68 |
| `item_serial` | u32 | Unique id of the bought cash item (record +0x00). Later 0x6E, 0x72 and 0x73 and C2S 0x45 find the record by this value. The next nine fields all come from ONE 28-byte buffer read at 0x462318. | record+0x00 |
| `item_id` | u16 | Item template id (record +0x04). Ids 0x75C..0x761 (1884-1889, equipment/consumable/etc/storage slot expansions) are applied right away (+5 slots, up to 45 for inventory or 60 for bank) and are not stored. | record+0x04 |
| `item_kind` | u8 | Record kind: 1 = counted item (quantity goes down on use, record removed at 0); 2 = duration/period item (expire_time is valid). Matches item def +0x1F6. The client only reads the low byte. | record+0x06 |
| `unk_07` | u8 | Unused by the client (probably the high byte of a u16 kind, or padding). Send 0. | record+0x07 |
| `quantity` | u16 | Count of the item (shown in the box window; decremented by use) | record+0x08 |
| `expire_time` | bytes[16] | Win32 SYSTEMTIME expiry for duration items: u16 wYear, wMonth, wDayOfWeek, wDay, wHour, wMinute, wSecond, wMilliseconds. A year below 1900 means no expiry (FUN_0045a9f0). Send zeros for counted items. | record+0x0A..0x19 |
| `origin` | u8 | Source flag. 3 = event reward, which shows "Congratulation.\r\n\r\nYou received an event item.." | record+0x1A |
| `unk_1b` | u8 | Unused by this handler; send 0 | record+0x1B |

**Semantics.** Result of a cash-shop purchase. On success the client sets cash and mileage to the absolute values sent and redraws their labels. It shows the bonus-mileage popup if mileage went up. It reads one 28-byte cash item record. If record.item_id is a slot-expansion ticket (0x75C..0x761), the client applies it (+5 slots, with a popup) and frees the record. Otherwise it adds the record to the cash item box list (mgr+0x28), with no check for duplicate serials. Both paths then rebuild box window 0x1FC (FUN_0045b280) and inventory-side window 0x1FD (FUN_0045b360), and redraw the labels. On failure the client only shows a popup. LIVE: the generic failure message has a second line 'Please try again in a few minutes.'; slot-extension success grows the bag from 35 to 40 slots.

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x43 'C' (buy): u8 opcode, bool pay_with_mileage, u8 count, then count x u16 item_id; sent from cash shop windows 0x1F7/0x1F8/0x1FF. The server probably sends one 0x6C per bought item, since each packet carries only one record.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler4 returns 0 without reading if mgr+0x14 or mgr+0x18 is NULL (cash-shop manager not initialized). A repeated serial makes duplicate box entries. Result 0x0E and other non-1 values read nothing after the result byte.

**References.** Not in PySlayer (doc/server_to_client/README.md only lists 0x6C among Packet_handler_4 opcodes). Not in windslayer_server.py. Our server's 0x80 'CashShopBalance' does not write mgr+0x588/+0x58C: in the corpus only FUN_0045ae40 (reset) and sub4 opcodes 0x6C/0x6E/0x70/0x71 write those fields. Record layout agrees with the 0x6F list parser (FUN_0045e8e0(item_id@+4, qty@+8, serial@+0); kind==2 && year!=0 -> expiry popup FUN_0045ebb0) and with FUN_00464380.

**Open questions.**
- Does the server send one 0x6C per item for multi-item (cart) purchases, or use another opcode such as 0x6D (u8 count + 0x7E-byte entries) for carts?
- Exact meaning of record bytes +0x07 and +0x1B; is item_kind really a u16 whose high byte is unused?
- Is the mileage sent here the balance after a 50% bonus? The client only compares it with the old value.

| `origin` | u8 | Record +0x1A, read as a BYTE by the client: 0 = bought with cash (shop UI 0x45FB4F computes a refund/price value only when this byte is 0); 3 = event reward (0x6C handler 0x462322 shows 'Congratulation... You received an event item'). Other values: no refund … | node +0x1A |
| `unk_1b` | u8 | Record +0x1B: no reader found (padding). Send 0. | node +0x1B |

**Semantics.** Full rebuild of the character's owned (out-of-box) cash items. Order: (1) free every node of lists mall+0x04 and mall+0x38 (mall = game_state+0x700). (2) For bags char+0x380 (slots byte +0x361), +0x5F6 (slots +0x362), +0x760 (slots +0x363) call purge helpers that first check the slot byte <= 45 (else the handler returns 1 immediately, nothing read) and then remove and compact every item whose template +0x1F0 != 0 (cash item). (3) Purge the fixed 45-slot bag +0x7E8 the same way. (4) Read i32 count; per record: alloc 28 zeroed bytes, read bool is_equipped, read the 28-byte record raw. is_equipped != 0 -> push to +0x38 only. Else push to +0x04, then if limit_type==2 and expire_year!=0 -> FUN_0045ebb0 chat expiry notice (no bag insert), otherwise FUN_0045e8e0(mall, item_id, quantity, serial) inserts into a bag by template category (0, 1, 5; others ignored; silent failure when full or quantity 0). (5) FUN_00465290 rebuilds the inventory UI; FUN_00441c20(1) rebuilds the window-5 period-item list. Returns 1.

**Trigger.** Server sends the complete owned cash item set whenever it must be synced (likely after world entry once the base inventory exists, and before 0x6A, which snapshots list +0x04 into +0x58). The requesting C2S opcode was not identified.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler4 returns 0 (unhandled) if [mall+0x14] or [mall+0x18] is NULL. The two lists are freed before the gate, so a failed gate still wipes them. Every 0x6F deletes all cash items (template+0x1F0 != 0) from the bags, including ones delivered by 0x07, so it must always carry the full set; count=0 means 'no cash items'. Worn items (is_equipped=1) are only tracked, not inserted. quantity=0 silently skips bag insertion. No bound on count; each record is heap-allocated. Always send exactly 4 + 29*count bytes. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C13, premium_cash#21): the stat-reset ALLOWANCE the client enforces is this record's u16 quantity at +0x08 - NOT the item definition's Cash_V. A "Reset 5 Stat Points" record must therefore be sent with quantity = 5 or the player can restore only one point. The same field also drives the stack count drawn on the Premiums icon, so for these items quantity is both stack size and allowance.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the read order (i32 count at 0x461AD5, then per record bool at 0x461B28 and a single 28-byte blob at 0x461B3E) and on total size. They differ on two points. (1) Gate: A wraps the body in a client-state if/else-stop; B only mentions the gate in hazards. The asm proves the gate is a real branch in the read path: the helpers at 0x4243D0/0x4245D0/0x4244E0 begin with CMP AL,0x2d / JBE (AL = byte [char+0x361/0x362/0x363]) and otherwise XOR EAX,EAX / RET 0xc; the handler tests the result (JZ 0x46302A at 0x46196B/0x461999/0x4619C7) and 0x46302A is MOV EAX,1 / return, before the first GetDataFromPacket. A is correct. (2) Record tail: A uses u8 origin + u8 unk_1b; B uses u16 unk_1a. The wire bytes are identical, because the record is read as one 28-byte blob (PUSH 0x1c at 0x461B3B). But the client reads +0x1A as a single byte (CMP byte ptr [ECX+0x1a],DL with DL=0 at 0x45FB4F in FUN_0045f2e0; CMP byte ptr [EDX+0x1a],3 at 0x462322 in the 0x6C handler), and nothing reads +0x1B, so A's split is the precise layout. On semantics, A's 'is_equipped' reading of the bool is confirmed by FUN_0045d0c0/FUN_0045d170 being called from the 0x1D and 0x1E/0x24 handlers to move records between lists +0x04 and +0x38; B's claim that +0x38 has no other reader is wrong. B's point that quantity=0 blocks bag insertion is correct and is included. Overall winner: A. Other refs: PySlayer has no opcode_0x6F.py. Our server (windslayer_server.py ~L789-823) has a disabled 0x6F sender that sends 28 zero bytes, which would parse as count=0 (wipe all cash items) plus 24 ignored bytes. Its comment about rep movsd, [+0x5B8]=0, FUN_0045AF00 and FUN_0045C470 describes the 0x6A block (0x461D37-0x461F2F), not 0x6F.

**Open questions.**
- Which C2S request (if any) the original server answered with 0x6F, and exact timing relative to 0x07/0x6A.
- Meaning of origin values other than 0 and 3; unk_07 and unk_1b have no reader in the cash-shop code (assumed padding).
- UI label of the fixed 45-slot category-5 bag at char+0x7E8.

For any visible character the client updates appearance: for the three random hair/dye items it applies the server-chosen hair_code to hair slot 4; for other items FUN_00427430 applies the change set in the item def (switch on def+0x1F4: 0 generic slot, 1 hair style, 2 hair color, 0x0E special), and items with no appearance effect do nothing here. FUN_00464380 finds the record by serial in list mgr+4. A kind-1 record loses one from quantity and is removed at 0. A kind-2 record gets the expiry copied in. Either way FUN_0045e8e0 updates the character inventory and windows 0x1FD etc. are rebuilt. Item 3323 also settles the record-length question: the client def +0x1F6 == 2 == gamedef Cash_T, so the 26-byte (duration) form is the correct length for it.

FUN_00463d90 opens that window when the player uses a generic cash item from the inventory, and it shows the 'Waiting for the server to response.' box that this packet closes. Send it to the user and to nearby players (the same full body works for all; other clients stop reading early and ignore extra bytes). MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x48 (use cash item). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Same SubHandler4 gate. If the uid is not in the scene, only 4 bytes are read (nothing is applied). For other players reading stops after item_id/hair_code. For the local player, if item_id has no item def, reading stops after the serial. The expiry is read only when def+0x1F6 == 2, so the server must use the same item-def table as the client; a mismatch makes the server send or omit 16 bytes the client does not expect (trailing bytes are harmless, missing bytes are read out of bounds). An unknown serial is ignored, but the inventory UI is still refreshed.

**References.** Not in PySlayer or windslayer_server.py. Item names from server/data/en/items_en.json: 3385 'Random Hair (F)', 3386 'Random Hair (M)', 3408 'Random Dye'. FUN_004270f0 (client-side random hair) is unreachable from 0x72 because these ids take the server-value path.

- Does the server send 0x72 to other players in range, or only to the user? The client handles both.
- Meaning of item def +0x1F4 use-type values 0/1/2/0x0E beyond appearance changes (for example, whether non-appearance items rely only on the effect and sound).

**Semantics.** Result/broadcast of a stat redistribution (stat-reset cash item). Looks up the entity by uid; if absent, stops. Overwrites the four base stats +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC (bonus fields untouched). If level +0x99 != 0, FUN_00427f40(0) recomputes max MP +0x1110 and clamps cur MP +0xA0. Scans party windows 0x75..0x78 for the first one whose +0x134 == uid and, if max MP != 0, updates its '%u/%u' MP text (element 2) and gauge. FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recomputes max HP +0x110C and clamps cur HP +0x9C; if max HP != 0, FUN_0043d3f0 updates the party HP display. FUN_0041ace0 recomputes derived combat stats (in a special mode scene+0xF6C != 0 it overwrites all four stats with 55 and level with 49). Queues effect {0xA, 0x140, uid} on client+0x430 and plays sound 0x140 at the entity. If the entity is the local player: closes modal window 0x16, reads cash_item_serial and consume_count, consumes that premium item (FUN_00464380 also refreshes inventory/quickslot UI) and refreshes the stat window (FUN_00442510). Returns 1 on every path.

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x4A sent from the stat redistribution window: u8 0x4A, u16 (low 16 bits of window+0x134), then 4x u8 = (low byte of current stat +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC) minus the window's per-stat value; the client then shows 'Waiting for the server to response.'. Send the 18-byte form to the requester; the 12-byte form (uid + 4 stats) can be broadcast to other clients that have the entity spawned. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x4A (stat reset). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler4 does not parse unless ctx+0x14 and ctx+0x18 are non-null. uid 0 or unknown uid: only 4 bytes read, no effect. For the local player, if the trailing 6 bytes are missing GetDataFromPacket leaves stale stack values (serial = entity pointer, count = low word of client pointer); FUN_00464380 then most likely matches nothing but still refreshes the UI; always send the 18-byte form to the owner. FUN_00464380 does not stop at the first type-1 match that leaves qty > 0 (keeps scanning) and calls FUN_0045e8e0 with -count even when qty < count. Stats are absolute; values inconsistent with level make the client-side remaining-points count negative. Max HP/MP recompute requires level 1..99 and class +0x110 <= 6. Effect/sound 0x140 plays for every recipient. No dialog shown. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C15, premium_cash#09): the client draws free points as total(level) - sum(stats) with NO clamp, so a 0x76 whose stats sum above the level total paints a NEGATIVE "Stat Point" value (observed -7). The server must keep sum(stats) <= total(level) when answering C2S 0x4A.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire format (u32 uid; stop if entity not found; 4x u16 into +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC; if local player, u32 serial + u16 count). The structural-signature difference is only notation (A nested the rest inside if/else-stop, B used an early stop); the bytes are identical. The asm confirms it: u32 via [0x4A40C8] at 0x462856 -> [esp+0x20]; FUN_004189f0 at 0x46286A and JZ 0x46302A (return 1) at 0x462875; four CALL ESI with ESI=[0x4A4090] at 0x462899/0x4628B2/0x4628CB/0x4628E4 into EDI+0xE6/E8/EA/EC; local gate CMP ECX,[EAX+0x1D8] / JNZ 0x46302A at 0x462A5E; u32 [0x4A40C8] at 0x462A8D -> [esp+0x24] and u16 [0x4A4090] at 0x462AA1 -> [esp+0x14], both passed to FUN_00464380 at 0x462AB4. On the side details, A was right that FUN_00427d40 recomputes max HP (it writes +0x110C and clamps +0x9C), where B only said 'derived stats'. A was also right that the trigger is C2S 0x4A (Add u8 0x4A at 0x460BCA, send at 0x460C50). B's guess of C2S 0x72 is wrong: 0x72 is the stone extraction request at 0x46C066. B was right, and A missed, that FUN_0041ace0 forces the stats to 0x37 and the level to 0x31 when scene+0xF6C != 0 (decomp lines 590-600). Other checks: not in PySlayer (no opcode_0x76) and not in our server. The stat offsets match the u16 stats our 0x07 spawn builder writes. C2S/S2C pairing offset of 0x2C (0x4A->0x76, 0x72->0x9C).

**Open questions.**
- Stat names for +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEC are inferred from stat-name table order; only +0xEA (INT -> MP formula) is behaviorally confirmed.
- Which S2C packet fills the premium-inventory vector at ctx+0x04 (A said 0x6A/0x79, B said 0x6F) was not re-verified.
- Whether C2S 0x4A's u16 (window+0x134) is an item code or a truncated cash-item serial is unresolved; the server reply's u32 serial must match the record key regardless.
- Whether the original server broadcast the 12-byte form to others cannot be proven statically (the non-local path exists).

} else {

}

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | 1 = message delivered; any other value = failure | stack local [esp+0x13] |
| `cash_item_serial` | u32 | key (+0x00) of the premium-inventory record to consume (count fixed at 1 by the client) | stack local [esp+0x14] -> FUN_00464380(ctx, serial, 1, 0) |

**Semantics.** Result of using a 'send message to a player' cash item. Always first dismisses message box window 0x16 (the waiting modal). If result == 1: clears window 0x3FD text element 7 (recipient name) and element 9 (message body), closes window 0x3FD, reads cash_item_serial and consumes one of that premium item (inventory/quickslot refresh), then shows modal 'You successfully sent the message.'. The server must always echo the real serial of the consumed record.

Window 0x3FD is opened by using cash items 0x766 or 0xCF8. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x4B (send note / message item). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler4 exits without parsing if ctx+0x14 or ctx+0x18 is null. result must be exactly 1 for success. On success with a missing u32 the serial is stale stack data (harmless, no match expected). Serial not found in the premium list -> nothing consumed, UI still refreshed. Live (C14): serial 0 (or any unmatched serial) leaves the item in the player's premium list while the success popup claims the message was sent - a silent client/server divergence.

**Open questions.**

- Exact in-game name of cash items 0x766/0xCF8 not resolved.
- Confirm from the binary that cash_item_serial == 0 is a deliberate "no item" sentinel rather than a lookup that simply never matches (live: the modal shows, nothing is consumed).

```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_serial` | u32 | unique serial of the time-limited cash item that expired (the record's +0x00 u32, as delivered by S2C 0x6F) | stack local [esp+0x28]; compared with u32 at +0x00 of each 28-byte record in the vector at ctx+0x04 (ctx = game_state+0… |

**Semantics.** Removes an expired premium (cash) item. The client walks the pointer vector at ctx+0x04 (begin ctx+0x08, end ctx+0x0C) from index 0. For each element whose u32 at +0x00 equals item_serial it: erases the element from the vector; looks up the item definition by the u16 item_id at element+0x04 (item table [ctx+0x1C], index id-1); if found, prints "[<item name>] is expired." to the chat log in color 0xFFFDF34C; frees the 28-byte record; and calls FUN_00441c20(1) on game_state to rebuild the inventory display. **Expected response.** none

After erasing index i the loop increments i, so the element shifted into slot i is skipped; this only matters for duplicate serials (use unique serials). The chat line needs the chat window ([UI+0x59C] != 0); an unknown item_id still removes and frees the record, just with no message. Only records that 0x6F put into the ctx+0x04 list (its per-record bool == 0) can be expired. Records in the ctx+0x38 list (bool != 0) are not searched.

**References.** Not in PySlayer (listed only as a Packet_handler_4 opcode) and not in windslayer_server.py. Record layout cross-checked against the S2C 0x6F handler (0x4618EC): i32 count, then per record bool + 28 raw bytes; bool==0 -> vector ctx+0x04, where +0x00 u32 is passed as the key and +0x04 u16 is the item id (FUN_0045e8e0 args at 0x461B7E). Items such as 3321..3326 'EXP 50%/100% 60/30/7 Days' are the kind of time-limited items this applies to.

**Open questions.**
- Exact meaning of the remaining fields of the 28-byte cash-item record (+0x06 u8, +0x08 u16, +0x0A u16) belongs to the S2C 0x6F spec; not needed for 0x93's wire format.

## udp_p2p

### C2S 0x03 — InputState_ToRoomHost

*client → server* · key `UDP-C2S:0x4236F5/0x03` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 6 (15-byte datagram on the wire)

Locations: `0x423287` mode != 0 and host flag == 0: jump to 0x42362D, skipping the snapshot build; `0x423637` mode != 0: continue at 0x42363D; host==0 -> 0x42364A; `0x423652` return (skipping the input reset) if local player scene+0x970 is NULL; `0x423658` send if local entity +0x98 == 3, or scene+0xF08 == 0, or (scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C) > 90…

```
u32 uid
u8 input_a
u8 input_b
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | Local player uid (account_id). | scene+0x220 |
| `input_a` | u8 | (action*10 + dir) & 0xFF. - dir = scene+0x254: 8 = none, 2/6 = horizontal direction. - action = scene+0x255: 0 none, 1-5 attack/skill keys, 6 dash, 7 skill cast (sticky). See UDP-C2S:0x4237FD/0x03 for the full key mapping. | scene+0x255 (tens), scene+0x254 (ones) |
| `input_b` | u8 | (skill_variant*10 + status_code) & 0xFF, where skill_variant = scene+0x256 (1..11) and status_code = scene+0x257 (0..5, recomputed each tick). | scene+0x256 (tens), scene+0x257 (ones) |

**Semantics.** Input/keep-alive datagram from a non-host room participant to the room's UDP host. This is the only UDP traffic a non-host client produces in room maps; no snapshot is built. Destination: IP string scene+0xF38 (host_ip from S2C 0x2F; SendTo uses inet_addr with gethostbyname fallback). The port is (u16 scene+0xF48 room_no + 10000) & 0xFFFF, passed through htons. scene+0xF48 is also written by the room-join UI at 0x44931C..0x44B031. Conditions: - scene+0xF90 != NULL. - scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6. - mode [scene+0xF88]+0x70 != 0 (arena/team-battle maps; the map XML mode attribute). - scene+0xF24 == 0 (always true in EN). - scene+0x970 != NULL. - At least one of: - (a) local entity +0x98 == 3 (player-type entity, as created by room/player spawn packets). The datagram is then sent EVERY tick (at most every 30 ms). - (b) scene+0xF08 == 0: no room snapshot 0x07/0x08/0x09 accepted since S2C 0x2F reset it, so it is sent every tick until the host answers. - (c) scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C > 9000 ms: keep-alive. F20 is the previous tick's time; F0C is stamped on each send and by S2C 0x2F. Input bytes are cleared at the end of every tick even when nothing is sent (dir=8; action/variant=0 unless action==7). On the host side FUN_00423850 uses the datagram's source ip:port to register the peer (entity+0x6A/+0x80, +0x14EA=1) and stores the input digits in entity+0x8B3..0x8B6. Framing: 8-byte Fireway header (len\|0x800\|seq<<12; shared per-socket seq at CSNSocket+0x13A8, wrapping 255->0) plus the EncodebyArray checksum/XOR (cencmsg.encode_by_array). reset=1.

**Trigger.** FrameMove tick in a room map (mode != 0) after S2C 0x2F provided host_ip/room_no, subject to the state/F08/9 s conditions above.

**Expected response.** The room host must send UDP snapshots to the client's g_sock_map, i.e. the source address of this datagram, normally port 42907. Accepted opcodes are 0x07/0x08/0x09 (mode 1 only; header+records, the same layout as 0x04). They must carry map_code == the client's map+0x1B8. Each accepted snapshot increments scene+0xF08, which drops the 0x03 rate to the 9 s keep-alive unless the local entity is +0x98==3. HP/MP datagrams 0x06/0x0B/0x0A/0x10 are also accepted.

**Gates / hazards.** - No EN 2008 client can be the host (scene+0xF24 is never set), and every client binds 42907, not room_no+10000. A private server supporting arenas must therefore itself listen on UDP host_ip:(room_no+10000) and act as the host. - host_ip must be NUL-terminated within 16 bytes. An unresolvable name makes inet_addr and gethostbyname fail; sendto then targets 255.255.255.255 without SO_BROADCAST, and the send fails silently. - room_no + 10000 is truncated to 16 bits. - If the local entity is +0x98==3, the flood is continuous (~33/s) regardless of host replies.

**References.** PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x2F: host_ip (scene+0xF38) and room_no (scene+0xF48) are described as 'Non-host peers later send UDP to this IP on port room_no+10000 (FUN_00423260 @0x4236E8)'. PROTOCOL.md C2S 0x0D: 'Not sent in P2P room mode ([map]+0x70 == 1)'. The receiver's host-registration logic is FUN_00423850 at 0x423850-0x423A04.

**Open questions.**
- Whether the original service ran a UDP room host/relay on host_ip:(room_no+10000), and which address it replied to. The client accepts snapshots from any source address.
- Whether the original host sent 0x07/0x08/0x09 to the recvfrom source port or to the TCP-reported p2p_udp_port (42907). These differ only behind NAT.

u8 input_a
u8 input_b
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | Local player uid (account_id from S2C 0x02). The receiver looks up the entity with +0x84 == uid and +0x98 in {1,3}. | scene+0x220 |
| `input_a` | u8 | (action*10 + dir) & 0xFF, computed with 8-bit IMUL. - dir = scene+0x254. 8 = no horizontal input (reset every tick). FUN_0042ac00 sets 2 when only key app+0xDE0 is held and 6 when only key app+0xDE4 is held; dash also uses 2/6. - action = scene+0x255: - 0 = n… | scene+0x255 (tens), scene+0x254 (ones) |
| `input_b` | u8 | (skill_variant*10 + status_code) & 0xFF. - skill_variant = scene+0x256 (1..11 for action 7; cleared with 0x255). - status_code = scene+0x257 (0..5): a local-player effect class recomputed each tick by FUN_0042cf20, e.g. 1 for effect ids 0x192-0x19C, 2 for 0x8… | scene+0x256 (tens), scene+0x257 (ones) |

**Semantics.** The local player's input state, sent to the client's own socket every tick in normal maps, right after the 0x04 loopback snapshot (seq = snapshot seq + 1). Destination: 127.0.0.1 : scene+0x244 (= 42907). Conditions: - scene+0xF90 != NULL and scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6. - mode [scene+0xF88]+0x70 == 0. - scene+0xF24 == 0 (always true in EN). - The local player pointer scene+0x970 is NOT checked on this path, so it is also sent at character select. After the send, dir resets to 8. Action and variant reset to 0 unless action == 7, which stays until a received snapshot shows the local entity with action code 0x17..0x21 (FUN_00458640 0x458CAx clears scene+0x255/0x256). Receiver: FUN_00458640 case 3 -> FUN_00423850(uid, a, b, src_ip, src_port). It finds the entity with uid match and +0x98 in {1,3}, stores the decoded digits in +0x8B3..+0x8B6 and +0x88 = scene+0xF1C. When the receiver is a host (never in EN) it also records src_ip/src_port in entity+0x6A/+0x80 and sets +0x14EA=1. If the receiver is in room phase 2, or phase 1 with F1C < 5100, actions 1/5/7 and input_b are zeroed. Framing: 8-byte Fireway header (len\|0x800\|seq<<12; seq is the shared per-socket counter at CSNSocket+0x13A8, wrapping 255->0) plus the EncodebyArray checksum. The payload is XORed with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF]. reset=1.

**Trigger.** Every FrameMove tick in map mode 0 (after the 0x04 loopback at 0x423787).

**Expected response.** None. It is consumed locally by FUN_00458640 case 3.

**Gates / hazards.** - Loopback only. Do not bind UDP 42907 on the client PC. - In the local field the player entity is usually +0x98==4, so the self-receive lookup (which needs +0x98 in {1,3}) usually finds nothing and the datagram is a no-op. It still consumes a sequence number. - Byte math is modulo 256, but the maximum 7*10+8 = 78 and 11*10+5 = 115 fit.

**References.** PROTOCOL.md S2C skill-use confirmation notes 'scene+0x255=7 and scene+0x256=variant ... go out on the UDP P2P state as action*10+dir'. FUN_0042ac00 input writes at 0x42B045-0x42B22A. FUN_0042cf20 +0x257 writes at 0x42D0CA, 0x42EFDE-0x42F105 and 0x42F2D8-0x42F3C0.

**Open questions.**
- Which of dir 2/6 is left and which is right. The key bindings app+0xDE0/0xDE4 are not resolved to named keys.
- Exact meaning of the scene+0x257 status classes 1..5 (buff/effect families).
