That port is only ever written as 42907 (0x4400D9, 0x459BAB, 0x476526), which is the client's own g_sock_map bind. The datagram never leaves the machine. Conditions, all required: - scene+0xF90 != NULL. - scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6. This includes character select (F00=5) and in-world. - mode = [scene+0xF88]+0x70 == 0. The map XML 'mode' attribute is parsed by FUN_00407190 at 0x4076E7; values >1 are stored minus 2. - Host flag scene+0xF24 == 0. This is always true in EN 2008: the only write is 0 in the CGameMain ctor at 0x411FC3, confirmed by a .text scan. Rate: once per FrameMove, at most every 30 ms (~33 Hz). It is followed in the same tick by the 0x03 loopback (seq+1). Records are emitted in scene-list order. The emit filter is identical to the count filter in this mode, so the count matches the records unless more than 254 qualify: extra Adds then fail silently and the header count is too high. Receiver (FUN_00458640 case 4, accepted only when its mode != 1): drops the datagram if map_code differs, otherwise applies each record to the entity with the matching uid. See the field meanings. Framing: 8-byte Fireway header. dword0 = (len+8)&0x7FF \| 0x800 \| seq<<12, where seq is the per-socket counter CSNSocket+0x13A8 shared by all g_sock_map sends, pre-incremented and wrapping 255->0. dword1 = EncodebyArray checksum. The payload is XORed with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] (static table; cencmsg.encode_by_array). reset=1 clears the buffer after the send.

**Trigger.** Every FrameMove tick (FUN_0042b260 -> FUN_00423260) while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6 and the map mode is 0.

**Expected response.** None from any server. The client's own receive path (FUN_00458640 case 4) consumes it.

**Gates / hazards.** - Loopback only. A server or tool on the same PC must not bind UDP 42907, or the client's socket creation fails. - If scene+0x244 were still 0 (never observed after login), sendto goes to port 0 and fails silently. - The stale bits 26-31 of rec_b must be masked. - Positions are truncated to even coordinates, X in 0..8190 and Y in 0..4094. Negative or larger coordinates wrap modulo the field width.

**References.** Fireway SendTo(str) 0x10003C60: inet_addr with gethostbyname fallback, SetHeader, EncodebyArray, sendto(len+8), and reset when arg3 != 0. Constants: 0x6F8AE0 = 0.5, 0x6F8A90 = 0.001, 0x6F8A98 = 2^32, 0x6F3270 = "127.0.0.1". The receiver-side decode in FUN_00458640 (0x458763-0x458D45) confirms every bit position. No server involvement is needed; the private server correctly never binds 42907.

**Open questions.**
- Direction convention of entity+0x15B0 values 2/6 (left/right) set from the facing bit is not verified.
- Exact semantic names of entity+0x8D1/+0x8D9 (attack-phase flags) and +0x8E0 (animation restart toggle) are inferred from receiver behaviour.

### C2S 0x11 — LanAddressProbeBroadcast

*client → server* · key `UDP-C2S:0x44E002/0x11` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 4 (payload after the opcode). The datagram is 13 bytes on the wire: 8-byte Fireway header + opcode + u32.

Locations: `0x44D8CA` S2C 0x02 login-result case entry; the broadcast runs only in the result==1 branch; `0x44D615` EnterCriticalSection(game_state+0x368). The whole handler runs under the lock that FrameM…; `0x44DFCA` SetBroadCast(1) via CALL EDI (EDI=[0x4A40E0] loaded at 0x44DFC2) = setsockopt(SOL_SOCKET,…; `0x44DFD4` Add u8 0x11 (IAT 0x4A40FC)

```
u32 account_id
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | u32 | Local account/player uid. It was read earlier in the same S2C 0x02 packet into scene+0x220. Receivers do not check it: case 0x11 only requires its own scene+0x220 != 0 and discards the value. | scene+0x220 ([game_state+0x4CC]+0x220) |

**Semantics.** A one-shot LAN broadcast the client sends right after a successful login. Its purpose is to learn the client's own IP address. The client's socket is bound to 0.0.0.0:42907, so it normally receives its own broadcast, as does every other client on the LAN. FUN_00458640 case 0x11 then zeroes scene+0x224..0x233, copies the recvfrom source IP string into scene+0x224 (p2p_ip) and sets scene+0x244=42907. Both values are later sent to the game server in the TCP enter-world request (p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port). Destination: 255.255.255.255:42907 (sin_addr=0xFFFFFFFF, htons(0xA79B)). SO_BROADCAST is switched on just before this send and off right after it. Framing (common to all g_sock_map sends): the socket was created by CreateSockets at 0x4402DB as Create(port 0xA79B, type 2=UDP, encode=true, header=true). NoEncode is not imported by the exe, so the encode flag always applies. Each SendTo emits exactly one datagram of 8 + payload_len bytes, where the payload is opcode + fields. - Header dword0 (SetHeader 0x10002150): bits 0-10 = (payload_len+8) & 0x7FF; bit 11 (0x800) = 1; bits 12-19 = seq; bits 20-31 = 0. - Sequence: the counter at CSNSocket+0x13A8 starts at 0 (Init / Initial_Socket), is incremented before every SendTo on this socket, and wraps 255 -> 0. The first datagram therefore has seq 1. One counter is shared by every UDP kind (this broadcast, the loopback 0x04/0x03, and 0x03 to the room host). - Header dword1 plus payload come from CEncMsg::EncodebyArray (0x10006B20), which is identical to cencmsg.encode_by_array. With T = the Fireway table at 0x1000B138 (low byte of each 4-byte entry): chk = (T[seq] + sum(plain[i] & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF, and every payload byte ^= T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF]. - The client's TCP Send uses the same header and cipher code. - A third SendTo argument of 1 zeroes the 0x7F8-byte payload buffer after the send.

**Trigger.** S2C 0x02 (login result) with result==1, after the character list and transfer status are parsed. It runs once per successful login.

**Expected response.** None. No server or peer reply is expected. The only effect is on receivers of the broadcast (normally the sender itself), whose case 0x11 handler records the source IP.

**Gates / hazards.** Gates: - Sent only in the result==1 path of S2C 0x02, and always sent there. - The receiver ignores 0x11 until scene+0x220 != 0. Hazards: - The u32 is not compared with the receiver's own uid. A 0x11 broadcast from another client on the same LAN overwrites scene+0x224 with that client's IP (last writer wins). - If broadcast delivery or loopback fails, scene+0x224 keeps its previous value, which may be empty. - A server process on the client machine must not bind UDP 42907. The client's own bind at CreateSockets 0x4402DB would fail and the socket-creation error path runs.

**References.** PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x02 (login result) already mentions this broadcast. PROTOCOL.md C2S enter-world fields p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port (scene+0x224 / +0x244) are what this datagram feeds. In server/windslayer_server.py, UDPMapServer (a logger/decoder for this datagram) is defined but deliberately not started in main(): the comment notes that binding 42907 breaks the client. No server action is needed. Fireway SendTo(ulong) body 0x10003E38-0x10003F4F: htons(port), raw ip into sin_addr, sendto(sock, buf, len+8, 0, &sa, 16), and reset if arg3 != 0.

**Open questions.**
- Whether the original server-side infrastructure ever listened for this broadcast. It cannot cross routers, so it is most likely a pure self-discovery trick.
- On Windows hosts with several interfaces, which source IP recvfrom reports for the looped-back broadcast. This decides the p2p_ip value.

The local player (state 3, uid == scene+0x220) also matches. | sender: scene+0x220 (0x423692/0x4237A2); receiver: compared at 0x42388B |
| `input_a` | u8 | Primary input, encoded action*10 + dir (u8 arithmetic). Ones digit -> entity+0x8B3 = input direction. The sender resets scene+0x254 to 8 every tick (8 = no direction); the key handler sets 2 or 6 (0x42B05E/0x42B045). Tens digit -> entity+0x8B4 = action state.… | sender: scene+0x255*10 + scene+0x254 (0x4236A5); receiver: entity+0x8B4 (tens), entity+0x8B3 (ones) |
| `input_b` | u8 | Secondary input, encoded variant*10 + sub. Tens digit -> entity+0x8B5 = action sub/variant (scene+0x256 = skill variant). Ones digit -> entity+0x8B6 = sub-state (scene+0x257, values 0..5 written by FUN_0042cf20). | sender: scene+0x256*10 + scene+0x257 (0x4236BF); receiver: entity+0x8B5 (tens), entity+0x8B6 (ones) |

**Semantics.** DATAGRAM FRAMING (Fireway CSNSocket UDP; applies to every UDP opcode on port 42907). One datagram = 8-byte header + body. - hdr0 (u32 LE): - bits 0-10 = size = 8 + body_len. The receiver trusts this, not the recvfrom length; the dispatcher gets len = size - 8. - bit 11 (0x800) = ENCODED flag. It is set by SetHeader when encryption is on and NoEncode is off. The server's NO_ENCODE_FLAG name for this bit is backwards. - bits 12-19 = seq (u8). - bits 20-31 = unused: the sender leaves them 0 and the receiver ignores them. - hdr1 (u32 LE) = checksum, checked only when bit 11 is set. - Encoding (EncodebyArray 0x10006B20 / DecodebyArray 0x10006BC0, static and key-independent; SetCodeKey is never called on this socket). T[i] = low byte of the dword at Fireway 0x1000B138 + 4*i (= cencmsg._STATIC_TABLE). - body[i] ^= T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] - checksum = (T[seq] + sum(plain[i] & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF - The decoder accepts when hdr1 - ((T[seq] + sum + T[seq+0x25]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq. - cencmsg.encode_by_array/decode_by_array implement exactly this. - Sender (client SendTo 0x10003C60/0x10003DF0): pre-increments a per-socket seq (+0x13A8: 1..255, then 0), sets size and bit 11, encodes, and sends exactly size bytes. - Receiver: GetUDPHeader drops a datagram only if its seq equals the last accepted seq on this socket (any source; initial last_seq = 0 from Init). Unlike TCP there is no ordering requirement, no size sanity check, and no socket close. A datagram with bit 11 clear is accepted as plaintext even though this socket encrypts. - Dispatch: FUN_00458640 returns if owner+0x408 (WM_CLOSE flag) != 0. Otherwise it locks owner+0x368, reads u8 opcode at offset 0 and handles exactly one message per datagram. OPCODE 0x03 (player input). - Reads u32 uid, u8 input_a, u8 input_b. FUN_00423850 finds the player/spectator entity with that uid. - Writes the decoded digits into entity+0x8B3..+0x8B6: dir, action, variant, sub. These are the same input slots that FUN_00412100 fills for remote players from the TCP movement queue; the entity update FUN_00413920 consumes them. - Stamps entity+0x88 = scene+0xF1C (room clock, +30 per tick). - Sets entity+0x15DC = 1 (activity flag) unless input_a == 8. - No map-mode gate: accepted in field and arena modes. - Scene bytes +0x254..+0x257 are read ONLY by the UDP sender FUN_00423260. In field mode the client sends this datagram to itself every tick (127.0.0.1:42907), so field-mode local-player keyboard input reaches the local entity only through this UDP loopback. In arena mode a non-host sends it to the room host instead (no loopback). - EN-only dead code (host flag scene+0xF24 is never set): - During countdown (F04==1 && F1C<5100) or round end (F04==2), actions 1/5/7 are zeroed, and so are the input_b digits. - The first packet from each peer stores its source ip (str16 at entity+0x6A) and port (+0x80) and sets +0x14EA=1. The host then unicasts snapshots there (0x423759).

**Trigger.** Generated by clients every logic tick in FUN_00423260, called from FUN_0042B260 when scene+0xF90 (map socket) != NULL. - Field mode ([map]+0x70==0), non-host: loopback to 127.0.0.1:[scene+0x244] (0x4237FD). - Arena mode ([map]+0x70==1), non-host: sent to host_ip:(room_no+10000) from S2C 0x2F. It goes every tick while the local entity +0x98==3; otherwise only while scene+0xF08==0 (no snapshot yet) or as a keepalive when scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C > 9000. - A server or room host emulator would send it to the client's ip:42907 (p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port from C2S 0x2B).

**Expected response.** None. The client sends no reply. In arena mode the host is expected to answer with snapshot datagrams 0x07/0x08/0x09 (not traced here).

**Gates / hazards.** Gates: - owner+0x408 == 0 (the game is not closing). - Header accepted: seq != last accepted seq; if bit 11 is set, the checksum must be valid. - uid must match an entity with +0x98 in {1,3}. Hazards: - SEQ COLLISION: the dedupe is per socket, not per peer, and the client's own loopback datagrams (2 per tick in field mode: 0x04 then 0x03) land on the same socket. A server datagram whose seq equals the last accepted seq is dropped silently. The only trace is a log line 'Error occured in Fireway (304)'. Never use seq 0 for the first datagram after socket init. Resending with a different seq is safe because this message sets absolute state. - If bit 11 is set with size field < 8, DecodebyArray loops over (size-8) treated as a huge unsigned count and the client crashes. With bit 11 clear, size < 8 just yields len < 0, opcode 0, no-op. - A datagram longer than 4078 bytes overflows Fireway's stack buffer (memcpy uses recv length, 0x100041E8). Keep size <= 0x7FF. - If the size field is larger than the bytes actually sent, the missing bytes read as 0. - There is no source-address filter: any host can inject input for any player uid, including the receiver's own local player (overridden until the next loopback tick). - FUN_00423850 dereferences scene+0xC without a NULL check. Safe in practice because the scene exists before the socket is created (0x4402E9). - u8 packing overflows if action > 25. - Blocking UDP loopback on 42907 (firewall, port already bound by a second client) removes field-mode local input.

**References.** - Byte-identical to the client's own UDP 0x03 sends at 0x4236F5/0x4237FD (Add u8 0x03, Add u32 [scene+0x220], Add u8 [+0x255]*10+[+0x254], Add u8 [+0x256]*10+[+0x257]). - cencmsg.py encode_by_array/decode_by_array match Fireway 0x10006B20/0x10006BC0. - PROTOCOL.md: S2C 0x07/0x05 name the same entity fields input_dir_8b3/action_state_8b4/action_sub_8b5/action_sub_8b6. - Portal trigger spec: +0x8B4==4 means Up. - C2S 0x93 spec: the idle check uses +0x15DC. - windslayer_server.py has no UDP sender; its UDPMapServer class is never started, and it correctly notes that 42907 is the client's own bind.

**Open questions.**
- In arena mode a non-host client never loops 0x03 back to itself. Does the original room host (external, at host_ip:room_no+10000, since the in-client host flag is dead in EN) relay 0x03 to every client, or is movement purely snapshot-driven (0x07/0x08/0x09)? Not decidable statically.
- Exact meaning of each digit value: dir codes besides 2/6/8, action codes besides 4 (Up) and 7 (skill), and the scene+0x257 sub-state (0..5). Consumers are in FUN_00413920/FUN_00412360 and were not fully traced.
- entity+0x88 (last-input room-clock stamp) has no reader found other than the reset in FUN_00428090. Its purpose (idle timeout?) is unconfirmed.

**Semantics.** DATAGRAM FRAMING (all UDP on g_sock_map; Create(0xA79B, type=2, encode=1, header=1) @0x4402DB): same 8-byte Fireway header as TCP. hdr0 u32 = size (bits 0-10 = 8+body_len) \| 0x800 (EncodebyArray flag) \| seq<<12 (bits 12-19, bits 20-31 = 0); u32 checksum; body = opcode + grammar, XORed with the static table (cencmsg.py EncodebyArray, the same as TCP). Receive path: recvfrom @0x10004755 -> UDPBufferManager 0x10004180 (copies the datagram into a ~4 KB stack buffer) -> GetUDPHeader 0x10003A00 -> listener slot 4 0x478850 -> FUN_00458640(ECX=body, owner=game_state 0x70EA00, len=(hdr0&0x7FF)-8, from_ip, from_port). The length comes from the header, not from the datagram size. GetUDPHeader has no [8,0x7FF] range check. Seq rule: one per-socket last_seq (+0x13AC, set to 0 by the ctor and Init). If last_seq >= 255 it is first reset to -1. The datagram is dropped (error 0x130) iff seq == last_seq; otherwise last_seq = seq, and that happens BEFORE the checksum check. Flag 0x800 set: DecodebyArray, and a checksum failure drops it (0x12F). Flag clear: the body is accepted as plaintext. The client's own SendTo pre-increments a per-socket counter (+0x13A8), wrapping 255->0, so client datagrams carry seq 1..255,0,1.... The source address is never validated. Dispatcher: if owner+0x408 != 0 the datagram is silently dropped; otherwise EnterCriticalSection(owner+0x368), u8 opcode, switch. OPCODE 0x04 (normal maps). Processed only when map_mode != 1. Steps: read the 4-byte header into scene+0xEEC; if hdr>>18 != current map code, stop. Then owner+0x1524 = timer, now = timeGetTime(), and for i in 0..count-1 read 8 bytes into scene+0xEF0 and walk the whole scene entity list (scene+0xC). For EVERY entity with +0x98 >= 3 (alive player or monster) and +0x84 == uid: (a) If +0x15A0 == 0 (never positioned), snap +0x15A4/+0x15A8 = (2x, 2y). If that entity is the camera target scene+0xEE8, also snap the camera (owner+0x488 = x, +0x490 = y-100 as f64, clear +0x474/+0x478/+0x4A8/+0x4AC/+0x498/+0x4A0, ints owner+0x1044/+0x1048). Otherwise, if now != +0x15A0 and (2x,2y) != (+0x1598,+0x159C), append a motion segment {from=+0x1598/+0x159C, delta, f64 duration=now-+0x15A0, f64 0} to entity+0x1588; FUN_0042AA10 then interpolates +0x15A4/+0x15A8. (b) +0x15B0 = facing (2/6). (c) If the entity is the local player (scene+0x970) and action_idx is 0x17..0x21 (a skill cast is echoed), clear the pending cast scene+0x255/+0x256. (d) Animation toggle: a change zeroes +0x15AC; store +0x15B2. (e) If the old +0x15B1 == 0 and attack_phase != 0, play FX by action_idx: idx 1/0x10 -> sound 2 plus effect {5,2,0,+/-10 by facing,0,x,y,0} queued on owner+0x430. idx 0x1F: class(+0x110)==2 and tier(+0x111)==2 -> FUN_0042B580(0xDA,0,0,x,y,1,7,facing). idx 0x1F/0x21 with class 6, tier 2: effect 0x114 (idx 0x1F; on non-arena maps it also queues effects 0x37/0x54 on the uid with sounds and an HP-gauge refresh) or 0x118 (idx 0x21). It is offset horizontally by trunc((+0x15AC-450)*mult)+100 against the facing, with mult 1.2 or 1.26..1.8 from FUN_00426C50(0x17C) returning 0x17C..0x185. (f) +0x15B1 = attack_phase. (g) If action_idx+1 != +0x15B4, call FUN_0042B860(owner, action, entity) for action-start FX. Action 0x10 clears the entity buff tables +0xE84/+0x107C and refreshes the stat panel, HP gauge and party bars. Then set +0x15AC: 0 unless the old action was 6, in which case new action 1 gives class(+0x112) 2/4 -> 120, 3 -> 210, 5/6 -> 270, else 150, and new action 4 gives +0x112==3 -> 180, 5/6 -> 200, else 1380. Then +0x15B4 = action. (h) Always: +0x15A0 = now, +0x1598 = 2x, +0x159C = 2y. Nothing is read after the last record. Records never create or remove entities. WHO SENDS IT: in the EN client, FUN_00423260 builds 0x04 every game tick (called from FUN_0042B260 while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6) from all entities with +0x98==3, or +0x98==4 and +0xE64>=3. When map_mode==0 and scene+0xF24 (host) == 0, it SendTo's it to 127.0.0.1:scene+0x244 (its own port 42907) @0x423787, followed by a 0x03 datagram @0x4237FD. So in normal fields this handler is the client's own simulation-to-display bridge: f64 pos +0x11F8/+0x1288, +0x8BD, +0x904/+0x8FE and +0x8E0 are copied through the wire bitfields into +0x1598..+0x15B4, which the renderer FUN_00431960 draws.

**Trigger.** Every client game tick (FUN_0042B260 -> FUN_00423260) while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6 on a normal map; sent by the client to itself at 127.0.0.1:42907.

**Expected response.** None. No reply on UDP or TCP. A private server does NOT need to send 0x04: the client loops it back to itself every tick.

**Gates / hazards.** Gates: (1) owner+0x408 != 0 drops the datagram before the opcode. (2) map_mode == 1 drops 0x04. (3) There is no NULL check on [owner+0x4D8] or [owner+0x4CC] in this case (unlike 0x06/0x0A/0x0B/0x10). (4) hdr>>18 must equal the current map code, otherwise nothing after the header is used (scene+0xEEC is still overwritten). (5) An entity is updated only if it already exists with +0x98 >= 3 and a uid < 2^25. Hazards: (a) The client already feeds itself 0x04 via loopback, so a server-sent 0x04 gets applied on top of it. Positions jitter between the two sources, and a server datagram whose seq equals the client's last loopback seq is dropped. (b) SERVER CONSTRAINTS IMPLIED BY THE LOOPBACK: entity uids (monsters too, and account_id for the local player) must be < 33,554,432 (2^25), and X must stay in 0..8190 and Y in 0..4094. Otherwise the display fields never match or wrap, and the entity renders frozen or at the wrong place. (c) Short datagram: GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) with offset+N > len does not copy or advance. It calls the g_sock_game listener OnError(0x17, opcode) (FUN_004788E0 logs 'Error occured in Fireway (23), WSA(4)', no disconnect) and the stale scene+0xEF0 record is re-applied for each missing record. (d) The count is not bounded by the length. (e) The first datagram on a fresh socket with seq 0 is dropped (last_seq starts at 0). (f) UDPBufferManager copies the datagram into a ~0xFF0-byte stack buffer with no length check. Keep datagrams <= 2047 bytes.

**References.** Sender FUN_00423260 (0x4232B2 opcode, 0x4233D8 header, 0x423432-0x423609 record packing, 0x423616 Add 8, 0x423787 loopback). Fireway.dll SendTo 0x10003C60 (SetHeader 0x10002150 + EncodebyArray when +0x13B5=1 and +0x13B4=0; NoEncode is never called by the exe). Map code field is also used by C2S TCP map_code ([[0x70EED8]+0x1B8]) in PROTOCOL.md. PySlayer and windslayer_server have no UDP snapshot support (the server only has an abandoned fake-0x11 UDP experiment).

**Open questions.**
- Exact names of the action enum values (entity+0x904) beyond 8=idle, 4=attacking, 0x10=dead/down, 0x16=downed/revive; and precisely what +0x8D9/+0x8D1 (the attack_phase sources) represent.
- Whether [0x70EED8] (map object) can be NULL when a datagram arrives before the first map load; case 0x04/0x07-0x09 dereference it without a check.
- FUN_00426C50(0x17C,0) is assumed to return the caster's learned skill id in 0x17C..0x185 (skill level scaling); not traced.

Then seq == last_seq -> drop (err 0x130); otherwise last_seq = seq, set before decoding. last_seq is per socket and shared by every sender, including the client's own loopback datagrams. - Bit 11 clear: body accepted as plaintext with NO checksum check. - Bit 11 set: requires +0x13B5 != 0 and +0x13B4 == 0, else drop 0x133. +0x13B4 is set only by NoEncode, which the exe does not import. DecodebyArray XORs each body byte with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] and requires h1 - ((T[seq] + sum(plain_i & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq, else drop 0x12F. T = low byte of each dword in the table at 0x1000B138; this equals cencmsg.py encode_by_array. - Every field read is CSNSocket::GetDataFromPacket (this = g_sock_game, used only for its error callback), little-endian. A short read leaves the destination untouched, does not advance, and logs through listener slot 6. Example plaintext datagram (seq 1, uid 1, hp 500, popup 37): 11 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 06 01 00 00 00 F4 01 25 00.

**Trigger.** The arena authority (battle server or host at the S2C 0x2F address; not emitted by the EN client) applies ordinary damage to an entity in a map-mode-1 room.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** - Silently ignored unless owner+0x408 == 0, owner+0x4D8 != NULL and map+0x70 == 1. In normal field maps use the TCP HP packets. - The uid must exist in scene+0xC. uid 0 always fails. - Seq: never repeat the seq of the previously accepted datagram on this socket, which also includes the client's loopback traffic. The first datagram after socket creation must not use seq 0. Plaintext (bit 11 clear) is accepted, but the seq check still applies. - h0 length must equal 8 + body length. Too short: reads fail and stale stack values get written. Too long: extra reads return 0. - cur_hp is u16 and not clamped. HP 0 does not kill; send the state via snapshots. - The popup is assigned, and each arrival flushes. A popup shows only if entity+0x98 >= 3 and the value is non-zero, and it needs scene+0x970 non-NULL (otherwise the slot stays pending). - No source-address validation.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the wire bytes (u32, u16, u16), the stack slots ([esp+0x30] -> +0x9C, [esp+0x18] -> +0x1114) and the jump-table routing (re-decoded from the binary: idx[3]=2 -> 0x4595B9). The dispute was the grammar, and analyst A is right. The asm exits to 0x459BB5 BEFORE any field read when owner+0x4D8 is NULL or map+0x70 != 1 (0x4595C1/0x4595CB), and exits after the uid read when FUN_004189f0 returns NULL (0x4595FF), so the cur_hp/popup reads are conditional. The verified TCP spec encodes such client-state gates in the grammar (TCP 0x40 'if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) { stop }', TCP 0x20 'if(client_in_battlefield_map) { stop }'); B's flat grammar drops them. B's claim that FUN_0042fd20 'also runs every tick' is wrong for this mode: FUN_0042b260 at 0x42B4BA CMP [map+0x70],0 / JNZ 0x42B4CC calls the flush only in mode 0 (A correct). B is right, and A silent or imprecise, on these framing details: initial last_seq = 0 (Fireway ctor 0x100019A2 XOR EAX,EAX -> 0x100019E6), so seq 0 is dropped as the first datagram; the zeroed buffer is 0xFEE bytes (byte [buf]=0 plus memset(buf+1,0,0xFED) at 0x100041C4-0x100041D5); and the checksum mask is applied before seq is added (0x10006C41 AND 0x0FFFFFFF, 0x10006C47 SUB, 0x10006C4C CMP with the seq byte). A's formula is numerically equivalent for real lengths. The kind/style decode of FUN_0042fd20 (0x42FD69-0x42FE5A, [7]=EBP=0) was verified. Local counterpart: FUN_00418ac0 0x419EEA. The server has no UDP sender for this opcode.

**Open questions.**
- Which process originally emitted UDP 0x06: a dedicated battle server at the S2C 0x2F host_ip:port+10000, or a host peer build not present in the EN client.
- Exact digit sprite sets for popup kinds 0/1 in FUN_00430aa0 (not asm-verified).

| `hdr.count` | bits 9-17 | Record count | loop bound |

| `rec_hi.unused` | bits 26-31 | Ignored; send 0 | none |

A datagram is dropped iff its seq equals the last accepted seq on the socket. Length is taken from the header. Arena ('P2P room', map_mode==1) snapshot for room phase 0 (waiting/intermission). Same wire grammar as 0x04, but accepted only when map_mode == 1. After the map-code check: (1) toggle the round-timer control in windows 4 and 0x17 based on the PRE-packet scene+0xF04 (==1: zero +0x18 of the 3rd child; else FUN_00489320(ui,4\|0x17,3,3)); (2) scene+0xF08++ (snapshots received since S2C 0x2F); (3) if scene+0xF04 != 0: FUN_00428090(scene,0). For a non-host (scene+0xF24==0, always true in EN) this only sets scene+0xF04 = 0. Then FUN_00442EE0 (blue/red/spectator status text), FUN_00443280 (team-balance notice) and FUN_004307C0 (camera follows the local player if it has a team, else picks a player to spectate via FUN_004305B0); (4) if timer != owner+0x1524: countdown/Fight! messages for timer 1..5 and the clock text F37*60-timer in windows 0x480/4/0x17 control 3; (5) owner+0x1524 = timer, then the per-record loop exactly as described for 0x04 (snap/interpolate position, facing, cast-echo clear, anim toggle, attack FX, action change via FUN_0042B860, +0x15AC timers, +0x15A0/+0x1598/+0x159C). Arena-only additions inside the action-change block: new action 0x10 prints '[<name>]is down.' colored by team (+0x14EB 1 = 0xFF5D9DFF, 2 = 0xFFFF5D5D), plus 'Revival in 20 seconds.' for the local player when room type scene+0xF70 >= 5. In attack FX idx 0x1F the extra 0x37/0x54 effects are skipped in arena. WHO SENDS IT: the arena room HOST (FUN_00423260 with scene+0xF24 != 0). Each tick it sends the opcode from its scene+0xF04 (0 -> 0x07, 2 -> 0x09, else 0x08) to every peer entity's +0x6A ip / +0x80 port, which it learned from that peer's UDP 0x03 hello (FUN_00423850). In the EN client scene+0xF24 is never set non-zero, so the host is external: host_ip:room_no+10000 from S2C TCP 0x2F. Non-host arena clients do NOT build snapshots. They only send 0x03 (u32 uid + two action/dir bytes) to that address every tick, so in arena maps the display state of ALL entities, the local player included, comes from these host datagrams.

**Trigger.** Arena host tick while the host's room phase scene+0xF04 == 0.

**Expected response.** None directly. The client keeps sending UDP 0x03 hellos/inputs to host_ip:(room_no+10000) every tick.

**Gates / hazards.** Gates: owner+0x408 == 0; map_mode == 1 (no NULL check on [owner+0x4D8]); hdr>>18 == map code; records apply only to existing entities with +0x98 >= 3 and a matching 25-bit uid. Phase code runs only when scene+0xF04 != 0 (the transition), but scene+0xF08++, the UI toggle and the timer block run on every accepted arena snapshot. Hazards: the 9-bit timer caps at 511 s, so for round_time_min (F37) > 8 the clock can never reach 0. The same short-read and stale-record behaviour as 0x04 applies. A server emulating the host must make count equal the number of records (the in-client host code counts only +0x98==3 entities in arena but writes records for qualifying state-4 monsters too). Seq collisions with other datagrams drop packets.

**References.** FUN_00428090 phase setter (writes scene+0xF04 @0x428BA5). Host sender FUN_00423260 @0x4232AE/0x423759. S2C TCP 0x2F supplies host_ip/room_no/round_time_min (scene+0xF38/+0xF48/+0xF37) and resets scene+0xF08. Not implemented in the private server.

**Open questions.**
- Whether the local player's on-screen position in arena comes exclusively from host snapshots (renderer uses +0x15A4/+0x15A8), i.e. whether an arena without snapshot traffic freezes all sprites. Inferred from the non-host sender path; not traced through the renderer.
- Exact semantic difference between phase 0 (0x07) and phase 2 (0x09) from the original host's point of view (intermission vs round result) - the EN client has no working host path to confirm.

Arena snapshot for room phase 1 (round start countdown and fighting). Grammar identical to 0x04/0x07; accepted only when map_mode == 1 and the map code matches. Common arena steps: timer-control UI toggle by old scene+0xF04, scene+0xF08++. Phase transition (only if scene+0xF04 != 1): FUN_00428090(scene,1). For a non-host this does: if old F04 == 0, reset the round counters (F5B=1, F5C..F60, F71, F72 = 0); if scene+0xF08 > 1, reset every entity's HP/MP to max (+0x9C=+0x110C, +0xA0=+0x1110), clear buffs (+0xE84 0x1F8 bytes, +0x107C 0x90 bytes), recompute stats (FUN_0041ACE0) and possibly clear +0x14ED/+0x14EE/+0x14F0; recount living team members into F73/F74; F04 = 1. The handler then recounts F73 (team 1) / F74 (team 2) for entities with +0x98==3, team != 0, HP > 0. If this packet's timer == 0 it prints the start message (room type F70 >= 5: '<round#>Starting the Round.'; F70 <= 3: 'The battle is starting.') and 'The round will start in 5 seconds.'. The local player gets HP/MP = max, then HP/MP gauges, team status, team balance notice and camera target are refreshed, and the stat panel too if F08 > 1. Then the common countdown block (timer changes 1..5 -> messages/sound, clock F37*60-timer), owner+0x1524 = timer, and the per-record loop (see 0x04). The loop adds, for 0x08 only: when an entity's action changes away from 0x16 and F70 >= 5, restore that entity's HP/MP to max and refresh the gauges and team UI (round-mode respawn). The arena 'is down.'/'Revival in 20 seconds.' messages apply as in 0x07. Sender: arena host FUN_00423260 when its scene+0xF04 is not 0 or 2, to each peer's learned UDP address (see 0x07). Its header timer is trunc(scene+0xF1C * 0.001), the only case where the timer is non-zero.

**Trigger.** Arena host tick while the host's scene+0xF04 == 1 (round running).

**Expected response.** None. Clients continue to send UDP 0x03 input/hello datagrams to the host.

**Gates / hazards.** Gates: owner+0x408 == 0; map_mode == 1; map code match; the transition block runs only when scene+0xF04 != 1. Hazards: (1) F70 == 4 with timer 0 prints an uninitialized 32-byte stack buffer (neither sprintf branch runs). (2) The phase-1 transition heals everyone and wipes buffs whenever F08 > 1, so flipping between 0x08 and another phase mid-round resets combat state. (3) 9-bit timer limit (511 s). (4) Short reads, stale records and seq-collision drops as for 0x04.

**References.** FUN_00428090 phase-1 path (decomp lines ~388-470). Host sender FUN_00423260 @0x4232A6. S2C TCP 0x2F sets F37 (round minutes) and resets F08. Not in PySlayer or our server.

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of room type scene+0xF70 values (<=3 battle vs >=5 round-based with revival; 4 unhandled) - set by the room join/create flow, not re-verified here.
- Whether the original host sent timer 0 exactly once at phase start (needed to get the start messages), or relied on the phase-transition packet always carrying timer 0.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | Healed entity uid (entity+0x84). If it is 0 or unknown, nothing more is read. | stack [esp+0x24] |
| `has_hp` | bool | 1 byte; any non-zero means hp follows. With has_mp == 0 it also triggers effect/sound 0x37. Both bools are read before either u16. | stack [esp+0x18] |
| `has_mp` | bool | 1 byte; any non-zero means mp follows (after hp if present) and triggers effect 0x58 (on the local uid) and sound 0x58. | stack [esp+0x30] |
| `hp` | u16 | Present iff has_hp != 0. New ABSOLUTE HP after healing, zero-extended, unclamped. Written to the target (remote or local); local copy and HUD updated when the target is local. | entity+0x9C; (scene+0x970)+0x9C if local |
| `mp` | u16 | Present iff has_mp != 0. New ABSOLUTE MP, zero-extended, unclamped (any entity; local copy + HUD if local). | entity+0xA0; (scene+0x970)+0xA0 if local |

**Semantics.** Heal/restore in arena/room mode (asm 0x459856-0x459B43). UDP relay form of TCP S2C 0x40 (same wire layout), but it writes remote entity HP/MP and adds the revive-camera call. Execution order: 1. Map gate. 2. Read u32 uid; lookup (EDI; stop if NULL). 3. Read bool has_hp, then bool has_mp. 4. If has_hp: a. If the target is the local player (scene+0x220 == entity+0x84), scene+0x970 != NULL and its HP +0x9C <= 0 before the update, call FUN_004307c0(EDX=owner). If the local team byte +0x14EB != 0, it sets the camera/follow target scene+0xEE8 = local entity. Otherwise, if scene+0xEE8 is NULL or its team is 0, it calls FUN_004305b0(owner, 0x27). b. Read u16 hp; entity+0x9C = hp; if local, (scene+0x970)+0x9C = hp and FUN_00443690. c. If has_mp == 0: malloc a 0x20 record {[0]=0x0A, [1]=0x37, [2]=0, [3]=target uid, rest 0}, push it to owner+0x430 (FUN_00459df0), and Play_Sound(0x37, x=+0x15A4, y=+0x15A8, owner+0x1044, +0x1048, +0x104C, +0x1050, 0). 5. If has_mp: a. Read u16 mp; entity+0xA0 = mp; if local, (scene+0x970)+0xA0 = mp and FUN_00443780. b. Queue record {0x0A, 0x58, 0, uid = scene+0x220}. This is the LOCAL player's uid even for a remote target (client quirk). c. Play_Sound(0x58) at the target's position. 6. Always (even with both flags 0): queue record {0x0A, 0x54, 0, target uid} and Play_Sound(0x54) at the target. Type-0x0A records are drawn by FUN_00430aa0 case 0x0A at the uid's entity. There are no damage numbers and no FUN_0042fd20/FUN_00430020 call. The alive state +0x98 is not changed. No emitter in the EN client. FRAMING: identical to UDP-S2C:0x06. - 8-byte header: u32 h0 (bits 0-10 total length incl. header, bit 11 encoded, bits 12-19 seq) + u32 checksum; one message per datagram; listener len = (h0&0x7FF)-8. - Seq equal to the per-socket last_seq (initial 0; reset to -1 once >= 0xFF) is dropped. - Bit 11 clear = plaintext, no checksum. Bit 11 set = XOR T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] with checksum h1 - ((T[seq]+sum(plain&0x5F)+T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq (cencmsg.py encode_by_array). - owner+0x408 != 0 drops all. LE reads; a short read leaves stale stack values and does not advance. Example plaintext (seq 2, uid 1, HP 800, MP 300): 13 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 0A 01 00 00 00 01 01 20 03 2C 01.

**Trigger.** The arena authority reports that an entity was healed or used HP/MP recovery (potion or heal skill). This includes healing a dead local player (the camera refocuses).

The asm exits at 0x4597B9/0x4597C3 before reading anything outside map mode 1, and at 0x4597F7 after the uid when FUN_004189f0 returns NULL, so the u16 read is conditional. This matches the verified TCP spec gate convention; B's flat 'u32 uid / u16 cur_mp' omits it. Both analysts correctly note: no FUN_00430020 call, and FUN_00443780 only on the local branch (JNZ exit at 0x459834). Framing seq-init (0) and checksum-mask placement follow B, verified in Fireway.dll at 0x100019E6 and 0x10006C41-0x10006C4C.

### S2C 0x11 — UdpLocalEndpointDiscovery

*server → client* · key `UDP-S2C:0x11` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: Body is 5 bytes including the opcode, so the datagram is 13 bytes and header size = 0x00D. Fixed length. A truncated body still works: the failed u32 read only logs, and the IP copy happens anyway.

Locations: `0x478867` Thunk into FUN_00458640 (ECX=body, owner=0x70EA00, len=(hdr&0x7FF)-8, from_ip, from_port); `0x458661` owner+0x408 (WM_CLOSE) gate, then EnterCriticalSection(owner+0x368) @0x458688, then u8 op…; `0x459B4F` Gate: scene [owner+0x4CC] != NULL and scene+0x220 (account_id/local uid) != 0; otherwise …; `0x459B6A` u32 read (IAT 0x4A40C8) into stack [esp0+0x14]; never used afterwards

```
u32 sender_account_id
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sender_account_id` | u32 | The broadcaster's account id / local uid (scene+0x220 on the sender). The receiver reads it and discards it: no comparison with its own uid. | sender: scene+0x220 (0x44DFE0); receiver: stack local only (unused) |

**Semantics.** Framing: same Fireway UDP framing as the UDP-S2C:0x03 spec. 8-byte header: u32 size\|0x800(encoded)\|seq<<12, then u32 by-array checksum. The seq must differ from the last accepted seq on the socket. Plaintext (bit 11 clear) is also accepted. Purpose: local P2P endpoint self-discovery. - Right after a successful login, the client broadcasts {0x11, account_id} to 255.255.255.255:42907 from its own socket, which is bound to 0.0.0.0:42907. The broadcast is delivered back to that socket. - Handler steps: 1. Checks that a scene exists and that account_id (scene+0x220) is set. 2. Consumes the u32 and ignores it. 3. Zeroes the 16-byte string scene+0x224 and copies in the datagram's SOURCE IPv4 dotted string, i.e. the client's own outgoing interface address as seen by the stack. 4. Forces scene+0x244 = 42907. - Uses of these values: - The client reports them to the game server as p2p_ip (str[16]) and p2p_udp_port (u32) in C2S 0x2B EnterWorldRequest. - FUN_00423260 uses scene+0x244 as the loopback SendTo port. - No other code writes scene+0x224. The scene ctor memset (0x411FAE, +0x48..+0xEE7) leaves it all zeros until this datagram arrives. scene+0x244 is also set to 42907 at 0x4400D9 and 0x476526.

**Trigger.** The client itself: S2C login result==1 handler (0x44DFBC-0x44E012), once per successful login. Nothing on the server side needs to send it. It could also arrive from any other host broadcasting on the LAN (another client logging in) or from a deliberate unicast.

**Expected response.** None. The learned endpoint is reported later in C2S 0x2B (key 0x42F904/0x2B, fields p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port).

**Gates / hazards.** Gates: - owner+0x408 == 0. - UDP header accepted (seq != last accepted seq; valid checksum if bit 11 is set). - scene != NULL and scene+0x220 != 0. Before login the datagram is consumed with no effect. Hazards: - NO SENDER VALIDATION. Every 0x11 datagram from any source overwrites p2p_ip with that sender's address. A server unicasting 0x11 would set p2p_ip to the SERVER's IP, not the client's. Another client logging in on the same LAN rewrites this client's p2p_ip to the other machine's IP. The server should not send this opcode. - If the broadcast loopback is blocked (firewall, no interface or broadcast route, port 42907 bind failure), p2p_ip stays empty (all zeros) in C2S 0x2B. - The IP string always fits in 16 bytes because Fireway builds it with inet_ntoa, so the unbounded strcpy cannot overflow. - Generic UDP framing hazards (see UDP-S2C:0x03): seq collision drop, crash on an encoded datagram with size < 8, overflow above 4078 bytes.

**References.** - PROTOCOL.md C2S 0x2B EnterWorldRequest: p2p_ip is 'learned from its UDP 0x11 datagram's source address'; captures show '127.0.0.1' and '10.5.0.2'. - PROTOCOL.md S2C login result: the broadcast of 0x11 + account_id to 255.255.255.255:42907. - windslayer_server.py _fake_map_server (disabled) once sent 20x UDP 0x11 + 64 zero bytes as a guessed 'map-server response' and saw UI errors. Statically, 0x11 only rewrites scene+0x224/+0x244, so it is not a map-server response. - The server's UDPMapServer class is never started, and there is no UDP send path.

**Open questions.**
- The earlier live experiment (20 UDP 0x11 datagrams to 127.0.0.1:42907) was followed by 'cascading UI errors'. Static analysis of case 0x11 shows no UI side effects, so those symptoms were probably coincidental or caused by concurrent TCP experiments. Unverified.
- Whether the original server actually used p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port from C2S 0x2B to broker arena P2P, or the room host at host_ip:room_no+10000 learned addresses from datagram sources instead.

### C2S 0x11 — UnequipItem

*client → server* · key `0x46CE18/0x11` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 5 + 2*enchant_count (enchant_count 0..5, so 5..15 bytes)

Locations: `0x46CAD0` item-activate handler (window id on the stack, ECX = UI control/slot index, EDX = ctx); b…; `0x44BE1C` caller: EAX = window id, ECX = slot, stack = game_state; passes ctx = game_state+0xD5C; `0x44BF04` drag path: source window 7 dropped on destination window 9 calls 0x44BD10(EAX=7); `0x43EAEE` double-click path: WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK (0x203) on an item slot calls 0x44BD10(EAX=window id)

```
u16 item_id
u8 enchant_count
repeat(enchant_count) { u16 enchant }
u16 enchant_last
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_id` | u16 | catalog id of the equipped item to take off | word rec+0x00 ([ESP+0x1C]); rec is the record 0x466980 copies from the selected slot of window 7 (Equipment) |
| `enchant_count` | u8 | number of leading non-zero words in rec+0x02..+0x0A (max 5) | computed by the loop at 0x46CDC0 (BL) |
| `enchant` | u16 | enchant/option word i of the equipped item | word rec+0x02+2*i |
| `enchant_last` | u16 | 6th attribute word, always sent | word rec+0x0C ([ESP+0x28]) |

**Semantics.** Asks the server to unequip an equipped item and return it to the bag. The client changes nothing locally and waits for the server. The body layout matches C2S 0x0F EquipItem (0x44C2C0) exactly, only the opcode differs.

**Trigger.** The player double-clicks an equipped item in the Equipment window (window id 7), or drags it from the Equipment window onto the Inventory window (9). Both reach 0x44BD10 -> 0x46CAD0 with window 7. The source slot/control index must be 3..27.

**Expected response.** Most likely S2C 0x1E (handler 0x454090, shared with 0x24): u32 uid, u16 item_id, u8 n, n x u16 enchant, u16 enchant_last. It calls 0x4269A0 to clear the entity's equip slot (+0x13C / +0x16E), recomposes the sprite (0x426D50) and, for the local player (uid == scene+0x220) with opcode 0x1E and bag capacity byte scene+0x3A9 <= 45, puts the item back in the bag with its attribute words. Our server's own notes also call 0x1E the remove/unequip opcode.

**Gates / hazards.** Client checks, in order: (1) slot index - 3 <= 0x18; (2) bag capacity byte char+0x361 (char = ctx+0x18 = scene+0x48) <= 45 AND at least one empty word in bag[0..cap) at char+0x380 (0x424D60), otherwise a modal notice 'You have no more slots for the item.' (0x489DA0) and no packet; (3) 0x466DF0 and 0x466E10 abort (no message) when ctx+0 == 0x259 and ctx+0x20 or ctx+0x1C is set (a special UI mode, probably a personal shop); (4) 0x466980 finds the selected Equipment record and its catalog entry; (5) the local player entity (char+0x928) has action state +0x904 not in {1,4,14,15} and < 24, the same for +0x15B4 (4 = attacking), and word scene+0x258 == 0; otherwise chat notice 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.' (0x4817D0) and no packet; (6) catalog type +0x154 == 1 (equipment), otherwise nothing. No local pending state: double-clicking again before the server answers sends another 0x11, so the server must check the item is still equipped.

**References.** Captured C2S 0x0F equip 'B3 00 00 00 00' (u16 179, u8 n=0, u16 0) confirms this shared shape (builder 0x44C2C0 uses the same loop, reading from rec+2). PySlayer parse_0F reads a fixed u16,u8,u16 and ignores the n-word loop; PySlayer has no 0x11 parser. Our server: _dispatch has no inbound 0x11. Its _build_en_opcode_1D_equip docstring states '0x1E is the REMOVE/unequip opcode', which matches the expected response. Do not confuse this with the server-notes '0x11 + account_id' UDP broadcast on the map/tertiary socket: that is a different message on a different socket.

**Open questions.**
- What differs between S2C 0x1E and 0x24 in handler 0x454090 beyond the 0x1E-only bag re-add branch (0x45424F); is 0x24 unequip-and-destroy or a remote-player variant?
- Meaning of the 6 attribute words (enchant/option).

### C2S 0x1F — GroundItemPickupRequest

*client → server* · key `0x43D80F/0x1F` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 2

Locations: `0x43D5C0` builds and sends the packet; `0x43D7F0` Add(u8) opcode 0x1F; `0x43D801` Add(u16) ground item uid (word [EBP+0x12]); `0x43D80F` Send(1)

```
u16 ground_item_uid
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ground_item_uid` | u16 | instance id of the ground item (dropped loot) to pick up. The same id is matched by S2C 0x13 (FUN_00440e50 compares node+0x12). | ground-item node +0x12 (word). Node comes from the list at scene(*0x70EECC)+0x1C. FUN_00423a10 wrote the value (param_6… |

**Semantics.** The player asks to pick up one ground item. The client does all range, ownership and bag-space checks first. It sends at most one 0x1F per key event: the first item in the scene ground-item list that passes all checks. The client does not change the item locally. It waits for S2C 0x13 to set node+0x16=2, set node+0x1C=picker, and, when the picker is the local uid, add the item to the bag and print "you've received %s. (Count:%u)".

**Trigger.** Pickup key held during any key-down message. The key is the bound slot at game_state+0xDFC, copied from COption+0x68 (registry "Key3", default 'W' 0x57) by FUN_00475710. FUN_0043d5c0 runs from MsgProc on WM_KEYDOWN when the UI did not consume the key and chat does not have focus (g_ui_root+8==0, g_ui_root+0x30==0). It also runs on WM_SYSKEYDOWN with Alt/F10. It then calls GetAsyncKeyState(pickup key).

**Expected response.** S2C 0x13 (handler 0x4518D0): u16 ground_item_uid, u16 count, u32 picker_uid. Broadcast it to everyone on the map so other clients mark the item taken. If validation fails there is no known error reply; the client simply keeps the item on the ground.

**Gates / hazards.** Gates, in order: (1) scene+0xF00 == 6 (in-game). (2) NOT (game_state+0xD7C != 0 && game_state+0xD5C == 0x259). (3) FUN_00468fa0() == 0: UI window 0x28C/modal state is not 3. (4) app+0x9E == 0 (device not lost) and app+0x9D != 0 (app active). (5) The pickup key is down. (6) scene != 0 and scene+0x970 (local player entity) != 0. Per item in the scene+0x1C linked list: skip null nodes and nodes with state byte +0x16 == 2 (already picked). Range: (player u16@+0x15A4 - node.x u16@+0x0E)^2 + (player u16@+0x15A8 - node.y u16@+0x10)^2 < 625 (unsigned). Ownership: node+0x1C owner == 0, or == scene+0x220 (local uid), or node+0x24 + 15000 < scene+0xF1C (15 s loot protection). Otherwise the item is flagged as not owned. Bag space by node+0x18 category (from item def +0x154): 0 = capacity byte scene+0x3AA <= 45 and FUN_00424c80 (qty node+0x14 <= 999; a same-id stack at ids scene+0x63E / counts scene+0x698 with count+qty < 1000, or an empty slot). 1 = capacity scene+0x3A9 <= 45 and an empty slot in scene+0x3C8 (equipment, no stacking). 2 = capacity scene+0x3AB <= 45 and FUN_00424d00 (qty <= 99; a stack at ids +0x7A8 / byte counts +0x802 below 100, or an empty slot). Any other category is never sent. If nothing is sent: an owned in-range item with no bag space and game_state+0x3DC != 0 shows "There isn't empty space \r\nin the inventory." and clears +0x3DC (MsgProc sets it back to 1 on WM_KEYUP). Otherwise, if some in-range item was not owned, it shows "You don't have ownership of this item." HAZARDS: holding the key auto-repeats WM_KEYDOWN, so the client can send 0x1F for the same uid many times before 0x13 arrives. The server must be idempotent: grant once, ignore uids already picked. The uid is only 16 bits on the wire (node+0x12 is a u16), so ground uids must fit in u16.

**References.** PySlayer: no C2S parser for 0x1F. Our server: this is the "pickup-request opcode still unidentified" noted near windslayer_server.py:1925. Ground drops (0x12) are deferred because of it. DISCREPANCY in our _build_opcode_13 (line ~1724): it packs the second u16 as the item id, but FUN_00440e50 uses that value (param_4) as the COUNT, both for the bag add (e.g. MOVZX EAX,[ESP+0x64] at 0x440EEB) and for the "(Count:%u)" text. The item id comes from the ground node (node+0x00). Our GROUND_ITEM_UID_BASE 0x00200000 truncates to 0x0000 on the wire, so it is unsafe as a u16 uid.

**Open questions.**
- Exact meaning of item category 2 (stack max 99, ids at scene+0x7A8, byte counts at +0x802): quest/material bag?
- Whether node+0x24 (drop timestamp) comes from the S2C 0x12 wire or is stamped from the client clock (it feeds FUN_00423a10 param_9)
- What game_state+0xD7C / +0xD5C==0x259 represent (some action/cutscene state that blocks pickup)

**Semantics.** Reinforcement completion request. FUN_004684d0 runs every frame. When progress window 0x293 is in state 3 and more than 5000 ms have passed since [this+0x60], and both reinforcement slot words (+0x64 stone, +0x66 equipment) are non-zero, the client finds window 0x28C and the first node of its equipment list. It then sends 0x68: equipment id, stone id, and the 6 option words of the equipment record copy. The server decides the result. After Send, if [this+8]!=0, the client runs window 0x28C controls 3 and 4. The two slot-clear handlers in FUN_00469090 zero +0x64 (0x46BE08) and +0x66 (0x46BE35). Then, as on every other exit from this block, it resets the timer [this+0x60]=0 and closes window 0x293.

**Trigger.** The player places a reinforceable item and an elemental stone in the Reinforcement window (0x28C, near the smithy) and presses Reinforce (FUN_00469090 @0x46BD5C). The packet goes out on the first frame more than 5 s later.

**Expected response.** S2C 0x8E (SubHandler1 @0x46EC37): u8 result, u16, u16, then if result==1 { repeat(6) u16, u16 }. Result dialog is window 0x29B: 'Reinforcement Successful.' / 'This equipment cannot be reinforced.' / 'Reinforcement Failed.'. The client has already cleared the slots and closed the progress bar; the busy flag [this+0x2C] is cleared by the 0x8E handler.

**Gates / hazards.** Send-time gates: window 0x293 is in the UI list with [win+0x3C]==3; elapsed > 5000 ms (unsigned delta, converted to float); FUN_004830f0(0x293) != 0; word+0x64 != 0 and word+0x66 != 0; window 0x28C exists; its list head [+0xB0] and node data [node+8] are non-null. If any 0x28C lookup fails, NO packet is sent, but the timer is still reset and window 0x293 closed. [this+0x2C] busy then stays 1 until a 0x8E arrives, which a server will never send unprompted, so reinforce/refine stays locked. HAZARD: 0x67 and 0x68 share window 0x293 and timer +0x60. The opcode is chosen only by whether +0x64/+0x66 are non-zero, not by which button started the bar. Start-time gates (FUN_00469090 / FUN_00468b10): the stone must be present, the equipment must be present and reinforceable, and stone level <= equipment level. Opening the window zeroes +0x64/+0x66.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: There is no real disagreement. Both analysts described the same 16-byte wire format, u16 [this+0x66] equipment id, u16 [this+0x64] stone id, then six u16 words from the equipment record at +2..+0xC. A wrote it as repeat(6) and B as 8 flat u16s, which is why the 'structural signatures' differ. The asm confirms both: 0x46869D push 0x68 / 0x46869F Add(uchar); 0x4686A5 movzx eax,word[edi+0x66] + 0x4686AC ebx=[0x4A40F4] Add(ushort) + 0x4686B3 call ebx; 0x4686B5 movzx ecx,word[edi+0x64] + 0x4686BD call ebx; 0x4686BF add esi,2 (esi=[node+8] from 0x46868F); 0x4686C2 mov [esp+0xC],6; body 0x4686D0 movzx edx,word[esi] / 0x4686D7 call ebx / add esi,2 / dec counter / jnz 0x4686D0; 0x4686E8 Send(1). Equipment is added BEFORE stone, as both said. The node walk at 0x468669-0x46867A starts with ECX=0 and takes the index-0 (head) node at once. The canonical grammar uses repeat(6) because the code is a counted loop over contiguous record words; the bytes are identical to B's expansion. Minor corrections: the socket is [this+0x14] loaded from g_sock_game at 0x464ED9 (both right). A's post-send claim that controls 3 and 4 empty both slots fits the two slot-clear blocks at 0x46BE08 (+0x64=0) and 0x46BE35 (+0x66=0). The exact control-number-to-block mapping was not traced through FUN_00469090's switch. B's narrower claim ('control 4 clears the stone slot') is also not contradicted. The naive scout (Add8(0x68) only) was wrong. PySlayer has no C2S 0x68 parser. windslayer_server.py does not dispatch 0x68. The S2C 0x8E success path reads exactly 6 u16s (loop counter 6 at 0x46ECB5), which supports the 6-word block.

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of the 6th option word (record +0x0C): it is sent, but the client's 'has a free slot' check only covers +0x02..+0x0A.
- Which of FUN_00469090 controls 3 and 4 maps to the +0x64 clear (0x46BE08) and which to the +0x66 clear (0x46BE35); not traced through the switch table.
- Meaning of the two unlabeled u16s and the trailing u16 in S2C 0x8E (outside this C2S spec).

**Semantics.** Tells the server that the client's 5-second gathering (Mining or Herb Gathering) progress bar has finished, and for which node type and with which tool. Each frame the client first checks for craft progress window 0x293 in state 3; only if that is absent or not in state 3 does it check gather window 0x295. When window 0x295 is in state 3 and timeGetTime() - [app+0xD5C+0x5C] > 5000 ms (unsigned; the 5000.0 constant at 0x4A67AC was verified), the client sends this packet. It then sets +0x5C = 0 and closes window 0x295 with FUN_00483430(0x295,1,1). Any window-0x295 event also clears the busy flag [app+0xD84] (= this+0x28) via FUN_00446300 at 0x446A26. While the bar is running it only updates the gauge (FUN_004891e0) and sends nothing.

**Trigger.** Player uses a gathering tool item (item def +0x154 == 2) while standing near a herb node (interaction code 0x138) or mineral node (0x139), with the matching skill (0x56 Herb Gathering / 0x52 Mining), a tool of the right grade and enough level. The 5 s progress bar in window 0x295 must then finish.

The handler clears the busy flag this+0x28.

The player's interaction code [[scene+0x928]+0x94] must be 0x138 (herb) or 0x139 (mining). The record at app+0x1540 must have +0x644 of 2 or 1. The skill must be known, FUN_00427310 must pass the tool-grade check, and the item level must be <= the player's level. At send time, if [win0x295+0x11C] == 0 the function returns without sending, without closing the window and without resetting the timer, so the progress window stays stuck. That should not happen because the start requires a non-zero record. The window closes right after sending, so the client does not wait for 0x8F to hide the bar. The timing is purely client-side.

**References.** No PySlayer parser or builder for C2S 0x69 or S2C 0x8F. Not in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. Crafting and gathering strings confirm the system: 'Mining', 'Herb Gathering', 'You need a shovel to conduct mining...', 'Learn the Herb Gathering skill from Lona in Popola'.

- Exact meaning of window state value 3 at +0x3C (probably visible/open).

### S2C 0x11 — GroundItemSpawn

*server → client* · key `0x11` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 1 + sum over entries of (26 + 2*opt_count)

Locations: `0x00451516` handler block (shared with 0x12); `0x004516BC` branch: CMP opcode(byte [esp+0x43]),0x12; JNZ -> 0x45183C (0x11 path reads the state byte); `0x004518AE` CALL FUN_00423a10 = allocate 0x40-byte ground-item record and append it to the scene grou…; `0x00423A10` GroundItem create/init

```
u8 entry_count
repeat(entry_count) {
  u16 item_id
  u16 quantity
  u16 x
  u16 y
  u16 ground_id
  u32 drop_time
  u32 owner_uid
  u32 source_uid
  u8 opt_count
  repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt_word }
  u16 opt_tail
  u8 state
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entry_count` | u8 | number of ground-item entries | stack [esp+0x5e], outer loop bound (0 = nothing happens) |
| `item_id` | u16 | item template id; 1-based index into item-def vector [scene+0xF84]+8. 0 or out of range -> no record created (fields still consumed). itemdef+0x154 (category 0/1/2) copied to rec+0x18 | stack esp+0xcc -> FUN_00423a10 arg2 -> rec+0x00 |
| `quantity` | u16 | stack count (the local/offline drop generator passes 1); no reader found in this pass | stack esp+0xc4 -> arg10 -> rec+0x14 |
| `x` | u16 | world X pixel coordinate | stack esp+0x164 -> arg4 -> rec+0x0E (u16) and rec+0x30 (f64) |
| `y` | u16 | world Y pixel coordinate; client subtracts 10 when state==1 (or when scene+0xF24 != 0) | stack esp+0x19c -> arg5 -> rec+0x10 (u16) and rec+0x38 (f64) |
| `ground_id` | u16 | ground-item instance id; the client echoes it in C2S 0x1F pickup and S2C 0x13 matches on it | stack esp+0xe0 -> arg6 -> rec+0x12 (replaced by a local counter scene+0xF34 if scene+0xF24 != 0) |
| `drop_time` | u32 | drop timestamp in the map clock scene+0xF1C (ms; set by S2C 0x03/0x08, +30 per client tick). Ownership lapses when drop_time + 15000 < scene+0xF1C | stack esp+0xd8 -> arg9 -> rec+0x24 |
| `owner_uid` | u32 | uid with loot rights; 0 = anyone may pick up. Otherwise only this uid can, until the 15 s window ends | stack esp+0xfc -> arg7 -> rec+0x1C |
| `source_uid` | u32 | uid of the entity that dropped it (for example the killed monster). Only 0x12 uses it for positioning | stack esp+0xb4 -> arg8 -> rec+0x20 |
| `opt_count` | u8 | number of item extension words that follow (must be <= 5; see hazards) | stack [esp+0x5f], inner loop bound |
| `opt_word` | u16 | item extension/option word i (same 12-byte block that equipment slots keep at +0x422+i*0xC; same u8 n + u16[n] + u16 pattern as S2C 0x1D) | stack u16 buffer esp+0x218+2*i -> copied to rec+0x02+2*i |
| `opt_tail` | u16 | 6th (last) extension word, always present | stack esp+0x222 (buffer slot 5) -> rec+0x0C |
| `state` | u8 | initial ground-item state: 0 = resting on ground, 1 = drop pop-in (y-10; after 800 ms becomes 3), 3 = falling/bounce physics then 0, 2 = being picked up (flies to rec+0x1C entity, freed after 1000 ms) | stack esp+0x1c0 -> arg11 -> rec+0x16 |

**Semantics.** For each entry the client builds a 0x40-byte ground-item record (FUN_00423a10) and appends it to the scene ground-item list (scene+0x18/0x1C). Record layout: +0 item_id, +2..+0xD six extension words, +0xE x, +0x10 y, +0x12 ground_id, +0x14 quantity, +0x16 state, +0x18 item category (itemdef+0x154: 0 = consume bag +0x3AA, 1 = equip bag +0x3A9, 2 = other bag +0x3AB), +0x1C owner_uid, +0x20 source_uid, +0x24 drop_time, +0x28 animation timer = 0, +0x30/+0x38 f64 x/y. Unlike 0x12, 0x11 always uses the wire x/y and takes the state byte from the wire, so it suits listing items already on the ground (state 0) or spawning drops at exact coordinates (state 1). Items are drawn and pickable only while scene+0xF00 == 6.

**Trigger.** Server sends it to show items already lying on a map (for example after the map-load sequence), or to spawn drops at explicit coordinates with a chosen initial state.

**Expected response.** None immediately. Later, when the player presses the pickup key within about 25 px (dx^2+dy^2 < 625) of an item they may take, the client sends C2S 0x1F u16 ground_id (send site 0x43D7E8) and the server should answer with S2C 0x13.

**Gates / hazards.** STACK OVERFLOW: extension words go into a 12-byte stack buffer (esp+0x218..0x223). opt_count 6 is harmless because opt_tail overwrites slot 5; opt_count >= 7 writes past the buffer. Keep opt_count <= 5 (recommended: exactly 5). STALE DATA: the buffer is zeroed once per packet, not per entry, so an entry with a smaller opt_count inherits the previous entry's words; send a constant 5. An invalid item_id silently skips record creation without desyncing the reads. With state=1 the client subtracts 10 from y. With state=2 the item is freed after 1 s. Pickup gate in 0x43D5C0: state != 2, distance < 25 px, and owner_uid in {0, local uid} or drop_time+15000 < scene+0xF1C; otherwise the client shows "You don't have ownership of this item." A full bag shows "There isn't empty space in the inventory." LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C19, item_inventory#09): the map change (S2C 0x08 / 0x03) CLEARS the client ground-item list, so every ground item must be re-sent with S2C 0x11 on map entry. Container: scene+0x18 = {vtable 0x6F7F3C, head node, tail node, u32 count at +0x24}; node = {next, prev, record*}.

**References.** KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x11/0x12) reads the option block first and has fewer fields, so the layout differs; EN asm is authoritative. PySlayer has no S2C 0x11 builder. Our server does not send 0x11. Its comment at windslayer_server.py:170 agrees that 0x12 is a ground spawn, not a walk.

**Open questions.**
- No reader of rec+0x14 (quantity) was found in this pass, so the name 'quantity' is inferred from the offline generator passing 1.
- [RESOLVED by live verification item_inventory#09, 2026-09-17] Live: YES - the ground list is cleared by the map change (0x08/0x03); the server must re-send 0x11 for the new map. Container scene+0x18 = {vtable 0x6F7F3C, head, tail, u32 count at +0x24}, node = {next, prev, record*}. Original question: "Whether the ground-item list is cleared on map change was not traced."
- scene+0xF24 != 0 looks like a local/offline simulation mode (FUN_00413920 generates drops locally); exact meaning unconfirmed.

### S2C 0x12 — GroundItemDrop

*server → client* · key `0x12` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 1 + sum over entries of (25 + 2*opt_count)

Locations: `0x00451516` handler block (shared with 0x11); `0x004516BC` branch on opcode == 0x12: no state byte read; position resolved from entities; `0x004516D5` FUN_004189f0(EDX=source_uid, scene): find entity by uid in scene+0xC list; `0x00451774` fallback FUN_004189f0(EDX=owner_uid, scene)

```
u8 entry_count
repeat(entry_count) {
  u16 item_id
  u16 quantity
  u16 x
  u16 y
  u16 ground_id
  u32 drop_time
  u32 owner_uid
  u32 source_uid
  u8 opt_count
  repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt_word }
  u16 opt_tail
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entry_count` | u8 | number of dropped items | stack [esp+0x5e] |
| `item_id` | u16 | item template id (1-based into [scene+0xF84]+8; invalid -> skipped) | rec+0x00 |
| `quantity` | u16 | stack count | rec+0x14 |
| `x` | u16 | fallback world X | rec+0x0E / rec+0x30 f64, only if neither entity is found |
| `y` | u16 | fallback world Y | rec+0x10 (minus 10) / rec+0x38, only if neither entity is found |
| `ground_id` | u16 | ground-item instance id (echoed by C2S 0x1F, matched by S2C 0x13) | rec+0x12 |
| `drop_time` | u32 | drop time in the scene+0xF1C map clock (ms); owner rights expire 15000 ms later | rec+0x24 |
| `owner_uid` | u32 | uid with loot priority (0 = anyone) | rec+0x1C; second position lookup key |
| `source_uid` | u32 | uid of the dropping entity (for example the dead monster) | rec+0x20; first position lookup key |
| `opt_count` | u8 | number of extension words (<= 5) | inner loop bound |
| `opt_word` | u16 | item extension/option word | rec+0x02+2*i |
| `opt_tail` | u16 | 6th extension word | rec+0x0C |

**Semantics.** Same record creation as 0x11, with state forced to 1 (pop-in animation, then fall physics after 800 ms, then resting). Position: if an entity with uid == source_uid exists in the scene entity list (scene+0xC), the item appears at that entity's truncated (int)posX (+0x11F8) and posY (+0x1288); otherwise at the entity with uid == owner_uid; otherwise at the wire x/y. A uid of 0 never matches. y is then reduced by 10 (state == 1).

**Trigger.** A monster dies with loot, or an item is dropped onto the map. Broadcast to players on that map.

**Expected response.** None immediately; later C2S 0x1F u16 ground_id pickup request, answered by S2C 0x13.

**Gates / hazards.** Same stack overflow (opt_count >= 7) and stale-word hazards as 0x11. POSITION PITFALL: if the monster (source_uid) was already removed client-side and owner_uid is the killer, the item appears at the killer's feet, not the death spot. To force the wire x/y, set source_uid and owner_uid to 0 or non-existent uids (owner 0 = free-for-all), or use 0x11 with state=1. Positions are truncated to u16. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C19, item_inventory#09): the map change (S2C 0x08 / 0x03) CLEARS the client ground-item list, so every ground item must be re-sent with S2C 0x11 on map entry. Container: scene+0x18 = {vtable 0x6F7F3C, head node, tail node, u32 count at +0x24}; node = {next, prev, record*}.

**References.** Our server's _build_opcode_12_drop (windslayer_server.py:1651) has the right widths (26 bytes for one entry with no options) but mislabels fields. It writes item, x, y, count, 0, ground_uid(u32), x(u32), 0(u32), 0, 0. The client reads item, quantity, x, y, ground_id, drop_time, owner_uid, source_uid. Result: quantity=x, x=y, y=1, ground_id=0, owner_uid=x. This explains the 'misaligned drop position' and 'un-pickable' notes at :1874. The builder is unused (drops go straight to the bag). The KR 0x11/0x12 layout differs.

**Open questions.**
- Whether FUN_004189f0 can match the local player (is the local entity in the scene+0xC list?). Probably yes, since RegisterLocalPlayer calls it, but not verified.
- rec+0x14 quantity has no confirmed reader.

### S2C 0x13 — GroundItemPickedUp

*server → client* · key `0x13` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 8

Locations: `0x004518D0` handler block; `0x00451938` CALL FUN_00440e50 (fastcall ECX=ground_id, EDX=picker_uid; stack: this, quantity); `0x00440E50` find the ground record by rec+0x12, mark it picked, add to the local bag if picker is the…

```
u16 ground_id
u16 quantity
u32 picker_uid
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ground_id` | u16 | ground-item instance id from 0x11/0x12 (and C2S 0x1F) | stack esp+0x200 -> ECX -> compared with rec+0x12 |
| `quantity` | u16 | count added to the bag (consume via FUN_00423b70, other via FUN_00423e70) and shown as '(Count:%u)'; not used for equipment | stack esp+0x1f8 -> FUN_00440e50 stack arg 2 |
| `picker_uid` | u32 | uid of the player who picked the item up | stack esp+0x1c8 -> EDX -> rec+0x1C |

**Semantics.** The client scans the ground-item list (scene+0x1C) for the first record whose rec+0x12 == ground_id; if none, nothing happens. On a match it sets rec+0x16 = 2 (picked: flies toward the picker entity and is freed after 1000 ms), rec+0x28 = 0, and rec+0x1C = picker_uid. If picker_uid == local uid (scene+0x220) it adds the item by category rec+0x18. Category 0: FUN_00423b70 into the bag at +0x63E/+0x698/+0x6F4, capacity +0x3AA, with quantity. Category 1 (equipment): first empty slot in u16[+0x3C8] (capacity +0x3A9, must be <= 45); writes item_id and copies the 6 extension words to +0x422+slot*0xC. Category 2: FUN_00423e70 into +0x7A8, capacity +0x3AB, with quantity. On success it refreshes UI panes 7/8/9/0x28 and shows the center notice "you've received %s. (Count:%u)".

**Trigger.** Server reply to C2S 0x1F (u16 ground_id) once the pickup is validated; broadcast to everyone on the map so the item disappears for all.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** If the local bag add fails (full, or equipment capacity > 45), no message is shown but the ground record is still marked picked and disappears, so the item is lost client-side. The server must check bag space before sending. Nothing happens for an unknown ground_id. Only the first record with a duplicate ground_id is affected, so keep ids unique per map.

**References.** PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x13.py sends u16, u16, u32 (same widths). KR Hex-Rays case 0x13 has a leading u8 result, so it is newer and differs. Our server's _build_opcode_13 (windslayer_server.py:1675) has the correct widths and order, but names the 2nd field 'item' when it is quantity. It is never called, and C2S 0x1F is not in _dispatch.

**Open questions.**
- Bag-slot synchronisation with any server-side inventory model is not covered by this packet (no slot index is sent; the client picks the first free slot).

(Count:%u)' + FUN_00465290 refresh (types 0-2)

```
u64 gold
u32 victy
u16 item_id
u16 count
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gold` | u64 | Inventory gold, total (not a change amount) | player_info+0x228; label window 9 child 0xB via FUN_004659d0 @0x46DE70 |
| `victy` | u32 | 'Victy' currency total (checked by 'You are short of Victy.' in FUN_00467680). PySlayer and our server call it Winnie. | player_info+0x238; label window 9 child 0x27 via FUN_00465a30 @0x46DE9C (%u) |
| `item_id` | u16 | Item to grant (1-based catalog id); 0 = no item, currency update only | local [frame+0x0C] -> FUN_00440920 arg1 |
| `count` | u16 | Number granted (type 0: u16 stacks up to 999; type 2: u8 stacks up to 99; type 1 equipment always adds exactly one slot) | local [frame+0x1C] -> FUN_00440920 arg3 |

**Semantics.** Stores gold at player_info+0x228 and refreshes the inventory gold label. Stores Victy at player_info+0x238 and refreshes the Victy label (window 9 child 0x27). Then FUN_00440920 grants item_id x count. It looks up the definition in [scene+0xF84] (item_id 0 or out of range: nothing happens) and switches on its type: 0 adds to the u16-stack tab (player_info+0x5F6 ids / +0x650 counts, capacity +0x362); 1 puts one equipment slot at player_info+0x380 with a zero option block at +0x3DA (capacity +0x361, must be <= 45); 2 adds to the u8-stack tab +0x760/+0x7BA (capacity +0x363); 3 learns a skill (needs [scene+0x970]) and shows 'You've learned skill(%s).'; 4 checks and applies a class change ('... is your new class.'). If a type 0-2 add succeeds, shows 'you've received <name>. (Count:<count>)' and refreshes the inventory UI. Returns 1. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.

**Trigger.** Shop buy result (reply to C2S 0x0B), quest reward, monster drop pickup, and any gold/Victy change (item_id=0). Seen live: after C2S 0x16 quest accept the server sent 0x18 (16 B) and the client accepted it.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** gold and Victy are absolute values and overwrite whatever the client had. No crash risks (fixed size). The add silently fails (no message) when the bag is full, count=0, the capacity byte > 45, or item_id is unknown. The currency updates still apply. Equipment ignores count (adds 1) but the message still prints count. Type 3 needs the skill structure at [scene+0x970].

**References.** Matches PySlayer opcode_0x18 (p64u gold, p32u Winnie, p16u item, p16 count) and our server's _build_opcode_18 (16 B). The EN client names the u32 currency 'Victy'. [ctx+0x18] (player_info) = [ctx+0x10] (scene) + 0x48: FUN_00440920 reaches the same fields through [this+0x4CC]+0x3C8/+0x3A9/+0x63E/+0x7A8, and SubHandler1 through [ctx+0x18]+0x380/+0x361/+0x5F6/+0x760.

**Open questions.**
- What item types 0 and 2 are called in the UI (type 1 is equipment).

### S2C 0x1D — EquipItem

*server → client* · key `0x1D` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 9 + 2*stone_count

Locations: `0x004529A1` GetDataFromPacket u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8) -> uid [S+0x16C]; `0x004529BC` GetDataFromPacket u16 (IAT 0x4A4090) -> item_id [S+0xAC]; `0x004529D8` zero the 12-byte option block [S+0x224..S+0x22F]; `0x004529F6` GetDataFromPacket u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) -> stone_count [S+0x4C]

```
u32 uid
u16 item_id
u8 stone_count
repeat(stone_count) {
  u16 stone_id
}
u16 block_tail
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | Entity (player) whose equipment changes | stack [S+0x16C]; used for FUN_004189F0 lookup and compared to scene+0x220 (local player uid) |
| `item_id` | u16 | Item catalog id being equipped (must exist in the catalog at scene+0xF84 with Type +0x154 == 1) | stack [S+0xAC]; written into the entity equip grid (+0x13C) by FUN_00426680 |
| `stone_count` | u8 | Number of following u16 option/stone values; the client reads exactly this many | stack [S+0x4C] |
| `stone_id` | u16 | Socketed stone/option ids (the registry saver names these QuickSlotStone, 5 per item). Only indices 0..4 survive: index 5 is overwritten by block_tail, and index >=6 writes past the 12-byte block. | option block [S+0x224 + 2*i]; copied to entity+0x16E region |
| `block_tail` | u16 | Last u16 of the 12-byte item option block (meaning unknown; same trailer as S2C 0x19 and C2S 0x0F) | option block +10 = [S+0x22E] (6th u16 of the block) |

**Semantics.** Equip-change notice for any entity. The 12-byte item option block is u16[6] = 5 stones + tail, with the wire encoding u8 n, n*u16, u16 tail. The client looks up the item (must be Type 1 equipment) and the entity by uid, and aborts silently if either is missing. It writes item_id into the entity's equip grid at the slot derived from itemdef+0x1CC (kind) and +0x1F0 (alternate grid), stores the block, remembers the previously equipped item and its block, recomposes the sprite and recalculates stats. For remote players that is all. For the local player (uid == scene+0x220, bag slot count scene+0x3A9 <= 45): it removes the bag entry at scene+0x3C8/+0x422 that matches item_id AND the exact 12-byte block, and aborts if there is none. It then puts the previously equipped item (if any) with its block into the first empty bag slot, refreshes the inventory (window 9) and equipment (window 7) windows, and updates the game_state+0x700 lists for items with itemdef+0x1F0. On the current quickslot page, slots holding item_id with the same block are swapped to the old item and old block, and the quickslots are saved to HKCU\Software\Hamelin\WindSlayer\<name>. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C33, item_inventory#03/#05): 0x1D ITSELF removes one matching copy from the bag (this is the root cause of the "item equipped and still in the bag" reports when the option block does not match - and of double removal when the server also sends 0x23). The equip-tab removal COMPACTS the bag (later slots shift down) and the swapped-out item is appended to the first empty slot, i.e. the end of the list after compaction. EN Kind 11 (Wooden Stick, item 179) maps to equip grid index 5 = the Equipment window's Weapon & Shield slot 1.

**Trigger.** Send in response to C2S 0x0F EquipItem. The live capture 'B3 00 00 00 00' is u16 item 179 followed by the same block encoding (u8 0 stones, u16 tail 0), so echo the client's block. Also broadcast to other players so they see the change.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Gates: catalog entry must exist with +0x154==1; entity with uid must exist; the local bag/UI path needs uid==scene+0x220, scene+0x3A9<=45, and an existing bag entry with a byte-identical 12-byte block. If that match fails, the grid and sprite ARE already changed but the bag, windows and quickslots are not, so the item shows both equipped and still in the bag. If the bag is full the old item silently disappears client-side (the add result is ignored). There is no bound on stone_count: the wire stays aligned (exactly n u16 are consumed), but n==6 loses stone 6 to the tail and n>=7 writes past the block into stack [S+0x230..]. Those first 12 bytes get re-zeroed; n>=13 clobbers unrelated locals up to S+0x422, below the cookie at S+0x1304, so no crash is expected. Keep stone_count <= 5. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.

**References.** Our server's _build_en_opcode_1D_equip (windslayer_server.py ~2171) sends u32 uid \| u16 item \| u8 0 \| u16 0, which matches this grammar; it is sent from _handle_equip_item. That docstring says 0x1D 'does NOT touch the bag (+0xf84)', but +0xF84 is the item CATALOG. For the local player 0x1D DOES remove the item from the bag list at scene+0x3C8 when the block matches, which may double up with the follow-up 0x23. The unused _build_en_opcode_1D (~2143) is wrong for this handler: it sends class as item_id and N=14, which overflows the 12-byte block. The memory note in reference_combat_render.md ('keeps the item IN THE BAG') conflicts with this static reading unless the bag entry's block was non-zero or the local gate failed. KR Hex-Rays 0x1D (doc line 5035) parses a different item struct via sub_40A010, so it is not comparable byte-for-byte. The 5-stone naming comes from FUN_004411A0 'QuickSlotStone%d%d' (inner loop < 5).

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of block_tail (6th u16 of the option block): refine level, durability, or a flag?
- Exact meaning of itemdef+0x1F0 (selects an alternate equip grid index in FUN_00426680 and skips the block copy there, e.g. costume/cash items) and of the game_state+0x700 lists updated by FUN_0045D0C0/FUN_0045D170.
- [RESOLVED by live verification item_inventory#03, 2026-09-17] Live: 0x1D does remove the bag copy when item id AND the 12-byte option block match; the earlier "item stayed in the bag" report was a block mismatch. A server that sends 0x1D and then 0x23 removes TWO copies. Original question: "Why live testing reportedly left the item in the bag after 0x1D: bag block mismatch, or the scene+0x3A9 or uid gate?"
