| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target_uid` | u32 | uid of the entity that receives the buff; looked up in the scene entity list (entity+0x84). uid 0 or unknown uid ends processing | stack local [base+0x158]; passed as EDX to FUN_004189f0 (entity lookup) |
| `source_uid` | u32 | uid of whoever applied the buff. Goes to FUN_00424e20 param_6 and is stored at buff+0x14 (entity+0xe98+slot*0x18). 0 means the target buffed itself: the target's own uid is stored instead, and for item ids 0x9C3..0x9F9 the duration is forced to 60000 | stack local [base+0x1dc] -> entity buff slot +0xE98 |
| `item_id` | u16 | id of the buff-granting item (1-based index into the item table at scene+0xF84). The item's Duration (def+0x1C8, the tooltip 'Duration:' field) becomes the buff timer. Its stat modifiers are at def+0x1B8..0x1C4 | stack local [base+0x150] -> AX for FUN_00404210 / FUN_00424e20 -> entity+0xE84+slot*0x18 |

**Semantics.** Adds a timed buff, granted by an item, to an entity. Steps: (1) find the target entity by uid; if it is missing, stop. (2) Read item_id and look up the item definition in scene+0xF84 (FUN_00404210); if it is missing, stop. (3) If def+0x1C8 (Duration) != 0, call FUN_00424e20(scene, entity, duration, 0, 0, source_uid). That writes a 0x18-byte record into the entity's buff array at +0xE84 (21 slots). Some item-id ranges (0x8E7-0x912, 0x9C3-0x9F9, 0xA9F-0xAC9, 0xAE3-0xAF8, 0x1D4-0x1DE, 0xB1A-0xB24) replace a conflicting buff that is already present. Record fields: +0 id, +2 \|def+0x1DC\|, +0xC duration, +0x10 def+0x158, +0x14 source uid. It then shows buff icons for party members or the local player (FUN_004259c0). If any stat modifier def+0x1B8/0x1BC/0x1C0/0x1C4 is non-zero, stats are recalculated (FUN_0041ace0). (4) For 0x41 nothing else happens. Unlike 0x42, the local character-info stat panel is NOT refreshed.

**Trigger.** Server-side result of using a buff item (scroll, potion or anything else with a Duration) on self or on another entity, so everyone who can see the target shows the buff.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Needs target_uid to be a spawned entity (the u16 is not even read otherwise). Needs item_id to be a valid 1-based item-table index. The buff is only added if the item's Duration != 0. If all 21 buff slots are full or a stacking rule blocks it, FUN_00424e20 returns 0 without adding anything. No UI dialog. No crash hazard found: the reads are fixed-size. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C4, combat_skill#08, item_inventory#10/#11): THE CLIENT NEVER EXPIRES A BUFF. In field mode it decrements buff-slot +0xC every tick for type-3 AND type-4 entities, past 0 into negative values; the slot is never removed, stats are never recomputed and the icon merely blinks. The server MUST send S2C 0x43 (remove + stat recompute) or S2C 0x3C (icon only) when a Duration ends. Two more live facts: identical item buffs STACK as separate records and icons (no refresh/replace outside the listed id ranges), and a wire source_uid of 0 is stored as the TARGET's own uid, so the slot +0x14 value is not a literal copy of the wire field. The icon is the item's own icon, drawn bottom-right above the HUD buttons, one per record.

**References.** PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x42.py builds u32,u32,u16 (10 bytes), which matches the EN layout exactly (no callers). The newer KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 7132) reads u32,u32,u16 plus an extra u8, so KR has grown and EN has no trailing u8. Our server never sends 0x41 or 0x42.

**Open questions.**
- Duration unit: 60000 is forced for self-cast ids 0x9C3..0x9F9, which suggests milliseconds; not confirmed against the buff tick code.
- Which C2S item-use opcode makes the retail server answer with 0x41 instead of 0x42 was not traced.

(e.g. 'Concoction Successful.'). result 0 or 0x11: same material-removal loop, no product; 0x11 prefixes 'Out of empty slot in inventory\r\n '. result 0x0F / 0x10: prefix 'Short of material item\r\n ' / 'The skill hasn't been learned yet.\r\n ', no consumption. Every non-1 result appends kind + 'Failed.' via "%s%s" (no space, e.g. 'ConcoctionFailed.'). All non-early-exit paths: FUN_00465290 inventory refresh, FUN_0048A060 sets text in window 0x28F, FUN_00483430(0x28F,4,1), FUN_00483270(0x28F, product_item_id), FUN_004838C0(control 4, product record), then [ctx+0x2C]=0.

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x67 (u16 product_item_id), which FUN_004684d0 sends at 0x468726 when the 5000 ms progress window 0x293 completes for a Concoction/Refining request (reinforcement slots [ctx+0x64]/[ctx+0x66] not both filled). Send exactly once per 0x67.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler1 only runs when [ctx+0x8] and [ctx+0xC] are non-null. Unknown/zero product_item_id -> silent return without clearing [ctx+0x2C], leaving concoction/refining/reinforcement blocked ('Not allowed during concoction, mineral refining, or reinforcement.'). Client mutates inventory LOCALLY from its own item data (materials removed on results 1, 0 and 0x11; product +1 on result 1); server must apply the identical change and must not send extra add/remove packets for the same craft or inventory double-counts. Equipment-category materials remove only 1 instance each regardless of recipe count.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts read exactly the same wire layout - u8 result at 0x46EA2A (IAT 0x4A4094, out [ESP+0x18]-12 = [ESP+0xC]) and u16 product_item_id at 0x46EA3E (IAT 0x4A4090, out [ESP+0x28]-12 = [ESP+0x1C]) - and no other GetDataFromPacket call exists between 0x46EA44 and the shared exit at 0x46EF5A. The only 'dispute' is A's trailing unconditional 'stop', which is redundant (stop is for terminating a branch); B's plain 'u8 u16' is the canonical form. Wire length 3 on every path; both correct on bytes. Extra detail verified here: the "%s%s" format at 0x4A630C and ' Successful.' (0x6F5958, leading space) / 'Failed.' (0x6F5950, no space) give 'Concoction Successful.' vs 'ConcoctionFailed.'; FUN_00467140 NEGs the count (0x46717A/0x4671E4) and uses -1 for equipment materials (0x4671AF). Not in PySlayer (only a try-import stub for opcode_0x8D) and our server has no 0x8D builder or 0x67 handler (grep of windslayer_server.py finds none).

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of item record +0x224 values other than 2 (all non-2 display 'Concoction').
- Whether the original server consumed materials on result 0x11 (client does it locally, so server should mirror).
- Semantics of FUN_00440920 arg2 (passed 0) - UI/inventory detail, not wire format.

### S2C 0x8E — ReinforceResult (equipment reinforcement with elemental stone)

*server → client* · key `0x8E` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **missing** · length: 5 if equip_item_id is unknown to the client or result != 1; 19 if result == 1 (1+2+2+12+2)

u16 equip_item_id

  stop
}
if(result == 1) {
  repeat(6) { u16 equip_option }
  u16 new_option_item_id
}
```

| `result` | u8 | 1 = success (the option block follows); 0x11 = 'This equipment cannot be reinforced.'; any other value = 'ReinforcementFailed.'. No local inventory change on any failure. | stack local [ESP+0xC] |
| `equip_item_id` | u16 | Item id of the equipment being reinforced (echo of first u16 of C2S 0x68 = [ctx+0x66]). If not in the client item table the handler stops after these 5 bytes. | stack local [ESP+0x10]; item-table lookup; FUN_004241d0 arg; window 0x29B +0x134 (success) / FUN_00483270(0x29B,id) (fa… |
| `stone_item_id` | u16 | Item id of the elemental stone (echo of second u16 of C2S 0x68 = [ctx+0x64]); on success 1 unit is removed from the stackable tab (ids inv+0x760, u8 counts inv+0x7BA). | stack local [ESP+0x28]; FUN_00423e70 arg on success |
| `equip_option` | u16 x6 (12 bytes) | The equipment instance's CURRENT 6 option words before reinforcement (echo of the 6 u16 sent in C2S 0x68). Only used to locate the exact inventory slot. Present only when result == 1. | zero-initialized stack buffer [ESP+0x34..0x3F]; FUN_004241d0 arg (compared 12 bytes via FUN_00427390 against inv+0x3DA+… |
| `new_option_item_id` | u16 | Option value (must be a valid item-table id) written into the first zero word among option[0..4] of the matched slot. If it does not resolve in the item table the client takes the failure path ('ReinforcementFailed.'). Present only when result == 1. | stack local [ESP+0x14]; FUN_004241d0 arg; window 0x29B +0x40; its record shown in control 6 |

**Semantics.** Result of reinforcing equipment with an elemental stone. Reads u8 result, u16 equip_item_id, u16 stone_item_id; looks up equip_item_id (FUN_00404210) and returns silently if missing (no further reads, [ctx+0x2C] not cleared). If result != 1 -> failure path with no further reads. If result == 1: reads 6 u16 option words then u16 new_option_item_id; if new_option_item_id is not a valid item -> failure path. Otherwise FUN_004241d0 scans equipment-tab slots (count u8 inv+0x361, ids u16 inv+0x380, 12-byte option blocks inv+0x3DA) for id == equip_item_id AND option block == the 12 received bytes, and stores new_option_item_id in the first zero word among option[0..4] (no change if no slot matches or all five are non-zero; success is still shown). Then FUN_00423e70 removes 1 x stone_item_id from the etc tab. Text 'Reinforcement Successful.' ("%s%s" with ' Successful.') into window 0x29B (FUN_0048A060); FUN_00465290 inventory refresh; clears list entries 4 and 5 of window 0x29B (entry+0x18=0); FUN_00483430(0x29B,4,1); window object +0x134 = equip_item_id, +0x40 = new_option_item_id; FUN_004838C0 control 4 = equip record, control 6 = new option record; [ctx+0x2C]=0. Failure path (0x46EEBB): 'This equipment cannot be reinforced.' (result 0x11) or 'ReinforcementFailed.' (no space) into window 0x29B; FUN_00489320(0x29B,5,3) and (0x29B,6,3); FUN_00483430(0x29B,4,1); FUN_00483270(0x29B, equip_item_id); FUN_004838C0 control 4 = equip record; [ctx+0x2C]=0; no inventory change.

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x68 (u16 equip_item_id, u16 stone_item_id, 6x u16 option words), sent by FUN_004684d0 at 0x46869D when the 5000 ms progress window 0x293 completes with both the equipment ([ctx+0x66]) and elemental stone ([ctx+0x64]) slots filled. Send exactly once per 0x68.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler1 requires [ctx+0x8] and [ctx+0xC] non-null. Unknown equip_item_id -> stops after 5 bytes and never clears [ctx+0x2C], leaving crafting/reinforcement UI locked. With result == 1 the packet must carry all 19 bytes; the upper halves of the [ESP+0x10]/[ESP+0x14] dword slots are uninitialized, and a short packet leaves new_option_item_id garbage. The 6 option words must byte-match the client's stored 12-byte block or the option is silently not applied while the stone is still removed (desync). Client consumes exactly 1 stone locally on success only; server must not send an extra stone-removal packet. Trailing option bytes on a result != 1 packet are simply unread.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: A's grammar 'if(result == 1 && item_table_has(equip_item_id)) { repeat(6){u16} u16 } else { stop }' and B's grammar 'if(item_db[equip]==null){stop} if(result==1){repeat(6){u16} u16}' produce the identical byte layout on every path; there is no wire disagreement. The asm order shows the item-table gate comes first (lookup at 0x46EC81, JZ 0x46EF5A exit) and only then CMP [ESP+0xC],1 / JNZ 0x46EEBB (0x46EC92/0x46EC97), with the 6-word loop at 0x46ECC0-0x46ECDB and final u16 at 0x46ECEE; the failure block 0x46EEBB..0x46EF5A contains no reads. B's two-step structure mirrors this code order, so it is adopted as canonical (A's combined condition is logically equivalent). Minor text corrections from the binary: format 0x4A630C = "%s%s", ' Successful.' at 0x6F5958 has a leading space and 'Failed.' at 0x6F5950 does not, so success text is 'Reinforcement Successful.' (B's semantics wrote 'ReinforcementSuccessful.') and failure text is 'ReinforcementFailed.' (B's field text wrote 'Reinforcement Failed.'); A had both right. C2S 0x68 layout confirmed at 0x46869D-0x4686E8 (u8 0x68, u16 [EDI+0x66], u16 [EDI+0x64], 6x u16). FUN_004241d0 decomp confirms insertion only into option[0..4]. Not in PySlayer (try-import stub only) nor our server (no 0x8E/0x68 in windslayer_server.py).

**Open questions.**
- Whether the original server set new_option_item_id equal to stone_item_id or to a derived id; the client only requires it to exist in the item table.
- Meaning of option word index 5 (never written by FUN_004241d0).
- Which S2C inventory packet seeds the 12-byte option blocks at inventory +0x3DA, so the server echoes consistent values.
- Whether the original server consumed the stone on failure (client does not remove it locally).

```
u8 result
u16 tool_item_id
if(item_def(tool_item_id) == null) {
  stop
} else {
  if(result == 1) {
    u16 reward_item_id
  } else {
    stop
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | 1 = success (reward_item_id follows); 0x11 = inventory full; any other value = generic failure ('Failed to obtian item.') | stack local [base+0x1C]; compared at 0x46E96C and 0x46E9C3 |
| `tool_item_id` | u16 | The gathering tool used. It should echo the u16 from C2S 0x69: 0x8A7..0x8AA are garden shovels (Herb Gathering), 0x8AB..0x8AE are shovels (Mining). The client removes 1 of it whenever the id has an item def, even if the gather failed. | stack local [base+0x18]; FUN_00404210 lookup, then FUN_00467140(id, NULL, 1) |
| `reward_item_id` | u16 | Item granted on success (count 1, no options). Read only when the tool's item def exists and result == 1. | stack local [base+0x0C]; FUN_00440920(game_state=[ctx+0x8], id, NULL, 1) |

**Semantics.** Result of a Mining or Herb Gathering action. The client reads result (u8) and tool_item_id (u16), then looks up the tool's item def with FUN_00404210. If there is no def (id 0 or out of range included), it only clears the gather busy flag [ctx+0x28] and returns: no message, no inventory refresh, no more reads. Otherwise it always removes 1 of tool_item_id from the local inventory (FUN_00467140, tab chosen by def+0x154) before it looks at result. If result == 1: it reads reward_item_id, adds 1 of it via FUN_00440920 (chat message "you've received %s. (Count:%u)", or "You've learned skill(%s)." for skill-book items), refreshes the inventory/quest UI (FUN_00465290), clears [ctx+0x28] and returns. If result == 0x11: message "There isn't empty space \r\nin the inventory.". Any other result: message "Failed to obtian item.". Both failure paths then refresh the inventory UI and clear [ctx+0x28].

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x69. FUN_004684D0 sends 0x69 once the 5000 ms progress bar of window 0x295 finishes. The window is opened by FUN_00467B00 when the player uses a garden shovel (0x8A7..0x8AA) on a herb node or a shovel (0x8AB..0x8AE) on a mineral node. 0x69 carries u32 node key (roster index, stored in window+0x11C at 0x467D4B) and u16 tool item id (stored in window+0x134 at 0x467D3F).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler1 gate: [ctx+0x8] != 0 and [ctx+0xC] != 0, otherwise the packet goes unhandled. While [ctx+0x28] != 0, FUN_00467B00 returns at once (0x467B1E), so no new gather can start until 0x8F clears it. A UI event for window 0x295 in FUN_00446300 also clears it ([game_state+0xD84] = 0 at 0x446A2A). The client removes the tool on failure too (any result, as long as the def exists), so the server must also remove it on failure, or resend the tool, or the inventories drift apart. Send reward_item_id only when result == 1. On any other path the packet is 3 bytes, and extra bytes are ignored anyway. A tool_item_id with no item def skips the removal, the messages and the UI refresh; only the flag is cleared.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: A's grammar was 'u8 result; u16 tool_item_id; if(item_def != null && result == 1) { u16 reward_item_id }'. B's was the same reads nested as if(def exists) { if(result == 1) { u16 } else stop } else stop. Both describe the same bytes in the same order, and the asm agrees with both. Reads: 0x46E91D u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) into [base+0x1C]; 0x46E931 u16 (0x4A4090) into [base+0x18]; 0x46E945 FUN_00404210 then JZ 0x46E9F9, which only clears [EBX+0x28] and returns; 0x46E963 FUN_00467140 removes the item unconditionally (stdcall RET 0xC, so the later [ESP+0x1C] still points at result); 0x46E96C CMP AL,1 / JNZ 0x46E9C3; 0x46E981 is the only other read, u16 (0x4A4090) into [base+0x0C]. None of the callees (FUN_00404210, FUN_00467140, FUN_00440920, FUN_00465290) receive the packet pointer or offset, so there are no hidden reads. B's nested form is kept because it follows the branch order in the code. On meaning, A was right that the u16 is the tool: FUN_00467B00 takes the used item id in [EBP+0x10], accepts only 0x8A7..0x8AA (garden shovel, Herb Gathering: entity+0x644 == 2, skill 0x56, map check 0x138) or 0x8AB..0x8AE (shovel, Mining: entity+0x644 == 1, skill 0x52, map check 0x139), stores it in window 0x295 +0x134 (FUN_00483270 at 0x467D3F), and FUN_004684D0 sends that same value as the u16 of C2S 0x69 (0x468584 / 0x4685A7). That settles B's tool-or-material question, and it covers both gathering types, so the name GatherResult is used rather than ItemMiningResult. The 5 s timer is confirmed: float 0x4A67AC = 5000.0. Other strings: 0x6F7FEC, 0x6F7538; 'Mining' 0x6F5F24, 'Item ' 0x6F5F3C, 'Herb Gathering' 0x6F5F2C. FUN_00440920 is the same add-item helper used by other reward packets (for example the S2C 0x18 quest reward). Neither PySlayer nor our server has this opcode.

**Open questions.**
- Result codes other than 1 and 0x11 all show the same generic failure message. The client does not show which codes the original server actually used.
- The client does not check that tool_item_id in 0x8F matches the id sent in C2S 0x69. It removes whatever id the server sends, so the server should echo the tool id it received.
- Not confirmed whether the programmatic close of window 0x295 in FUN_004684D0 (FUN_00483430 at 0x4685CB) reaches the FUN_00446300 path that clears [game_state+0xD84]. If it does not, a missing 0x8F leaves gathering blocked until the player closes the window by hand or the flag is otherwise reset.

### S2C 0x9C — ElementalStoneExtractResult

*server → client* · key `0x9C` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **missing** · length: 21 when result == 1 (1+2+10+2+2+4); 1 otherwise

Locations: `0x00462CDC` handler block (opcode 0x9C case); `0x00462CEA` u8 result (IAT 0x4A4094) -> [esp+0x13]; CMP 1 / JNZ 0x462E11 failure; `0x00462D09` u16 equip_item_id -> [esp+0x1c]; `0x00462D15` zero 12-byte record buffer [esp+0x30..0x3b]

```
u8 result
if(result == 1) {
  u16 equip_item_id
  repeat(5) { u16 socket_stone }
  u16 socket_extra
  u16 stone_id
  u32 cash_item_serial
} else {
  stop
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | 1 = extraction succeeded; any other value = failure modal and stop | stack [esp+0x13] |
| `equip_item_id` | u16 | item id of the equipment; matched against u16 array ci+0x380[i] for i < byte ci+0x361 | stack [esp+0x1c] -> FUN_00424260 arg3 |
| `socket_stone[0..4]` | u16 x5 | stone ids currently in sockets 0..4 of that equipment (words 0-4 of its 12-byte record, BEFORE extraction); read in a 5-iteration loop | stack buffer [esp+0x30],[esp+0x32],[esp+0x34],[esp+0x36],[esp+0x38] |
| `socket_extra` | u16 | 6th word of the 12-byte record (not a stone socket; only used for the exact 12-byte identity compare) | stack buffer [esp+0x3a] |
| `stone_id` | u16 | stone id to remove from sockets 0..4. 0 = client removes socket index rand() % (number of non-empty sockets) | stack [esp+0x24] -> FUN_00424260 arg5 |
| `cash_item_serial` | u32 | key (record +0x00) of the premium-inventory record (extraction tool) to consume, count 1 | stack [esp+0x28] -> FUN_00464380(ctx, serial, 1, NULL) |

**Semantics.** Result of an elemental stone extraction. On result == 1: builds a 12-byte record from the 6 u16 words and calls FUN_00424260. That picks the FIRST slot i < byte ci+0x361 whose u16 id at ci+0x380[i] == equip_item_id AND whose 12-byte record at ci+0x3DA+i*12 is byte-identical to the packet record. If stone_id != 0, it zeroes the first of sockets 0..4 equal to stone_id (not found: no change). If stone_id == 0, it zeroes socket index rand() % count_nonzero; that is a filled socket only while stones are packed from socket 0. If the removed value is nonzero, the remaining stones are shifted toward socket 0. The removed stone id is returned but discarded; the stone is NOT added to the inventory by this packet. Then FUN_00465290 rebuilds the inventory UI, cash_item_serial is consumed (count 1) and the modal 'Extracted elemental stone.' is shown. Otherwise the modal 'Elemental stone extraction failed. \r\n\r\nPlease try again in a few minutes.' is shown and nothing more is read. Returns 1.

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x72 sent from extraction window 0x473 (FUN_00469090 at 0x46C066..0x46C0B8): u8 0x72, u16 tool item id (window slot; tools 0xF70 and 0xD6D require a selected stone, else 'Select the elemental stone to extract.'), u16 equipment item id ([win+0x66], else 'Place your equipment'), u16 selected stone id, 6x u16 from equipment record +2. The server can echo equip id and the 6 words byte-exact, and must replace stone 0 with the stone it actually removed.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler4 does not parse unless ctx+0x14 and ctx+0x18 are non-null. result must be exactly 1. CRASH: stone_id == 0 while the matched slot's sockets 0..4 are all empty -> IDIV by zero at 0x42430D. DESYNC: stone_id == 0 lets the client pick a random socket on its own; always send the real nonzero id. If equip_item_id plus the 6 words do not exactly match the client's stored record (or the slot index >= byte ci+0x361), no socket changes, but the tool is still consumed and the success modal still shows. The extracted stone must be delivered by a separate item-add packet.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire format: u8 result; if result == 1 then u16 equip id, six u16 record words, u16 stone id, u32 cash serial; else stop. The signature difference is only notation (A listed six u16 lines, B wrote repeat(6)). Neither exactly matches the code's shape, which is a 5-iteration loop plus one separate read; the grammar above mirrors that, and the bytes are identical. VA evidence: u8 [0x4A4094] at 0x462CEA -> [esp+0x13] with CMP 1 / JNZ 0x462E11; u16 at 0x462D09 -> [esp+0x1c]; loop counter [esp+0x14]=5 at 0x462D2B with u16 read at 0x462D41, ADD ptr 2, SUB/JNZ at 0x462D4C/0x462D51; separate u16 at 0x462D69 -> [esp+0x3a]; u16 at 0x462D7D -> [esp+0x24]; FUN_00424260 at 0x462DA6; u32 [0x4A40C8] at 0x462DCB -> [esp+0x28]; FUN_00464380(ctx, serial, 1, 0) at 0x462DDB. A's divide-by-zero crash is confirmed (the EBX count at 0x4242CB..0x424304, then IDIV EBX at 0x42430D). One correction to both: the random path zeroes index rand()%count, not a guaranteed non-empty socket, and shifting is skipped when the zeroed value was 0 (TEST AX,AX at 0x42435E). The C2S 0x72 layout both cited is confirmed at 0x46C066..0x46C0B8. For game_system, A's 'item' was chosen because the main effect is changing equipment sockets; B's 'premium_cash' also fits, since a cash tool is consumed. Not in PySlayer or our server. The record layout matches the FUN_00465290 12-byte copy from ci+0x3DA+i*12.

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of socket_extra (record word 5) is unconfirmed; it is only used in the identity compare.
- Which S2C packet delivers the extracted stone into the inventory is unknown.
- Behaviour of tools other than 0xF70/0xD6D (which allow stone 0 = random) was not enumerated.

### C2S 0x21 — TradeRequestAccept

*client → server* · key `0x469C33/0x21` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 17

Locations: `0x469C33` Send(1); `0x469BCA` dialog 0x70 case (outer jump table); only event 3 is handled; `0x469BF1` FUN_00483120(dialog 0x70, control 1) -> label, text at +0x50; `0x469C05` strcpy of the label into a zeroed 17-byte stack buffer

```
str[17] requester_name
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requester_name` | str[17] | name of the player who asked to trade, echoed back (NUL padded) | label text of dialog 0x70 control 1, which S2C 0x45 set from its str[17] name |

**Semantics.** Accepts an incoming trade request. The requester sends C2S 0x20 (u32 target uid), and the server shows the target a popup via S2C 0x45 (requester name). Clicking OK on that popup sends this packet with the requester's name so the server can open the trade for both players.

**Trigger.** Event 3 (OK/accept button) on popup dialog 0x70, which S2C 0x45 opened.

**Expected response.** S2C 0x46 (str[17] partner name; opens trade window 0x4E and resets its buttons) or S2C 0x47 u8 status (6 = "Trading.", 4 = "The player is rejecting trade.").

**Gates / hazards.** No preconditions beyond the dialog event. Hazard: the copy is an unbounded strcpy from the label (up to 0x81 bytes) into a 17-byte stack buffer. The S2C 0x45 name must be NUL-terminated within 16 chars, or the client overflows the stack. If control 1 is missing, strcpy reads from NULL and the client crashes. No decline packet is built in this function.

**Trigger.** The player drags an item from the Inventory window (UI window id 9) and drops it on the Trade window (window id 0x4E) while a trade is open. Stacking items (catalog type 0 or 2) do not send from here: they open the quantity dialog (UI 0x74, default value = rec+0x0E), and on OK FUN_00469090 sends the same opcode from send site #66 (Send at 0x469D9C, Adds at 0x469F27..0x469F4F) as: u16 item_id, u16 entered_qty, u8 0, u16 0.

When owner_uid == local uid (char+0x1D8 = scene+0x220), the client takes the item out of its bag (0x467140) and adds it to its own trade grid (0x489A80, window 0x4E). Hazards: the client keeps no pending state, so repeated drags of the same item send duplicate 0x22s. The server must check ownership, the 12-slot limit, the no-trade flag and that a trade session is active. The receiver must zero-fill enchant words >= enchant_count. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.

**References.** Our server: _dispatch (windslayer_server.py ~line 602) has no inbound 0x22 handler. Outbound 0x22 in our server is S2C SetLevel, a different direction and meaning. PySlayer: no client_packets parser for 0x22. The trailing layout (u8 n, n x u16, u16) is the same as C2S 0x0F equip (builder 0x44C2C0, captured payload 'B3 00 00 00 00') and C2S 0x11, and it mirrors S2C 0x4B, which reads exactly these fields plus a u32 owner uid after qty.

**Open questions.**
- What the 6 attribute words at rec+0x02..+0x0D mean in-game (enchant, socket, option?). Our server calls this the enchant region (entity +0x16E).
- What exactly Trade window sub-controls #2 and #3 (FUN_00489090 ESI=0x4E, index 3 and 2, returns control+0x1C) represent. Probably the trade-lock or confirm button state; S2C 0x48 changes control 3 via 0x489020.
- Whether the retail server also sent the owner a separate bag-removal packet, or relied only on 0x4B (0x4B's owner path already calls 0x467140 to remove the item from the bag).

| `stall_owner_uid` | u32 | Unique id of the player whose open item stall the user wants to browse | clicked entity +0x84 (uid) of a remote player (entity+0x98 == 3, uid != scene+0x220) |

**Semantics.** Asks the server to open another player's item stall for browsing. The client changes no state on send. S2C 0x86 clears it with 'The shop is closed or adjusting.'. 0x61 is sent only while that flag is set.

**Trigger.** Left mouse button release (WM_LBUTTONUP 0x202) in field mode (scene+0xF00 == 6) over another player whose stall is open (entity+0xE2 == 0, entity+0x14F4 != 0). Screen anchor: sx = ent+0x15A4 - cam(game_state+0x1044) + 400 + edge_adj, sy = ent+0x15A8 - cam(+0x1048) + 0x102 + edge_adj. The hit counts when the mouse (game_state+0x3FC/+0x400) is within dist^2 < 0xA28 of (sx,sy), or inside the stall-sign box sx-0x67 < mx < sx+0x67 and sy-0x6E < my < sy-0x50. Entities with +0xE2 != 0 are room/portal objects that open the 'Enter the arena?' / 'Would you enter the play room?' / 'Enter the cash shop?' (0x81) dialogs instead. Also: entity+0x14F4 != 0; FUN_00466df0(game_state+0xD5C) == 0 and FUN_00466e10 == 0 (no own stall / stall browse session active in stall manager id 0x259, flags +0xD7C/+0xD78); FUN_00468fa0 == 0 (no trade window 0x28C in state 3 / blocking modal). Hovering sets the cursor (ui_root+0x10 = 0x48). No pending lock, so repeated clicks resend.

UI strings confirm EN terminology 'Item stall' / 'Open stall'.

Live geometry: the window opens centred at (250,205)-(565,410).

Must be sent before every new trade because it is the only place [ctx+0x24] is reset; otherwise a stale partner-confirmed flag can open the final window too early on the next 0x48.

| `gold` | u64 | Gold the confirming party offers. Shown (formatted with %I64u) in trade window 0x4E control 0x1F only when confirmer_uid is NOT the local player. Ignored in the self branch. | local [ESP+0x48] (low) / [ESP+0x4C] (high) -> FUN_004659d0 -> window 0x4E control 0x1F label |

**Semantics.** A party locked in their side of the trade. Self branch (confirmer_uid == my uid): set trade window 0x4E control 3 (confirm button) state=0 and set +0x18=1 (greyed/locked) on each record in my offered-items list (0x4E+0xB0). Gold is ignored. Partner branch: write gold as a decimal string into 0x4E control 0x1F, set the partner-confirmed flag [ctx+0x24]=1, and grey out each record in the partner list (0x4E+0xC0). Then, on either branch: if my confirm button state (0x4E ctrl 3 +0x1C) is 0 AND [ctx+0x24]!=0, both sides are locked. The client then copies every 0x38-byte item record from 0x4E into the final-confirmation window 0x291 (partner +0xC0 -> 0x291 +0xBC/+0xC0 list, mine +0xB0 -> 0x291 +0xAC/+0xB0 list). It sets 0x291 control 0x1D to my gold edit text (0x4E ctrl 0x1E) and 0x291 control 0x1E to the partner gold label (0x4E ctrl 0x1F), shows window 0x291 and hides window 0x4E. Returns 1 on all paths. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, trade#12): the EN caption of window 0x291 is "Comfirming Trade" [sic]; its list headers are "Items to Send" / "Items to Receive" and ctrl 3 is labelled "Trade". The wire behaviour (self echo greys the own list, partner echo opens 0x291 and hides 0x4E) matched the spec exactly.

**Trigger.** On C2S 0x23 {u64 gold} from a party, the server should send 0x48 {that party's uid, gold} to BOTH parties. The self echo is required: the second confirmer's final window only opens on its own echo, because its [ctx+0x24] was set earlier by the partner's 0x48. The first confirmer's final window opens when the partner's 0x48 arrives, because the client already zeroed its button 3 before sending 0x23.

**Expected response.** When the final window 0x291 opens, OK (button 3) sends C2S 0x25: u64 my_gold (0x291 ctrl 0x1D), u8 my_item_count, repeat(my_item_count){u16 item_id(+0x0) u16 rec_0E u8 opt_count(0..5, count of leading non-zero u16 at +0x2..) repeat(opt_count){u16 opt} u16 rec_0C}, then u64 partner_gold (ctrl 0x1E), u8 partner_item_count, repeat{same record}. Buttons 2/4 send C2S 0x24 (cancel). The server then presumably answers with S2C 0x4A ("Trade completed.") or 0x49.

**Gates / hazards.** Shared sub1 gate. confirmer_uid must exactly equal the uid the client registered for its own player, or the self echo is treated as the partner (it would overwrite the partner gold label and set the partner flag). [ctx+0x24] is only cleared by S2C 0x46, so always start trades with 0x46. In the both-confirmed path, if window 0x4E has fewer than 0x1E/0x1F child controls, EDI stays 0 and FUN_004838c0 strcpy's from NULL and crashes (not expected with stock UI data). FUN_00489090 dereferences [0+0x1C] if 0x4E's child list is shorter than 3.

**References.** Not implemented in our server or PySlayer. NOTE: our server's _dispatch treats C2S 0x25 as 'UseSkill (u16 skill)' and echoes a cast. In this EN client the ONLY C2S 0x25 send site is the trade final-accept in window 0x291 (FUN_00469090 @0x46A99C), so that handler would misfire on a trade accept. 'You are short of gold.' (0x469CAD) checks the 0x23 gold against money at [ctx+0x18]+0x228 (the same u64 that S2C 0x18/0x19 update).

**Open questions.**
- What item record fields +0x0C and +0x0E are (likely durability/count, and count/flag). They are only echoed in C2S 0x25 and passed to FUN_00467200 on cancel.
- Confirm [ctx+0x18] == scene+0x48 (so +0x1D8 == scene+0x220). Supported by two independent offset pairs (uid and manner points, both delta 0x48) but not proven by a direct write.

### S2C 0x49 — TradeCanceled

*server → client* · key `0x49` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **missing** · length: 0

Locations: `0x0046E465` handler block start (sub1 case 0x49). The block runs to RET 0x10 at 0x0046E53F and makes …; `0x0046E470` FUN_004817d0(ui, "Trade has been canceled." @0x6F501C, colour 0xFFFD4C87): system message; `0x0046E47E` FUN_00483430(0x4E,1,1) calls FUN_00446300(win=0x4E,0,1,0,param_6=1): hides the trade wind…; `0x0046E48F` FUN_00483430(0x291,1,1): hides the final-confirm window

```
stop
```

**Semantics.** The packet has no payload: the handler never reads from the packet, so any trailing bytes are ignored. Steps: (1) Posts the system message "Trade has been canceled." (colour 0xFFFD4C87). (2) Hides trade window 0x4E and final-confirm window 0x291 through FUN_00483430(id,1,1). That becomes FUN_00446300(..., param_6=1), which only hides the windows (FUN_004835b0) and sends nothing. (3) If window 0x4E exists and the list of items I offered (list object at +0xAC, count/head at +0xB0) is not empty, it pops records until the list is empty. Each record is 0x38 bytes, allocated by the self branch of S2C 0x4B. The handler uses rec+0x0 = u16 item_id, rec+0x2 = 12 option bytes and rec+0xE = u16 (count/durability-like). It looks up the item definition through FUN_00404210 in [[ctx+0x10]+0xF84]. If found, FUN_00467200 restores the item by category = def+0x154. Category 0: FUN_00423b70(bag+0x5F6, bag+0x650, bag+0x6AC, id, byte bag+0x362, 0,0,0) with ECX=rec+0xE. Category 1: writes the id into the first zero u16 slot of bag+0x380 (slot count = byte bag+0x361, must be <= 0x2D) and copies the 12 bytes from rec+2 to bag+0x3DA+slot*12; rec+0xE is not used. Category 2: FUN_00423e70(bag+0x760, id, byte bag+0x363) with ESI=bag+0x7BA and EAX=rec+0xE. Here bag = [ctx+0x18]. On success the inventory UI refreshes (FUN_00465290). The record is freed either way. (4) Returns 1. The partner's offered-items list (object at +0xBC, head at +0xC0) is not touched.

**Trigger.** Send to both trade parties when either side cancels (C2S 0x24), and by server policy when a party disconnects or leaves the field mid-trade or when final validation fails.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Shared sub1 gate only. Safe to send with no trade open: the windows are simply hidden and the restore loop is skipped when window 0x4E is missing or its list is empty. The client restores offered items to its bag locally, because it removed them when S2C 0x4B (self branch, FUN_00467140) added them to the trade. The server's inventory model must still treat those items as owned. If the item definition is not found, or category 1 has no free slot (or its slot count is over 0x2D), the record is freed without a restore and the client bag loses the item until the next resync. Hiding the windows does NOT send C2S 0x24, so there is no echo loop.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree the payload is empty (length 0, no fields). A wrote grammar "" and B wrote "stop". This is a difference in notation, not in wire format. The asm from 0x0046E465 to the RET 0x10 at 0x0046E53F has no CALL through any GetDataFromPacket IAT slot (0x4A4090/94/98/C8/CC/D0/D4/B0/118). None of the callees (FUN_004817d0, FUN_00483430, FUN_004830f0, FUN_00459e60, FUN_00404210, FUN_00467200, FUN_00465290) receives the packet pointer (EDI is overwritten at 0x0046E4A1) or the offset (EBP+0x10). The first packet read after this point belongs to the 0x4B block at 0x0046E550. The canonical grammar is "stop", meaning zero bytes are read. Two semantic details were checked in FUN_00467200's asm. (a) Category mapping: A was right and B was wrong. Category 0 goes to FUN_00423b70 (0x004672C9..F2), category 1 to the u16 slot array at +0x380 plus 12 option bytes at +0x3DA (0x00467249..C6), and category 2 to FUN_00423e70 at +0x760 (0x00467223..3F). B's claim that category 1 is equipment and category 2 is stackable does not match that dispatch. (b) The u16 at rec+0xE is the second stack argument (MOV SI,[ESP+0x10] at 0x0046720A). It is used by categories 0 and 2 and ignored by category 1. B mentioned it as a count and A left it out. List offsets: both are consistent. My-items list object is at +0xAC with head/count at +0xB0 (0x0046E4AF/0x0046E4C0). The partner list object is at +0xBC (0x0046E702 in 0x4B) with head at +0xC0 (0x0046E832 in 0x4A). The record size 0x38 is confirmed by PUSH 0x38/FUN_0048b484 at 0x0046E653. A's claim that the windows close without re-sending C2S 0x24 is confirmed: in FUN_00446300, case 0x4E re-enters only when param_6==2, and caseD_2 exits after FUN_004835b0 when param_6==1. Neither PySlayer nor our server implements this opcode. The companion opcode 0x4A ("Trade completed.", u64 money into [ctx+0x18]+0x228 at 0x0046E7FB) is outside this batch.

**Open questions.**
- Whether the original server also sent explicit inventory resync packets after 0x49, or relied only on this client-side restore (server policy, not visible in the client).
- What exactly the u16 at rec+0xE means (count vs durability) for categories 0 and 2. It comes from the S2C 0x4B payload, which is outside this batch.
- Where the partner list at +0xBC/+0xC0 is cleared. It is not cleared in this handler, and the 0x46 block does not visibly clear it either (it may happen inside FUN_0047d700 on window open).

| `opt_extra` | u16 | Sixth option word, always present (option block +0x0A; PySlayer writes a non-enchant value here, exact meaning unconfirmed) | [esp+0x52] -> struct +0x0C |

**Semantics.** Trade window item-added notification. All six option words form a 12-byte block (slots opt_count..4 stay zero). If owner_uid == local player's uid: look up item_id in the item DB (null -> silently ignored); call FUN_00467140(item_id, &opts12, count) which REMOVES count of that item from the local inventory (stackables by count; equipment by exact item_id + 12-byte option memcmp in slots +0x380/+0x3DA); on success allocate a 0x38-byte struct {u16 id @0, 6xu16 opts @2, u16 count @0xE} and append it to the OWN list of trade window 0x4E (window+0xAC, head +0xB0, count +0xB8), then FUN_00465290 refreshes the inventory UI. Otherwise (partner's item): if trade window 0x4E exists, append the same struct to the PARTNER list (window+0xBC, head +0xC0); no item-DB validation. These partner structs are what 0x4A later adds to the inventory.

**Trigger.** Server echo of C2S 0x22 (trade add item: u16 item_id, u16 count, u8 n, n*u16 opts, u16 extra; client blocks locally when own list already has 12 entries). Send to BOTH traders: to the offerer with owner_uid = offerer uid (this is what actually removes the item from their inventory client-side) and to the partner with the offerer's uid.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Function-level gate: [ctx+8] (game_state) and [ctx+0xC] (UI root) must be non-null or the packet is unhandled and falls through to SubHandler2. opt_count > 5 overflows the 12-byte stack option buffer (index 5 is overwritten by opt_extra; >=7 corrupts neighbouring locals; >=59 reaches the /GS cookie at frame+0xB0 -> fatal __security_check_cookie crash). Self path: if the option words don't exactly match the inventory copy of an equipment item, removal fails and the item never appears in the trade window (desync). Self path does not require the window to be open for the inventory removal, but FUN_00489A80 silently drops (leaks) the struct if window 0x4E isn't open -> item vanishes from inventory with no trade entry. Partner path requires window 0x4E open. Always returns handled (EAX=1).

**References.** Not present in PySlayer (no trade opcodes) or windslayer_server.py. The item layout (u16 id, u8 n<=5, n*u16, u16 extra) matches PySlayer opcode_0x03 inventory equipment entries and the EN C2S 0x22 builder at 0x46C62C, with u16 count and u32 owner_uid inserted after the id.

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of opt_extra (sixth option word) is unconfirmed.
- Whether the server must also validate opt words vs its own DB; client only uses them for its local equipment removal match.

I use "stop" because it states outright that nothing is read, while an empty grammar looks the same as a missing one. The string at 0x6F5038 is used only by SubHandler1. ### S2C 0x14 — SetBaseStat

*server → client* · key `0x14` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **partial** · length: 7 (fixed)

Locations: `0x0045478A` handler block entry (opcode 0x14); `0x0045479F` GetDataFromPacket u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8) -> [ESP+0xD4]; `0x004547BA` GetDataFromPacket u8 stat_index (IAT 0x4A4094) -> [ESP+0x7C]; `0x004547D2` GetDataFromPacket u16 value (IAT 0x4A4090) -> [ESP+0x64]

```
u32 uid
u8 stat_index
u16 value
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | uid (entity+0x84) of the entity whose allocated base stat is set | stack [ESP+0xD4] (IAT 0x4A40C8); entity lookup key, compared to party frame +0x134 and scene+0x220 |
| `stat_index` | u8 | 0=Strength (+0xE6), 1=Dexterity (+0xE8), 2=Intelligence (+0xEA, drives max MP), 3=Spirit (+0xEC, drives max HP). Values > 3 write nothing, but the derived-stat recalc and stat-window refresh still run | stack [ESP+0x7C] (IAT 0x4A4094); switch via jump table 0x4585E4 |
| `value` | u16 | new ABSOLUTE allocated base-stat value (assignment, not a delta) | stack [ESP+0x64] (IAT 0x4A4090) -> word entity+0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC |

**Semantics.** All three fields are always read first. entity = FUN_004189f0(scene, uid); if it is null, stop (break at 0x4547EF). Switch on stat_index (jump table 0x4585E4, verified: 0->0x45480A, 1->0x45481B, 2->0x45482C, 3->0x4548F0; >3 -> 0x45492D): - Case 0: word +0xE6 = value. - Case 1: word +0xE8 = value. - Case 2: word +0xEA = value. If level +0x99 != 0, FUN_00427f40(0) recomputes max MP (+0x1110) and clamps cur MP (+0xA0) down to it. Then the party frames UI 0x75..0x78 are scanned; on the frame whose +0x134 == uid, if max MP != 0, text 2 = '%u/%u' (+0xA0, +0x1110) and bar 2 = ratio. - Case 3: word +0xEC = value. FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recomputes max HP (+0x110C) and clamps cur HP (+0x9C) only if it exceeds the new max. If the low word of max HP != 0, FUN_0043d3f0(uid, (u16)max_hp, (u16)cur_hp) updates the party HP display. All paths that found the entity then run FUN_0041ace0(scene, entity), which recomputes derived stats including the equipment bonuses +0xF0..+0xFC. If uid == scene+0x220 (the local player), FUN_00442510 redraws the stat window: 'Lv.%u', each stat as '%u' or '%u+%u' (base + bonus), and remaining stat points = total(level) - (E6+E8+EA+EC), where FUN_00440e10 total(L) = 9 + 4*min(L-1,28) + 5*max(0,L-29), or 0 if L > 99.

**Trigger.** Server reply to the client's stat-point allocation (C2S 0x04 in our server), or any server-side base-stat resync.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** The entity must exist, otherwise the packet is consumed (7 bytes) and ignored. The value is absolute: our server's hard-coded value 4 overwrites the real stat. Remaining points are derived client-side from level minus the sum of the four stats, so wrong values also corrupt the displayed free points. The packet never writes cur HP/MP directly; it only clamps them down after the max recalculation, so using 0x14 as a 'monster HP' packet is wrong. Case 2 skips the MP recalc when level == 0. Case 3's party HP update tests only the low 16 bits of max HP.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Analysts A and B agree on the read sequence: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 at 0x45479F, [ESP+0xE0]-12 = [ESP+0xD4]), u8 stat_index (IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x4547BA, [ESP+0x88]-12 = [ESP+0x7C]), u16 value (IAT 0x4A4090 at 0x4547D2, [ESP+0x70]-12 = [ESP+0x64]). A appended `if(entity_by_uid(uid) == null) { stop }`. The asm shows the entity lookup (CALL 0x4189F0 at 0x4547E6) and its null break (JZ 0x44D7AD at 0x4547EF) come after all three reads, and no later path reads the packet. The KR Hex-Rays case 0x14 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 4222) reads a u32 plus four u16 deltas: a different build, not applicable to EN. windslayer_server.py _handle_set_stats (line 957) uses the correct layout but uid = account_id and a hard-coded value 4. The comments at lines 88 and 1817 calling 0x14 an HP/monster-HP packet contradict the binary.

On result 1 NO further packet data is read: the client allocates a 0x15F0 entity and copies everything from its own creation screen (scene=*(0x70EECC)): name <- scene+0x206 (strcpy), appearance words entity+0x122<-scene+0x3AE, +0x128<-+0x3B4, +0x12A<-+0x3B6, +0x12C<-+0x3B8, +0x132<-+0x3BE, +0x134<-+0x3C0 (class), +0x13A<-+0x3C6, +0x136=0. n=scene+0x14 (current entity-list count = number of characters already shown): posX(+0x11F8)=(n+1)*110, posY(+0x1288)=300, uid(+0x84)=30000000+n, alive(+0x98)=3, +0x8D6=1, HP(+0x9C)=100, level(+0x99)=1; adds it to the scene via 0x422120, sets +0x8B4=4, then FUN_00483430(0x13,1,1) (leaves the creation window). If sent outside the char-select screen it would inject a bogus entity (uid 30000000+n, alive=3) into the world scene. No max-character check in EN (KR checks 12 slots), so over-creating just keeps placing entities further right. Only 1 byte is read; the KR build reads a 2nd u8 and has a result 5 ('nickname available'). Do not send the KR 2-byte form (the extra byte would be ignored here, but the length changes). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08): the n = scene+0x14 derivation is only safe on a freshly loaded character-select list. After an S2C 0x1F delete the surviving entities keep shifted uids/positions, so a 0x1C create can produce a uid or x that collides with an existing character.

**References.** KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc line 4916) reads u8 result + u8 flag and supports results 1..5; EN reads only result and supports 1..4, with the same meanings for 2/3/4. Our server (windslayer_server.py _handle_create_character ~line 2523) never sends 0x1C: it answers C2S 0x0E by re-sending the full 0x02 login/char-list, which also works. protocol.md's 0x0E layout matches the send site at 0x446FE4. PySlayer has no opcode_0x1C builder.

```
u8 result
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | 1=deleted, 2=server/DB busy, 3=created <24h ago (can't delete), 12=wrong password; 4..11, 0 and >12 = silent (popup just dismissed) | stack local [S+0x78] (switch selector only) |

**Semantics.** Reply to the character-delete request. Always dismisses the message box (window 0x16) first. Result 1: takes the selected character entity pointer at game_state(0x70EA00)+0x3F8 and, if it is not null, calls FUN_00422B90(scene, entity->uid). That frees the entity from the scene list and, in char-select mode (scene+0xF00==5), shifts entities by x -= 110 and uid -= 1. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): FUN_00422B90 walks the scene list FROM ITS HEAD and shifts every entity that comes AFTER THE FIRST MATCH IN LIST ORDER. The character-select list is HEAD-INSERTED (the last-loaded character is first), so the characters that actually move are the ones with LOWER slot indices (drawn to the LEFT); higher slots keep their x and uid, a gap is left behind, and slot 0 can end up at x = 0 / uid 29999999. After a delete the client no longer satisfies uid = 30000000+index or x = 110*(index+1). It then clears the selection. Result 2 shows 'Server process is running. Please try again in a few minutes (DB)', result 3 the 24-hour message, and result 12 'Invalid password'.

**Trigger.** Send after C2S 0x12 DeleteCharacter. Send site 0x44AB49: u8 0x12, str[17] name of the selected entity (game_state+0x3F8), str[21] password buffer (or zeros). The client only sends it when the selected entity has +0x15A8==0x214 and +0x904==8, then shows 'Waiting for the server to response.' CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Result 1 is harmless when nothing is selected (null check). The handler deletes whatever is selected on the client, not a name from the packet, so the server must answer the request actually made. KR's success path reads an extra date struct and shows a 1-week message; EN reads nothing more, so do not append data. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08): after a successful delete the client-side uid/x invariants are broken (see semantics), and a following S2C 0x1C create - which derives uid = 30000000 + n and x = 110*(n+1) from n = scene+0x14 - can COLLIDE with a surviving character. The server should re-send the whole character list (a fresh success S2C 0x02 after a fresh login, never a second 0x02 in the same char-select session, see C6) rather than rely on the client's post-delete layout.

**References.** KR (PySlayer doc line 5080) has the same u8 result switch, but its success path reads more data. EN reads 1 byte only. Our server does not dispatch C2S 0x12 and never sends 0x1F. The error strings are from strings.tsv (0x6F6680, 0x6F6BBC, 0x6F4E38).

**Open questions.**
- Exact source of the 21-byte password field in C2S 0x12 (a UI edit box lookup, window 0x201). This does not affect this S2C spec.

```

i32 exp_delta
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exp_delta` | i32 | signed experience change added to the local player's total exp (scene+0x278). Positive shows "You've received (+%d) experience points.". Negative is clamped so the total never goes below 0 and shows "Lost (%d) EXP." (prints the negative number). 0 shows no me… | stack [base+0x60] -> added to [scene+0x278] at 0x454571 |

**Semantics.** Local-player exp update; ignored entirely if no local player entity is registered (scene+0x970 == 0). delta > 0: FUN_00427cb0(old_total, old_total+delta) checks whether the next cumulative threshold of the exp table 0x6F0EB0 (same data as 0x6F0C28) is crossed. If so it does a client-side LEVEL-UP: opens UI event 0xA2 (FUN_00483430), queues level-up effect 0x24 on the local uid (FUN_0042b580), plays sound 0x24, sets local entity+0x99 = FUN_00440df0(new_total) (can jump several levels), recalculates max HP with full heal (FUN_00427d40(...,1)) and max MP with full refill (FUN_00427f40(1)), and refreshes the stat window (FUN_00442510, 'Lv.%u'). Then it posts the gain message to the chat/system log (FUN_004817d0, color -1). delta < 0: clamps the delta to -total. FUN_00427ce0 checks for a level-down threshold; if one is crossed it sets the level from the new total, recalculates HP/MP (no heal, clamps MP to max) and refreshes the stat window. Then it posts 'Lost (%d) EXP.' (color 0xFFFD4C87). Always: scene+0x278 += delta and FUN_00442aa0 redraws the exp bar ('%u/%u').

**Trigger.** Server grants or removes exp for the local player (monster kill, quest reward, death penalty).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** The local player must be registered (scene+0x970 != 0), otherwise the packet is silently dropped and the exp is NOT accumulated. Level-up is computed purely client-side from scene+0x278, so the server's exp total must match the client's starting exp (set by the login/spawn packets) or level-ups will happen at the wrong time or never. Our server also sends 0x22 after a threshold crossing, which plays the level-up effect and sound a second time.

**References.** windslayer_server.py _send_exp sends struct '<i' (4 bytes), which matches. It notes 0x21 'doesn't reliably apply the level', which fits the scene+0x278 baseline dependency above. The newer KR build reads 8-byte (64-bit) exp here, so it is NOT compatible. reference_combat_model.md 'curve @0x6f0eb0' is confirmed.

**Open questions.**
- Which login/spawn packet initializes scene+0x278 (total exp) was not traced in this batch.

```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | uid (entity+0x84) of the player (local or remote) whose level is set | stack [ESP+0x10C] (IAT 0x4A40C8 u32); used as effect target, entity lookup key (FUN_004189f0), and compared to party-fr… |
| `level` | u8 | new ABSOLUTE level. 0 = packet ignored after reading | stack [ESP+0x4D] (IAT 0x4A4094 u8) -> byte entity+0x99 |

**Semantics.** Both fields are always read. If level == 0 (0x4545B5) nothing else happens. Otherwise: (1) FUN_0042b580(0x24, uid, 0,0,0, 1, 9, 0) queues a deferred event record (type 9, id 0x24, target uid), which is the level-up effect. It runs before the entity lookup, so it is queued even if the uid is unknown. (2) entity = FUN_004189f0(scene, uid). If the entity is missing, jump to step 6. (3) byte entity+0x99 = level; FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 1) recomputes max HP (+0x110C) and sets cur HP (+0x9C) = max (full heal). It does this only when level is 1..99 and class byte +0x110 <= 6; otherwise it writes nothing. Then FUN_00427f40(1) with ESI=entity recomputes max MP (+0x1110) and sets cur MP (+0xA0) = max, again only if level < 100 and class < 7. (4) CSpriteControl::Play_Sound(0x24, entity+0x15A4, entity+0x15A8, gs+0x1044, gs+0x1048, gs+0x104C, gs+0x1050, 0) plays the level-up sound at the entity's screen position. (5) Scan the party-member frames, UI ids 0x75..0x78 (FUN_004830f0). For the first frame whose +0x134 == uid: if max HP != 0, write text 1 = sprintf('%u/%u', +0x9C, +0x110C) and set bar 1 = cur/max. Then, if max MP != 0, write text 2 = '%u/%u' (+0xA0, +0x1110) and set bar 2. If max HP == 0, both HP and MP updates are skipped. (6) FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C) always runs when level != 0, whether or not the entity or a party frame was found (0x454694 / 0x454780). It walks a record list filtered by the LOCAL player's level range (+0xDEC/+0xDF0 of each record), class/job and prerequisite ids, which looks like an available-quest list rebuild. The local stat window (FUN_00442510: 'Lv.%u', stat points) is NOT refreshed, the exp counter scene+0x278 is not changed, and no packet is sent back.

**Trigger.** Server-side level-up of any player: broadcast to observers and party members, and send to the owner to apply the new level to the avatar and play the effect.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** level == 0 makes the packet a no-op after both fields are consumed (still 5 bytes). The entity must already be spawned for the level/HP/MP to apply; the effect event is queued regardless. The effect and sound play every time, even if the level did not change, so pairing this with a 0x21 exp update that already levels the client plays them twice. Levels > 99 are stored in +0x99, but max HP/MP are not recalculated. Because 0x442510 is not called, the local HUD 'Lv.' label and remaining stat points stay stale until another refresh (e.g. 0x14 or 0x21 paths). The KR build returns early when the entity is missing; EN still runs the FUN_004781c0 refresh. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (login_character#14): besides the stat window, the HUD level label (top-left "LV") is NOT refreshed by 0x22 either.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Analysts A and B agree on the wire bytes: u32 uid (GetDataFromPacket IAT 0x4A40C8 at 0x454597, dest [ESP+0x118]-12 = [ESP+0x10C]) followed by u8 level (IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x4545AF, dest [ESP+0x59]-12 = [ESP+0x4D]). The only structural difference is that A appended `if(level == 0) { stop }`. The asm shows the level==0 test (CMP byte [ESP+0x4D],0 / JZ 0x44D7AD at 0x4545B5) comes AFTER both reads, and no path in the block reads anything else. The condition therefore gates side effects only, not how many bytes are consumed. A's trailing stop is redundant and misleading, so B's grammar `u32 uid / u8 level` is the correct canonical form, and the gate belongs in gates_and_hazards. On semantics: both correctly say FUN_004781c0 also runs when the entity is missing (JZ 0x454775 at 0x4545F4 falls into the call at 0x454780). B's label 'party list refresh' for FUN_004781c0 is not supported. Its decomp iterates records gated by the local player's level (+0x928 -> +0x99) against per-record min/max, class and prerequisite ids, which is consistent with an available-quest list, not a party list. B's note that 0x427D40 no-ops for level > 99 or class > 6 is confirmed by the FUN_00427d40 decomp. Cross-refs: windslayer_server.py _send_level packs '<IB' (matches). Its docstring's 'refreshes the HP/MP bars' refers only to party frames, and cur HP is full-healed by the flag=1 recalc. PySlayer Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x22 (line 5283) reads u32 + u8 the same way, but returns early when the entity is missing.

**Open questions.**
- FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C) exact identity: it looks like an available-quest list rebuild (records filtered by level range, class/job, a prerequisite id checked against 0x55 u16 ids at +0x262, and 3 ids at +0x256), but the owning UI was not traced.
- Deferred event type 9 / id 0x24 queued by FUN_0042b580 is assumed to be the level-up visual; the consumer (FUN_00459df0 queue) was not traced.

Window opens even if items are empty.

Not implemented in our server.

**Open questions.**
- Exact meaning of the four u16 stats (str/dex/int/spr naming comes from KR PySlayer and EN create-char, not from a label string in this window).
- Whether the item list in window 0x72 positions items by entry index or by item kind (item object carries no slot index, so position likely comes from item data or insertion order).

- ResetBuffer for the 0x2A request was not located inside FUN_00446300 (Send path shared at 0x4484C4).

(format "%s%s" with no space; EN string at 0x6F5128 has no leading space, so include a trailing space in the name only if cosmetic spacing is desired - but the field is fixed 17 bytes) in color 0xFFFD4C87 via FUN_004817d0. No state change. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.

**Trigger.** Negative reply to a name-targeted lookup, at least C2S 0x2A (view player info) when the target is offline; the positive reply is 0x52.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** None. Name must be NUL-terminated within the 17 bytes (sprintf_s %s on the stack buffer; a non-terminated 17-byte name would run into adjacent stack bytes).

**References.** KR Hex-Rays 0x53 is identical in shape (str[17] + '님은 서버에 없습니다.'). PySlayer opcode_0x53.py is a broken stub (emits opcode byte 0x51 + str[17]). Not in our server.

**Open questions.**
- Whether the original server also used 0x53 as the not-found reply for other name-addressed requests (whisper, party invite by name, friend add).

### S2C 0x58 — PlayerClassChange

*server → client* · key `0x58` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **missing** · length: 6 (4+1+1) when the uid is found; only 4 bytes consumed when it is not. Always send all 6.

Locations: `0x004575FA` handler block start (primary switch); `0x0045760F` GetDataFromPacket u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8) into stack [esp+0x1B0]: uid; `0x00457623` FUN_004189f0(scene=[game_state+0x4CC], EDX=uid). Returns 0 right away if uid==0, otherwis…; `0x0045762E` JZ 0x44D7AD: if the lookup returns null, break (nothing more is read)

```
u32 uid
if(find_entity_by_uid(uid) != null) {
  u8 class
  u8 class_tier
} else {
  stop
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | UID of the player whose class changed. Matched against entity+0x84 in the scene list at scene+0x0C. uid 0 or an unknown uid means the handler stops here and ignores the rest of the packet. | stack local [esp+0x1B0], used only as the lookup key |
| `class` | u8 | Base class index into the 15-byte name table at 0x70C588, row 0: 0 Novice, 1 Warrior, 2 Monk, 3 Archer, 4 Rogue, 5 Mage, 6 Priest. 0 means no class change yet: FUN_00446300 at 0x4493D2 shows 'You can use [Battlefield] after class change'. The HP and MP recomp… | entity+0x110 |
| `class_tier` | u8 | Advancement tier/branch, 0..2. The name index is (tier*7+class)*15 (0x440CAE..0x440CC0). Tier-1 row: 8 Berserker, 9 Fighter, 10 Sniper, 11 Assassin, 12 Elementalist, 13 Bishop. Tier-2 row: 14 Paladin, 15 Counter, 16 BeastMaster, 17 Trapper, 18 Summoner, 19 Da… | entity+0x111 |

**Semantics.** Reads the uid and looks up the entity. If it is not found, processing ends and the last 2 bytes are ignored. Otherwise it stores class at +0x110 and class_tier at +0x111. These are the same fields that 0x02 and 0x07 fill. If class_tier == 0, the client then (1) runs FUN_0041ace0 to recompute derived stats, (2) runs FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) to recompute max HP (+0x110C) and lower cur HP (+0x9C) if it is above the new max, (3) if level (+0x99) != 0, runs FUN_00427f40(0) to recompute max MP (+0x1110) and clamp cur MP (+0xA0), and (4) runs FUN_004781c0 to rebuild the local player's available-quest list. There is no popup, no sound and no reply packet.

**Trigger.** Server sends this when a character's class changes (job advancement). Send it to the player and to clients that have that entity spawned.

**Expected response.** none (no Add/Send in the block or its callees)

**Gates / hazards.** No in-world gate. FUN_004189f0 returns null for uid 0 without touching the scene. For uid != 0 it dereferences scene+0x0C without a null check, so the scene object must exist. An unknown uid is silently ignored. A non-zero class_tier skips all stat/HP/MP/quest recompute, so derived stats stay stale until something else recomputes them. A class of 7 or more makes the HP/MP recompute return early and indexes past the name table. A class_tier above 2 overlaps the next class's quest flags. HP and MP are only clamped down (arg 0). The quest refresh needs the local player object ([+0x928] != 0 check at 0x4781D0). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (login_character#16): 0x58 does NOT redraw the local status window or the HUD class label - they keep the old class name until another FUN_00442510 redraw. For the owner, follow it with a packet that forces a redraw (e.g. the 0x18 job-item path or 0x74).

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 @0x45760F), a lookup via FUN_004189f0 @0x457623 with JZ break @0x45762E, then u8 into +0x110 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457647) and u8 into +0x111 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457664), then a recompute gate on +0x111==0 @0x457673. They differ only in how the DSL writes it. A wrote 'if(found){u8 u8} else {stop}'. B wrote 'if(null){stop} u8 u8'. Both put the same bytes in the same order under the same condition, so neither is wrong. I chose A's explicit if/else because it maps directly onto the asm's JZ-to-break. B's field notes are also verified: the Battlefield gate at 0x4493D2 checks +0x110==0, and the quest filter at 0x4782DD..0x4782F0 uses class*3+tier. A's name-table claim is verified by dumping 0x70C588 from the exe, with one correction: the tier-2 row is not aligned with the class indexes (index 14=Paladin sits at class 0). Other references: PySlayer KR Hex-Rays case 0x58 reads u32 plus three u8 and gates on the third. EN reads two u8 and gates on the second, so EN is 6 bytes and must not copy the KR layout. PySlayer has no server builder for 0x58. Our server has no 0x58 builder, but its 0x02/0x07 builders write class/0 into the same two fields.

**Open questions.**
- Tier-2 name row at 0x70C588 is shifted by one versus the class index: (2*7+1)=15 is 'Counter' for Warrior, (2*7+0)=14 is 'Paladin' for Novice, and Priest tier 2 is empty. So either class_tier is not a simple sequential tier, or the client string table has an off-by-one. Needs a live check of which (class, tier) pairs the real server used.
- Why stats, HP, MP and quests are only recomputed when class_tier == 0 is unclear.
- Which C2S request or NPC flow triggers a class change in EN was not traced.

### S2C 0x74 — CharacterNameChanged

*server → client* · key `0x74` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **missing** · length: 21 (4 + 17); only 4 bytes consumed when uid is 0 or not a loaded entity

Locations: `0x00457EF6` handler block start (primary switch case 0x74); `0x00457F0B` GetDataFromPacket u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8) -> uid, stack slot [esp_at_block+0x1A0]; `0x00457F1F` FUN_004189F0(scene=[ESI+0x4CC]) with EDX=uid: returns NULL if uid==0 or no entity in scen…; `0x00457F2A` JZ break when lookup returned NULL (name NOT read)

```
u32 uid
if(entity_with_uid_exists) {
  str[17] new_name
} else {
  stop
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | Entity uid (entity+0x84) of the character whose name changed. uid 0 or a uid not present in the current scene entity list ends the handler without reading the name. | stack local (block-relative [esp+0x1A0]); used for FUN_004189F0 lookup and compared to scene+0x220 |
| `new_name` | str[17] | New character name, exactly 17 raw bytes, NUL-padded; must contain a NUL within the 17 bytes (max 16 chars) because for the local player it is copied with an unbounded strcpy. | read directly into entity+0x00 (name[17]); if uid == scene+0x220 also copied to scene+0x206 |

**Semantics.** Reads u32 uid and looks the entity up in the current scene's entity list (FUN_004189F0 walks scene+0xC nodes, matching node->entity+0x84 against EDX=uid; uid 0 returns NULL immediately). If not found, the handler breaks to 0x44D7AD without reading anything else. Otherwise it reads 17 bytes straight over the entity's name buffer (entity+0x00), so the name changes in place. If uid equals the local player uid (scene+0x220), it copies the name (inline strcpy loop) to scene+0x206 and calls FUN_00442510, which rebuilds the character-info panel labels (Lv.%u, stats, stat buttons) when scene+0x970 (local player entity) is non-null. No chat line, popup or sound in the EN build.

**Trigger.** Server broadcast to clients that have the renamed character loaded (including the renamer) after a successful rename. The requester separately receives S2C 0x73 (u8 result; result==1 is followed by a u32 and shows 'Your character name has successively changed.'; otherwise 'The name is already being used.').

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Global OnReceive gate: every packet is dropped while [game_state+0x408] != 0 (0x44D5F5). Unknown uid or uid 0 -> silently ignored; the 17 name bytes are left unconsumed (harmless as the handler ends). new_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes: the local-player copy to scene+0x206 is an unbounded byte loop that would run past entity+0x11 into following entity fields and overflow the scene name buffer. Only entity+0x00 is written; a cached nameplate record (entity+0x11DC) is not touched here, so whether the overhead name re-renders immediately is unverified. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C45, premium_cash#05): the server must NEVER send the short (4-byte) form. A 0x74 whose 17 name bytes are missing is read out of bounds by the client - live it did no visible harm, but the read is unbounded. Always send all 21 bytes, and only for a uid the receiver has loaded. (Test-tooling note: encoding this packet needs "__assume__": {"entity_with_uid_exists": true}, otherwise the client-state condition defaults to false and only 4 bytes are produced.)

**References.** ADJUDICATION: There is no real wire-format dispute. Analyst A gave 'u32 uid; if(entity exists){ str[17] new_name }' and Analyst B gave the same plus an explicit 'else { stop }'. Both describe identical byte behavior and both are correct; B's form is adopted only because it states the early-exit path explicitly. Evidence from the asm: at 0x457F0B a u32 is read via IAT 0x4A40C8 into [esp+0x1A0] (pushes: len EDI, &offset [esp+0x10], pkt EBX, dst lea [esp+0x1AC] after three pushes = [esp+0x1A0]); 0x457F17 loads EDX=uid and 0x457F1F calls FUN_004189F0, which takes EDX as the key, returns NULL for uid 0 or no match and never writes EDX (RET 4); 0x457F2A JZ 0x44D7AD skips the rest; 0x457F32/0x457F38 re-check entity+0x84==uid; 0x457F4B/0x457F4D push N=0x11 and dst=EAX (the entity pointer, i.e. entity+0x00) before the char-buffer read at 0x457F4E (IAT 0x4A4098); 0x457F61 compares uid with [scene+0x220] and JNZ breaks; 0x457F77..0x457F83 is an inline strcpy to scene+0x206; 0x457F87 calls FUN_00442510. A's related 0x73 claim is confirmed at 0x46278F..0x46282C (u8 result via 0x4A4094; ==1 then u32 via 0x4A40C8 and the success string 0x6F46CC; else string 0x6F4DFC). KR Hex-Rays case 0x74 (u8 subtype + uid + name + rename chat line) does not match EN. PySlayer has no opcode_0x73/0x74 builder; our windslayer_server.py has no 0x74 references.

**Open questions.**
- Whether nameplates for remote players re-read entity+0x00 each frame or use a cached record at entity+0x11DC (decides whether other players see the new name right away without a respawn).
- Meaning of the u32 that follows result==1 in S2C 0x73 (passed to FUN_00464380); outside this batch.

### S2C 0x7F — ExpDeltaFromMenti

*server → client* · key `0x7F` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 8 if exp_delta > 0, else 4

Locations: `0x004542C4` handler block start (shared 0x21/0x7F); gate scene+0x970; `0x4542E9` read i32 exp_delta; `0x4542F4` JLE: delta<=0 skips menti read; `0x4543C6` CMP opcode,0x7F

```
if(scene+0x970 == 0) { stop }
i32 exp_delta
if(exp_delta > 0) { u32 menti_id }
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exp_delta` | i32 | signed exp change for the local player (same processing as 0x21: level-up/down, message, scene+0x278 += delta) | stack [base+0x60] -> scene+0x278 |
| `menti_id` | u32 | id of the mentee (apprentice) the exp bonus came from. Matched against record+0x18 of the entries in the mentor/menti list (game_state+0x4E4 manager, list head +0x28; records are filled by SubHandler3 e.g. S2C 0x0B: name[17]@+0, u8@+0x14, u32@+0x18, u8@+0x20)… | stack [base+0x204]; compared with [record+0x18] |

**Semantics.** Same as 0x21 (ignored if no local player; level-up/down; scene+0x278 += delta; exp bar refresh), but when delta > 0 it also reads menti_id and searches the mentor manager list. If a record with +0x18 == menti_id is found, it posts "You've received (+%d) experience points.(Menti[%s])" with that record's name. If not found, NO message is shown but the exp is still added. For delta <= 0 the u32 is not read and the 0x21 behaviour applies (the 'Lost (%d) EXP.' message for negative values).

**Trigger.** Server grants the mentor a bonus share of exp earned by one of their mentees ('Menti').

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Same local-player gate and exp-baseline hazard as 0x21. Sending menti_id with delta <= 0 is harmless (trailing bytes are ignored). The name lookup needs the mentor list to have been filled first (SubHandler3 0x0B-family packets); otherwise the message is skipped.

**References.** Strings: 0x6F5E00 "You've received (+%d) experience points.(Menti[%s])", plus the mentor/menti login strings used by SubHandler3 0x4708C0 / 0x470780. The newer KR build shares a case with 0x21 but uses 64-bit exp and a different extra read order, so it is NOT compatible. Not in windslayer_server.py or PySlayer.

**Open questions.**
- Whether menti_id is the mentee's in-world uid or a DB character id: it is compared to the u32 at record+0x18 filled by SubHandler3 0x0B, whose source was not traced further.
- Exact list-object layout (manager+4 list vs head at +0x28) not verified; only the compare offsets are certain.

**Semantics.** Opcode byte only, no payload. Closes an open Item Stall. The user sends it by closing the stall window (event 2) or pressing control 0x1A while the stall is open. The client also sends it by itself on the S2C 0x08/0x5E/0xA3/0xA4 handler path and from FUN_0042cf20 when the local player's state +0x15B4 is not 8. Locally the client only clears ctx+0x1C and does not clear ctx+0x20. If the stall is not open (ctx+0x20 == 0), the same events just close the window with no packet.

**Trigger.** User: event 2 or 0x1A on dialog 0x259 while ctx+0x20 != 0. Automatic: the OnReceive block at 0x450867 (S2C 0x08/0x5E/0xA3/0xA4), or FUN_0042cf20 @0x42F42F when the local player leaves state 8.

**Expected response.** Probably S2C 0x84 u8 result (1 -> the client closes dialog 0x259). Inferred.

**Gates / hazards.** Sent only while ctx+0x20 != 0 (and ctx+0x0C != 0). ctx+0x20 is not cleared on this path, so the FUN_0042cf20 trigger may fire again on later updates until the server reply closes the window or state changes. The server should treat repeated 0x60 as harmless and idempotent.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Analyst A reported a zero-payload 0x60 from dialog 0x259 events 2/0x1A, with automatic triggers. Analyst B missed it: the path reaches the shared Send only by JMP 0x469BA3 @0x46B6D4. The asm confirms A. 0x46B6C1 CMP [EBX+0x20],ESI (ESI=0). JZ 0x46B6D9 (close window, no send). 0x46B6C6 MOV ECX,[EBX+0x14]. PUSH 0x60. MOV [EBX+0x1C],0. Add(uchar) @0x46B6CE. JMP 0x469BA3 -> Send(1) @0x469BA8, with no further Adds. Jump-table decode: events 2 and 0x1A -> 0x46B6C1. The callers were verified in the asm: 0x42F424 PUSH 0x259 / ECX=2, and 0x450916 ECX=EBX+1=2 with EDX=0x259 pushed. The s2c_dispatch_map routes opcodes 0x08, 0x5E, 0xA3 and 0xA4 to handler 0x450867, which flows into 0x450919. The S2C 0x84 handler @0x46D1AD reads u8 and on 1 closes dialog 0x259. Our memory notes: +0x15B4 is 8 when idle and 4 when attacking. Not in PySlayer or our server.

**Open questions.**
- Does closing dialog 0x259 (FUN_00483430) run a callback that clears ctx+0x00/+0x08/+0x20? That decides whether the FUN_0042cf20 auto-close repeats.
- The pairing with S2C 0x84 is inferred.
- The return-value meaning of FUN_004837c0(0x259) in the @0x450901 check (== 1 skips) was not confirmed.

*server → client* · key `0x19` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 15 + 2*opt_count (opt_count must be <= 5)

```
u64 gold
u16 item_id
u16 count
u8 opt_count
repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt }
u16 opt_extra
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gold` | u64 | Inventory gold after the sale; its label is refreshed right away | player_info+0x228; label window 9 child 0xB via FUN_004659d0 @0x46DC20 |
| `item_id` | u16 | Item id that was sold, 1-based index into the item catalog [[ctx+0x10]+0xF84] | local [frame+0x24] -> FUN_00404210 (catalog lookup), FUN_00467140 arg1 |
| `count` | u16 | Number sold. Removed from type-0/type-2 stacks; ignored for equipment (type 1 always removes 1). Printed in 'Sold %u (%s).' | local [frame+0x14] (low word) -> FUN_00467140 arg3 (read as a word) |
| `opt_count` | u8 | How many option words follow (0..5) | local [frame+0x0C] |
| `opt` | u16 | Option words 0..opt_count-1 of the item's 12-byte option block. The array starts zeroed, so words not sent stay 0. | local opts[i] at [frame+0x34+2*i] |
| `opt_extra` | u16 | Word 5 of the 12-byte option block (always read after the loop) | local opts[5] at [frame+0x3E] |

**Semantics.** 1) Store gold at player_info+0x228 and refresh the inventory gold label. This happens even if the rest fails. 2) Read item_id and count, zero a local 12-byte option block (6 u16 words), read opt_count, then opt_count u16s into words 0.., then one u16 into word 5. 3) Look up the item definition by item_id; if none (item_id 0 or past the end of the catalog), stop quietly (returns 1). 4) Remove the item according to its type (def+0x154): type 0 subtracts count from u16 stacks (the whole thing fails if total owned < count); type 1 (equipment) removes the first slot whose id matches AND whose 12 stored option bytes equal the packet's block exactly, then shifts later slots down; type 2 subtracts count from u8 stacks; any other type fails. 5) Only if removal worked: show system chat 'Sold <count> (<item name>).' and refresh the inventory UI. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.

**Trigger.** The server's reply to a shop sell request (C2S 0x0C in our server). The gold field lets the server credit the sale price.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** CRASH HAZARD: the opts array is 6 words on the stack and opt_count is never checked. opt_count >= 6 writes past word 4 (word 5 is later overwritten by opt_extra) into other locals; opt_count >= 63 reaches the /GS cookie at [frame+0xB0], and the client terminates when the handler returns. Keep opt_count <= 5. Equipment matching: an item added with 0x18 has an all-zero option block, so it can only be removed with opt_count=0 and opt_extra=0 (or with the exact nonzero words the client stored). Equipment removal also fails if the tab capacity byte player_info+0x361 > 45; types 0/2 fail if their capacity byte (+0x362/+0x363) > 45. count=0 on a type 0/2 item removes nothing and shows no message. The chat line needs the chat window ([ui+0x59C]) to exist.

**References.** Matches PySlayer opcode_0x19 (u64 gold, u16 idx, u16 count, u8 n, n*u16, u16) and our server's _build_opcode_19 (15 B, opt_count=0). Memory note 'combat model: 0x19=SELL' agrees. Our server's comments call the loop list 'extra'; it is really option words 0..4 of the item option block, and the trailing u16 is word 5 (the C2S 0x3C encoder in FUN_00469090 builds the same block: u8 n (non-zero words among the first 5), n*u16, then u16 word 5; non-equipment sends u8 0 + u16 0).

**Open questions.**
- What option words 0..4 and word 5 mean (sockets/refine/durability?).
- Tab names for item types 0 and 2 (u16 stacks up to 999 with a per-slot u32, vs u8 stacks up to 99). Type 1 is equipment, type 3 skill book, type 4 class-change item.
