| `target_uid` | u32 | Uid of the entity carrying the buff | stack [esp+0x170]; compared with scene+0x220 (local player uid) |

**Semantics.** Same slot removal as 0x3C (arena-gated FUN_004256c0, event 0xE2 for 0xA31-0xA3B, compaction). Then: FUN_00425af0(scene, entity, 0) returns 0 at once unless the id is in an aura range (0x8E7-0x912 or 0xAE3-0xAF8). For auras it re-applies team auras (arena map) or party auras (party uids scene+0x25C..+0x26C) to the affected members and returns non-zero when the local player is affected. If the definition has any non-zero stat field at +0x1B8/+0x1BC/+0x1C0/+0x1C4, FUN_0041ace0 recomputes the entity's stats. If target_uid == scene+0x220 (local player) or the aura result was non-zero, it refreshes the stat panel (FUN_00443840), HP/MP gauges (FUN_00443690) and party HP bars (FUN_0043d4e0).

**Trigger.** Server when a stat-affecting or aura buff/debuff on an entity expires or is dispelled. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C4): MANDATORY. The client never expires a buff by itself (it counts slot +0xC down into negative values and leaves the record and icon in place), so every timed buff granted with 0x3B / 0x41 / 0x42 must be terminated by the server: 0x43 when stats or auras must be recomputed, 0x3C when only the icon has to go.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Invalid id -> uid not read, nothing happens. Unknown uid -> nothing. Aura re-evaluation and stat recompute run once the entity is found, even if no slot matched (harmless). Adjacent duplicate slots: only the first is removed per packet. KR layout has an extra u8 after the id; EN does not.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Wire formats agree, and the u16/lookup/u32 evidence is the same as for 0x3C (0x456660, 0x45667C/0x456687, 0x4566A4, 0x4566BC/0x4566C9). The only structural difference is notation. The 0x43 branch starts at 0x4567B0 (cmp [esp+0x43],0x43) and does no further packet reads. Naming follows 0x3C: the table is CITEMControl (B right), and the entries are skill-effect records (A right). On FUN_00425af0, A is correct and B's 'stat recompute' is imprecise: the decomp entry check returns 0 unless AX is in 0x8E7-0x912 or 0xAE3-0xAF8, so it is aura re-application, and the general stat recompute is FUN_0041ace0 at 0x456807, gated on def+0x1B8..+0x1C4. Both analysts correctly state the HUD refresh condition at 0x456818-0x456823 (local uid or EBX!=0). KR Hex-Rays shares case 0x3C/0x43 (branch on opcode 67) but has an extra u8. Not in PySlayer. Our server: not implemented.

**Open questions.**
- Which buffs the original server removed with 0x43 versus 0x3C (likely 0x43 for stat/aura buffs).
- Exact meaning of item-def fields +0x1B8..+0x1C4 (likely stat bonus values) and +0x160 (used by FUN_00427d40 inside the aura path).

```
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | entity uid whose skill list is updated | stack base+0x1E8 |
| `skill_item_id` | u16 | item/skill id of a skill record (template Type field +0x154 must be 3; template +0x1DC = skill level within its family, family base = id - level) | entity+0x29A[k] (u16[30] learned-skill list), k chosen by FUN_00426b80 |

**Semantics.** Adds or upgrades a learned skill on an entity in the scene: looks up the item template for skill_item_id; if Type (+0x154) == 3 (skill), calls FUN_00426b80 over the entity's 30-entry u16 learned-skill list at +0x29A. If a skill of the same family (id - \|template+0x1DC\|) is present with a lower id, it is replaced; if the same family is already at >= this id nothing changes; if the family is absent the first empty (0) slot gets the id; if all 30 are full nothing happens. No UI message, no refresh. The same list is filled at spawn by the u8-count u16 loop in 0x07/0x2B, is checked by FUN_00467680 ('You already have learned this skill.'), and is updated for the local player by FUN_00440920 case 3.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Stops silently if uid not in scene, if the id has no template, if template Type != 3, if template skill level (+0x1DC) == 0, or if the list is full / already at an equal or higher level. Unknown ids are bounds-checked (no crash).

**References.** PySlayer opcode_0x57.py (KR) sends u8 + u32 + u16 ('About Item/skill') - EN has no leading u8. wsre.py labels 0x57 'QuestLogAdd/Reward' and project_status.md mentions a '0x57 log-add' quest fallback - WRONG for EN. enter_world_fields.md / our 0x07 builder call the +0x29A u16 loop an 'inventory count/extras' - it is the learned-skill list. gamedef note: starter quest item 377 is Type=3, consistent with Type 3 = skill. Not implemented in our server.

**Open questions.**

- Whether the scene list searched by FUN_004189f0 includes the local player (if yes, 0x57 also updates the local skill list without a skill-window refresh).

### S2C 0x5F — SkillRequestUnlock

*server → client* · key `0x5F` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 0

Locations: `0x00457794` handler block start (primary switch); `0x0045779A` write word [[game_state+0x4CC]+0x258] = 0 (scene pending-skill id); `0x0044C0E1` skill-use path: only sends C2S 0x15 <skill_id> when scene+0x258 == 0, then sets scene+0x2…; `0x0044C3B3` equip path: C2S 0x0F equip only allowed when scene+0x258 == 0

```
(empty payload)
```

**Semantics.** No payload. Clears the scene's pending-skill word (scene+0x258). The client sets that word to the skill id when it sends C2S 0x15 for a skill (FUN_0044c090). While it is non-zero, the client refuses to send another skill request and silently blocks equip/unequip (FUN_0044c2c0 / FUN_0046cad0; 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.'). The 0x25/0x3B skill-effect handler also clears it. 0x5F releases the lock WITHOUT any effect, so it is effectively a 'skill request rejected/cancelled' reply.

**Trigger.** Send in reply to a C2S 0x15 skill request that the server rejects or will not animate (cooldown, invalid target, not enough MP, etc.). Otherwise the client stays locked until some 0x25/0x3B arrives or a map-change reset runs (FUN_0042c360 also zeroes it).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** No gate. It dereferences [game_state+0x4CC] (scene) without a null check, so do not send it before the scene exists. It has no visual effect and is a no-op if no skill is pending.

**References.** Our server's _handle_use_item (C2S 0x15) ignores non-consumable ids and sends nothing, so casting a skill there leaves scene+0x258 set: the client can't cast again and can't equip until a map change. Sending 0x5F in that branch would fix it. Not in PySlayer. The 0x25/0x3B handler at 0x453D89 clears the same word.

**Open questions.**
- Whether the original server also used 0x5F for other kinds of cancel (e.g. interrupted cast) is unknown; the client-side effect is the same either way.


| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skill_id` | u16 | Skill definition id (the same table and ids as C2S 0x15 use-skill and the quick slots). The HP amount is NOT on the wire: the client uses skill_record+0x158 (signed i32 HP delta) from its own data table. | stack local frame+0xB0; index (1-based) into the vector at [[0x70EECC]+0xF84] |

**Semantics.** Applies a skill's HP effect to the whole party on the client. Steps: 1) record = skill_table[skill_id-1] (vector begin +8, end +0xC). If it is out of range or null (including skill_id 0), stop. 2) For each of the 5 u32 party uid slots at scene+0x25C, +0x260, +0x264, +0x268, +0x26C that is non-zero and matches an entity in the scene list (FUN_004189f0): spawn effect event 0x10E on that uid (FUN_0042b580(0x10E, uid, 0,0,0,1,0xA,0)), play sound 0x10E (non-positional), entity+0x9C (cur HP, i32) += record+0x158, clamp to entity+0x110C (max HP) and to >= 0. If the low 16 bits of max HP are non-zero, call FUN_0043d3f0(uid, (u16)max, (u16)cur) to update that member's party HP bar ('%u/%u' plus gauge) on party frame windows 0x75..0x78. 3) If the local player entity scene+0x970 exists, record+0x158 != 0 and FUN_004258d0(skill_id) returns 1: spawn effect 0x10E on the local uid, play sound 0x10E positioned at the local entity (+0x15A4/+0x15A8) relative to the camera (this+0x1044..0x1050), local cur HP += delta clamped to [0, max], and FUN_00443690 refreshes the HUD HP text '%d/%d' and gauge. FUN_004258d0 returns 0 (skips the self-heal) for these skill_id ranges: 0x187-0x191, 0x1BE-0x1C8, 0x24D-0x257, 0x8C6-0x8D0, 0x8F2-0x8FC, 0x997-0x9A1, 0x9C3-0x9F9 (five consecutive 11-id blocks), 0xA5D-0xA67, 0xAF9-0xB03, 0xB0F-0xB19, 0xB25-0xB2F.

**Trigger.** After a party member casts a party-wide HP skill (e.g. a group heal), send to every party member's client so each one applies the heal locally.

**Expected response.** None

**Gates / hazards.** The client changes HP locally from its own skill table, so the server must apply the same delta (record+0x158) to its HP state or the HP bars will drift. Use explicit HP packets such as 0x54/0x28 to resync if needed. If the party slot list contains the local player's own uid (RegisterLocalPlayer compares the slots against the local uid, so self can be in the list), the local player may be healed twice: once in the loop, and again in step 3 for skills not excluded by FUN_004258d0. Unknown or zero skill_id does nothing. Out of party (all slots 0) only step 3 applies. Every call allocates an effect event (FUN_0042b580) per target and plays sound 0x10E. Avoid sending in bursts (the earlier lag was traced to per-hit effect events from 0x40).

**References.** Our server has no 0x92 builder; windslayer_server.py only mentions '0x92->0x10e' in a comment about hard-coded sounds, which matches Play_Sound 0x10E here. The KR Hex-Rays case 0x92 differs: it parses a larger struct through sub_40A010 (12 locals, skill id in the third field) and uses effect/sound 0x70, but the loop over 5 party slots (KR offsets 592..612) and the local-player branch have the same structure. The EN wire format is only a u16, confirmed by the single GetDataFromPacket(ushort&) at 0x457CFB. The skill table identification rests on the quick-slot code (FUN_0043d8b0 -> FUN_00404210 on the same table -> FUN_0044c090 sending C2S 0x15 with record +0x154 type, +0x158 HP, +0x15C MP cost) and on the matching FUN_004258d0 gate in the 0x41/0x42 handler (0x453EEE).

**Open questions.**
- Whether scene+0x25C..+0x26C (the party uid slots) includes the local player's own uid in practice, which would double-apply the heal for skills FUN_004258d0 does not exclude.
- Exact skill names for the excluded id ranges in FUN_004258d0 (11-id blocks = one skill per level range). They could be cross-checked against gamedef.sqlite3.
- Whether record+0x158 is really 'HP delta' for every skill type. It is signed: negative values are HP costs (see the 'Not enough HP.' check in FUN_0044c090).

### C2S 0x01 — LoginRequest

*client → server* · key `0x44D8BF/0x01` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 62

Locations: `0x44D7CF` S2C 0x5A (key exchange) handler entry; the login send is the tail of this handler; `0x44D7E4` reads i32 key from S2C 0x5A, then SetCodeKey at 0x44D7F8; `0x44D872` Sleep(1000) before building the packet (receive critical section app+0x368 still held); `0x44D880` Add(u8 0x01) opcode

```
str[41] account_id
str[21] password
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | str[41] | Login account ID typed in the login dialog, NUL-terminated. Exactly 0x29 bytes are copied from a 185-byte buffer. | app[+0x4CC] (player/account struct) +0x48; filled by strcpy at 0x448160 from UI edit ctrl 0x1c |
| `password` | str[21] | Plaintext password, NUL-terminated. Exactly 0x15 bytes are copied from a 48-byte buffer. | app[+0x4CC] +0x101; filled by strcpy at 0x448184 from UI edit ctrl 0x1e |

**Semantics.** Account login on the game socket. The server sends S2C 0x5A (i32 code key) as the first packet after connect. The client's 0x5A handler: (1) calls SetCodeKey(key); (2) initializes the object at app+0x700 (FUN_0045ae40); (3) computes the MD5 hex of the account-ID string into app+0xD0A. The second %s in that sprintf is a zeroed 64-byte stack buffer, so the key is NOT hashed. (4) strncmp's the hex against player+0x131 (32 bytes) and sets player+0x218 = 1 if they differ, else 0. (5) Sleeps 1000 ms. (6) Sends opcode 0x01 + 41 bytes of account ID + 21 bytes of password. Nothing else is Added: no ResetBuffer, no helper Adds, no branches between the first Add and Send. The hash and the key are not sent.

**Trigger.** Automatic: runs every time S2C 0x5A is received on the game socket. Normally this happens once, right after the user presses login in the channel/login dialog and ConnectToGameServer succeeds.

**Expected response.** S2C 0x02 login result: u8 result (1 = success, followed by the account/character list; other codes show an error dialog and the client closes the socket).

**Gates / hazards.** Before connecting, the login dialog (FUN_00446300) requires non-empty account and password (strlen checks at 0x4481A9 and 0x4481C9) and a channel status of 3 at 0x448211. The strcpy's are unbounded and do not clear the rest of the buffer. So (a) an account ID of 41+ chars is sent with no NUL terminator, and (b) bytes after the NUL can be leftovers from an earlier, longer entry in the same session. The server must split each field at the first NUL. Because of the Sleep(1000) inside the receive critical section, the login arrives about 1 s after 0x5A, and no other S2C packet is processed meanwhile. Every extra S2C 0x5A makes the client re-send the login (the server already ignores a mid-flow 0x01). The Send argument is always 1 (encode mode; it is not part of the body).

**References.** Matches the live capture (0x01 payload = 62 bytes), protocol.md ('CHAR[41] username, CHAR[21] password') and windslayer_server.py _handle_login (payload[0:41], payload[41:62]). Correction to protocol.md: it says the 0x5A handler 'computes MD5 of username+key'. The asm shows sprintf("%s%s", account_id, <zeroed 64-byte buffer>), so it is MD5(account_id) only. The key is not mixed in, and the hash is used only locally (player+0x218 flag). PySlayer has no client_packets parser for 0x01.

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of player+0x218 (set when MD5(account_id) != player+0x131); it may mark a changed or new account for saved-login UI. It is not on the wire.
- The max length of edit controls 0x1c/0x1e was not checked. If it is 40/20 or less, the NUL is always inside the field.

Once that entity's int X (+0x15A4) exceeds 780 (0x30C) (likely the walk-off after Start), and UI window id 0x16 is absent or its +0x3C == 1, the packet is built on the next logic tick. The UI branches on entity+0x110 only copy text between controls of window 0x2B and do not change the bytes.

**Expected response.** S2C 0x03 (in-game state; its handler at 0x44E38F kills timer 2 and closes windows 0x16/0x13), then S2C 0x07 local-player spawn (PySlayer and our server also send 0x0A welcome chat; ours also sends 0x28/0x44 HP/MP).

**Gates / hazards.** If scene+0x224 was never filled, p2p_ip is zeros, so the server must not require it. What happens when TIMER_RECEIVELOADED (id 2, 5500 ms) fires with no S2C 0x03 was not traced (memory notes a ~35 s loading loop re-arming). The branch with entity+0x110 != 0 dereferences a NULL text pointer if window 0x2B is missing (client-side crash only).

**References.** Capture (42 bytes) '00 00 00 00 00 \| 31 32 37 2E 30 2E 30 2E 31 00*7 \| 9B A7 00 00 \| 54 65 73 74 48 65 72 6F 00...' matches: 5 refuse flags, 16-byte IP, u32 42907, 17-byte name. This CORRECTS memory protocol.md, which calls it a 'client version string' plus a 'WORD 0xA79B magic key', and our server's docstring ('[5-13] ip', '[21-22] 0xA79B magic'). The real layout is str[16] at 5..20 and u32 port at 21..24. Our server reads name = payload[25:42], which is correct. PySlayer parse_2B reads the IP from body[6:0x15], consistent.

**Open questions.**
- TIMER_RECEIVELOADED (id 2) expiry handler not located: does it resend 0x2B or abort?
- Identity of UI window 0x16 (its +0x3C must be 1) and meaning of entity+0x110 on the select screen.
- Whether the original server used p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port to broker P2P arena rooms (FUN_00458640 UDP protocol).

| `version_code` | u16 | Client-version gate. Accepted only if ==3 (normal: Start button enabled) or >=0xEA61 (60001: notice/refusal mode). Anything else: stop reading, launcher runs the auto-patcher (G_UpdateList.h from windslayer.globalgamecdn.com). | stack local [esp+0xC8] |
| `notice_len` | u16 | Byte length of the notice text that follows (0 allowed) | stack local [esp+0xD0]; malloc(notice_len+1) |
| `notice_text` | str[notice_len] | Launcher notice text (no NUL needed; buffer is zero-terminated by client). Shown in launcher dialog control 0x403; if version_code>=0xEA61 also shown in popup dialog 0x16 (strcpy into a 0x3E9-byte buffer) | heap buffer -> SetDlgItemTextA(gs+0x3E0, 0x403) at 0x44D74A; freed at 0x44D784 |
| `server_count` | u8 | Number of world servers. UI shows only 4 (loop at 0x441528); record array is 0x80 bytes each from gs+0x1290 and runs into gs+0x1490 (selected server/channel bytes) at index 4 -> keep <=4 | game_state+0x128C |
| `server_status` | u8 | World status, stored zero-extended as u32. UI: <1 hidden, 1..2 greyed, 3 selectable, >3 hidden. Value 1 means no channel data follows for this server. | game_state+0x1290+i*0x80 (u32) |
| `channel_slot_count` | u8 | Number of channel slots for this server (loop bound). Slots are 12-byte records at gs+0x1294+i*0x80+j*12; only 10 fit before this byte itself (UI loop shows 10) -> keep <=10. Every slot 1..count not listed below is marked state 2 = '(inspection)' (maintenance) | game_state+0x130C+i*0x80 |
| `channel_entry_count` | u8 | Number of channel entries actually present on the wire | game_state+0x130D+i*0x80 |
| `channel_no` | u8 | 1-based channel number of the next entry. First one read unconditionally when channel_entry_count!=0 (even if channel_slot_count==0); subsequent ones read only after a matched entry while entries_read<channel_entry_count. Must be strictly ascending and <=chan… | temp (reuses stdcall arg slot); copied to slot byte gs+0x1298+i*0x80+(no-1)*12; slot state u32 set to 3 |
| `user_count` | u16 | Channel population/load. UI colour = user_count/200: 0 green, 1 yellow, >=2 red | game_state+0x129A+i*0x80+(channel_no-1)*12 |
| `game_server_ip` | u32 | Game server IPv4 for this channel, passed to CSNSocket::Connect(ip, 7022) at 0x440814. Our server sends host-order 0x7F000001 (LE bytes 01 00 00 7F) for 127.0.0.1 and that works | game_state+0x129C+i*0x80+(channel_no-1)*12 |

**Semantics.** Version-server (TCP 7011) reply. Global gate: whole OnReceive is skipped if [game_state+0x408]!=0. Reads version_code; if not 3 and <0xEA61 the launcher starts its HTTP auto-updater and nothing else is read. Otherwise reads the notice text and calls ParseChannelList, which fills the per-server/per-channel tables, closes the version socket (error 'Failed to close version server socket' aborts the UI refresh), copies the previously chosen server gs+0x1492 into gs+0x1490 if that server's status==3, and redraws the server/channel list ('Channel - N', 'Channel - N (inspection)', load colours). Then the notice goes to launcher control 0x403. version_code>=0xEA61: popup with the notice, immediately followed by FUN_0044d4b0(0) = 'Connection to Server got disconnected' + SetTimer(main hwnd,7,5000); Start is NOT enabled. version_code==3: SetTimer(launcher,8,300) which enables and blinks the Start button. Canonical well-formed wire per channel entry is simply u8 channel_no, u16 user_count, u32 ip (7 bytes) repeated channel_entry_count times.

**Trigger.** Immediately after the client connects to the version server (7011); server sends it once and the client closes the socket.

**Expected response.** None on the version socket (client closes it). If version_code==3, the user picks a server/channel and presses Start -> ConnectToGameServer TCP to game_server_ip:7022, where the server must send 0x5A.

**Gates / hazards.** Top-of-dispatch gate [gs+0x408]!=0 drops the packet. Wrong version_code -> launcher tries to download patches from a dead CDN. server_count>4 overflows into gs+0x1490.. (selected server/channel); channel_slot_count>10 overwrites the slot_count/entry_count bytes and the next server record. Non-ascending or out-of-range channel_no silently leaves remaining entries unread (and slots marked 'inspection'). notice_text >1000 bytes overflows the popup buffer in the >=0xEA61 path (strcpy into 0x3E9 bytes). version_code>=0xEA61 path ends in a disconnect dialog + 5 s timer 7.

**References.** Our VersionServer._build_version_body matches exactly: u16 3, u16 len, text, u8 1 server, u8 status 3, u8 slots 1, u8 entries 1, u8 ch 1, u16 0, u32 0x7F000001. protocol.md agrees (port in list ignored, 7022 hardcoded at 0x44080E). PySlayer (newer KR) differs: KR accepts version 4 (not 3) and its channel entry carries extra u32 port + u8; KR also uses msg 0x402 and loads main99_01.hmi - do not copy KR layout.

**Open questions.**
- Exact effect of timer 7 set by FUN_0044d4b0 in the >=0xEA61 path (likely client exit after 5 s) was not traced.
- IP byte order relies on Fireway CSNSocket::Connect doing htonl (per our server comment / live success), not re-verified in Fireway.dll here.
- Difference between server_status 0 (hidden) and 2 (greyed) in terms of server intent (e.g. offline vs full) is UI-only; no textual label found.

Then reads transfer_status (+optional 33-byte text) and updates the transfer text. Finally scene+0xF18=0, resets three sub-systems (gs+0xD2C, gs+0xD5C, gs+0xDC4), stores the game server peer address at gs+0x14C8 and broadcasts UDP 0x11 + u32 account_id to 255.255.255.255:42907 on the map socket.

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x01 login (after 0x5A). Also re-sent after character creation to refresh the list (our server does this).

**Expected response.** Success: no TCP reply; client sends UDP broadcast (map socket) u8 0x11 + u32 account_id to port 42907. User then acts on the char-select screen (create character / enter world, e.g. C2S 0x2B). Failure: none (socket closed by client).

**Gates / hazards.** Only the global [gs+0x408]!=0 drop; no in-world check - a success 0x02 received while in world tears the client back to character select (matches our server note). Any result!=1 (including unknown values) closes the game socket. Each success allocates new character entities. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C6, login_character#03/#05): the previous entities are NOT freed - they are appended, scene+0x14 is INCREMENTED (not reset) and uids restart at 30000000+i, so a second success 0x02 received at character select produces DUPLICATE uids and overlapping bodies (clicking then selects the older entity). SERVER RULE: never send a second success 0x02 while the client is at character select; announce a new character with S2C 0x1C instead. Level is derived client-side from total_exp; sending a level number in job_branch changes the displayed class name instead. Extra trailing bytes after the last read are ignored. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C38, login_character#23): the "hide window 0x12 controls 5, 6 and 7" done for transfer_status values other than 1/2 (when scene+0x218 != 0) is STICKY - a later 0x02 with status 1 or 2 only sets the control-7 text and does NOT make the controls visible again. The ID-transfer UI (and therefore C2S 0x65/0x66) is reachable only if the session's FIRST 0x02 carries status 1/2 (or scene+0x218 == 0).

**References.** Our _build_login_success is wire-compatible (12-byte header, 75-byte records, u8 3, plus 16 ignored trailing bytes) but MISLABELS fields: the byte it calls 'level' is job_branch (entity+0x111; sending level=1 shows 2nd-job name e.g. 'Berserker'), the first u32 'look' is total_exp, the 6 u32 'fields' are 3 u32 ranks + 3 i32 rank changes, 'unknown_1' is the cash first-purchase flag, 'has_premium' is the gender flag, 'premium_flags' is manner points, the trailing byte 3 is transfer_status. It uses results 0x0B (short payload) and 0x11 (bad password) correctly. protocol.md error list is incomplete (see result field). PySlayer KR 0x02 differs: extra header bytes and per-char layout (bool, u8, u16 job, u32 exp, ...) with 0x2AD8-byte entities - do not copy. RegisterLocalPlayer uid gate (scene+0x220) agrees with project_local_player_spawn.md.

- Polarity of account_gender_flag (item gender 1 needs flag!=0; whether 1 = male is unconfirmed).
- EN class-name table row for job_branch 2 appears shifted by one (Paladin at class 0); actual 2nd-branch mapping per class unverified.

A second success 0x02 appends a second set of entities, increments scene+0x14 and restarts uids at 30000000+i, giving duplicate uids and overlapping characters. Original question: "Whether previous char-select entities are freed on a repeated 0x02 (FUN_00406fd0 / map reload may clear the scene) was not traced."

### S2C 0x5A — KeyExchangeSeed

*server → client* · key `0x5A` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 4

Locations: `0x0044D7CF` handler block (primary switch, index table idx 59); `0x0044D7E4` read i32 code_key_seed; `0x0044D7F8` CSNSocket::SetCodeKey(g_sock_game, seed); `0x0045AE40` re-init billing/cash object at game_state+0x700 (no packet reads)

```
i32 code_key_seed
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code_key_seed` | i32 | Cipher seed for the game connection; passed straight to CSNSocket::SetCodeKey so all following traffic on g_sock_game uses the keyed stream | stack local [esp+0x1D8] -> SetCodeKey(g_sock_game) at 0x44D7F8 |

**Semantics.** First packet on the game server connection. Client installs the key (SetCodeKey), re-initialises the cash/billing sub-object at gs+0x700 (stores game_state, ui root, socket, scene+0xF84, &username), computes MD5(username) as 32 hex chars into gs+0xD0A and sets scene+0x218 = 1 if it differs from the 32-char string at scene+0x131 (else 0; later drives the 'Account transfer' text in 0x02). It then sleeps 1000 ms and sends C2S 0x01 login = str[41] username (scene+0x48) + str[21] password (scene+0x101), 62 bytes after the opcode, which matches the captured 62-byte login.

**Trigger.** Server sends immediately on accepting the TCP connection to 7022 (before any client traffic). At Fireway level it must carry the NoEncode flag and be encoded with EncodebyArray since no key exists yet (per our server/memory).

**Expected response.** C2S 0x01 login: str[41] username, str[21] password (62 bytes), sent ~1 s later, encrypted with the new key. Server should answer with S2C 0x02.

**Gates / hazards.** No state gate other than the global [gs+0x408]!=0 drop. Any 0x5A received mid-session re-keys the cipher (desync unless the server re-keys identically), blocks the network thread 1 s inside the receive critical section, and re-sends login (our server ignores mid-flow 0x01).

**References.** Our GameServer._handle_fireway sends 0x5A + <i seed with NoEncode+EncodebyArray - matches. protocol.md matches (MD5, Sleep 1000, login send). PySlayer KR 0x5A handler is the same idea but the KR login it triggers carries many more fields (id + 3 more strings + 4 bytes); EN sends only username[41]+password[21].

**Open questions.**
- Origin of the 32-char string at scene+0x131 compared against MD5(username) (probably launcher/command-line supplied) was not traced; it only affects the account-transfer UI text in 0x02.

```
u8 result
if(result == 2) {
  str[33] new_id
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | ID-transfer (Yahoo/unregistered ID -> new ID) result code. 0 = ' Inexistent SS#. Do not put "_","." to register ID.'; 1 = 'You don't have any character information. Please create a character in the game and than try again.'; 2 = transfer applied (reads new_id… | stack local frame+0x79, used only as the switch index |
| `new_id` | str[33] | Transferred/new account ID, NUL-terminated inside the 33 bytes. Shown as '<new_id>Applying' on window 0x12 control 7. | stack buffer frame+0x70C (not pre-zeroed); sprintf_s(frame+0xC10, 0x40, '%s%s', new_id, 'Applying') -> FUN_004838c0 win… |

**Semantics.** Result of an account ID-transfer request made from the character-select / ID-transfer window 0x12 ('Application for a transfer ID from ID without SS#...'). Each result code opens a message box (window 0x16) with the fixed English text listed under the result field. Case 2 also reads a 33-byte ID string, sets window 0x12 control 7 to new_id followed by 'Applying', sets control 5 to state 3 (disabled) and shows 'Successfully completed ID transfer.\r\n log in with new ID \r\n transfer ID same way as before.' Case 7 sets controls 5, 6 and 7 of window 0x12 to state 3. Values above 8 do nothing and read nothing more.

**Trigger.** Reply to the client's ID-transfer request from window 0x12 (character select). The request opcode was not identified in this batch. For a private server this is legacy Yahoo-ID migration and can be left unused.

**Expected response.** None

**Gates / hazards.** No state gate. new_id MUST contain a NUL within its 33 bytes: the stack buffer is not cleared, and sprintf_s into a 64-byte buffer with '%s%s' + 'Applying' will hit the CRT invalid-parameter handler (likely a crash) if the combined string is 64 bytes or longer. Keep new_id at 32 characters or fewer. Results above 8 are silently ignored.

**References.** No PySlayer or KR equivalent (the dispatch map lists kr_source_file n/a, since the Yahoo ID transfer existed only in EN/2008). Jump table 0x458614 = [0x457AE6, 0x457B03, 0x457A60, 0x457B20, 0x457B3D, 0x457B5A, 0x457B77, 0x457B94, 0x457BE4], checked against the raw binary. S2C 0x02 (0x44DE85) carries the matching status byte (this+0x1546: 1 = '<id>Applying' with str[33], 2 = 'requesting ID transfer.', otherwise 'Account transfer possible'). Our server does not implement it.

## system_misc

### C2S 0x05 — KeepAlive

*client → server* · key `0x43E8AB/0x05` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 0

Locations: `0x43E3F0` send site; `0x43E89D` Add(u8) opcode 0x05; `0x43E8AB` Send(1); `0x44EF1D` SetTimer(hwnd, 6, 240000 ms): arms/re-arms the keepalive

```
(empty payload)
```

**Semantics.** Periodic heartbeat that keeps the game connection alive. The payload is empty and the client expects nothing back.

**Trigger.** Win32 timer id 6, repeating every 240000 ms (4 min). The S2C 0x03 (enter world / map info) handler arms it and re-arms it (resetting the interval) on every 0x03, i.e. on every map load. It is killed on logout-to-server-select and on app cleanup.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** No gate beyond the timer being active (sent inside the app critical section, whatever the UI state). Do NOT reply with S2C 0x05: per project notes that resets in-game state and kicks the client. The server may use the absence of 0x05 for more than about 4 minutes (plus slack) as an idle/dead-connection signal.

**References.** Our server _dispatch: 0x05 consumed with no reply ('client heartbeat ~4 min'), which matches the 240000 ms timer. PySlayer has no C2S 0x05 parser.

*client → server* · key `0x4414BA/0x40` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 5

Locations: `0x441460` builds and sends; `0x44146F` Add(u8) opcode 0x40; `0x44147C` Add(u8) arg1 refuse_whisper; `0x441489` Add(u8) arg2 refuse_exchange

```
u8 refuse_whisper
u8 refuse_exchange
u8 refuse_party
u8 refuse_talk
u8 refuse_friend
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `refuse_whisper` | u8 | 1 = refuse whispers (private messages), 0 = allow | COption(game_state+0x4E8 = 0x70EEE8)+0x2C committed (registry "RefuseWisper", checkbox control 0x10) |
| `refuse_exchange` | u8 | 1 = refuse trade/exchange requests | COption+0x30 ("RefuseExchange", checkbox 0x11) |
| `refuse_party` | u8 | 1 = refuse party invitations | COption+0x34 ("RefuseParty", checkbox 0x12) |
| `refuse_talk` | u8 | 1 = refuse personal (1:1) chat requests | COption+0x3C ("RefuseTalk", checkbox 0x13) |
| `refuse_friend` | u8 | 1 = refuse friend-registration requests | COption+0x38 ("RefuseFriend", checkbox 0x14) |

**Semantics.** Sends the player's five privacy 'refuse' toggles so the server can block whisper, exchange, party, personal chat and friend requests. Each value is the low byte of an i32 checkbox state (0 or 1). The wire order follows checkbox control ids 0x10..0x14, NOT the COption memory order: talk (+0x3C) comes before friend (+0x38).

**Trigger.** In the Options window (UI 0x1AD) the player toggles at least one refuse checkbox (sets COption+0x14 dirty=1) and clicks control 0xB (OK/Apply). FUN_004741a0 copies pending +0x18..+0x28 into committed +0x2C..+0x3C and sends only if at least one value changed. It then writes the registry and clears the dirty flag.

**Expected response.** none (fire-and-forget; the client updates its registry copy right away)

**Gates / hazards.** No send if dirty flag COption+0x14 == 0 or no value differs from the committed copy. The dirty flag is cleared either way. On login FUN_00474820/FUN_00473f70 load the registry values into both pending and committed copies without sending 0x40. The same five flags, in the same order, are sent at the start of C2S 0x2B enter-world (0x42F85F..0x42F8AD from game_state+0x500/+0x504/+0x508/+0x510/+0x50C), so the server gets the initial state there. Nothing to desync. The server should store the flags per character and enforce them; clients show S2C notifications such as "has refused to have a personal chat." / "has refused to register you as a friend." (SubHandler3 0x4708C0).

**References.** Not in PySlayer. Not in our server's _dispatch. Cross-check: our _handle_enter_world documents 0x2B payload bytes [0-4] as zeros; they are exactly these five refuse flags (whisper, exchange, party, talk, friend), which matches the captured 0x2B starting "00 00 00 00 00".

**Open questions.**
- Exact server-side semantics of 'RefuseTalk' vs 'RefuseWisper' (personal chat room invite vs /whisper) should be confirmed against the S2C refusal notices in SubHandler3

### S2C 0x17 — SuppressDisconnectNotice

*server → client* · key `0x17` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 0

Locations: `0x00451D7E` handler block (whole body: one MOV then break); `0x00478880` reader of game_state+0x1528: socket-close callback shows 'Connection to Server got discon…; `0x004788E0` reader: Fireway error 0x83 callback shows 'Transferring to server failed.' only if flag==0; `0x0044D4B0` reader: opcode 0x5D reason dialog skipped if flag!=0

```
stop
```

**Semantics.** Reads nothing. Sets game_state(0x70EA00)+0x1528 = 1 (absolute 0x70FF28). That flag means 'disconnect already handled'. While it is set, the client shows no disconnect dialog and does not start the 5-second WM_CLOSE timer: not on socket close (FUN_00478880), not on Fireway error 0x83 (FUN_004788e0) and not on a later 0x5D. In short: 'the server is about to drop you on purpose, don't show an error or close the game'. Every write to +0x1528 in the corpus sets it to 1. Nothing clears it, so the suppression lasts for the rest of the process.

**Trigger.** Send just before the server closes the game socket on purpose (e.g. a server/channel transfer or logout) so the client doesn't show 'Connection to Server got disconnected' and close itself 5 s later.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** No preconditions. Hazard: the flag is never reset, so after one 0x17 the client silently ignores every later disconnect, including 0x5D kicks and real network drops. It will not show a dialog or close itself. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, quest_cards_misc#18): live-verified - after an empty 0x17 the following S2C 0x5D produced NO dialog and the client did NOT exit (still in world 10 s later, normal HUD). RECOVERY: nothing clears the latch except a full client restart, so a session that has received 0x17 can never be told about a disconnect again.

**References.** Matches the KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x17: *(v3+13360)=1, same 'no payload, set flag' behaviour at the KR struct offset). Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py.

**Open questions.**
- Game_state initialisation wasn't checked to confirm +0x1528 starts at 0 (it's a static global, so it probably does). Whether a reconnect path clears it indirectly (e.g. a memset of game_state) wasn't traced.
- The exact situations where the original server sent 0x17 are unknown. Logout and server transfer are guesses from what the flag does.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | u8 | Kick reason. 1='Disconnected due to unusual game play.' 2='Disconnected due to unusual\r\ninput delay.' 3='Identified as an macro tool user,\r\nDisconnecting.' 99='Transferring to server failed.' **Semantics.** Reads a u8 reason. Calls FUN_0044d4b0 with ESI=game_state. If game_state+0x408==0 (window not already closing) and game_state+0x1528==0 (no disconnect already handled), it sets +0x1528=1 and shows the reason text in a modal message box (FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0)). The client does not close the socket itself here; the 5-second timer closes the whole game.

**Expected response.** Nothing is sent. The client shows the dialog and closes itself about 5 s later.

**Gates / hazards.** Ignored if game_state+0x408!=0 (client closing) or +0x1528!=0 (after 0x17 or an earlier disconnect notice). Only the first notice is shown. Because the game exits, don't send this for a soft error. RECOVERY: none, the client must be restarted. A preceding S2C 0x17 suppresses both the dialog and the exit.

**Open questions.**

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_type` | u8 | notice kind: 8 = current channel notice, 9 = item received; all other values are ignored by the EN client | stack local [base+0x89] |
| `channel_no` | u8 | (sub_type 8) channel number printed as 'In channel %u.' | stack local [base+0x7D], only used for the chat-log message (color 0xFFFDF34C) |
| `item_id` | u16 | (sub_type 9) item definition id (1-based index into item table *(scene+0xF84)) | stack local [base+0x9C]; selects inventory tab via itemdef+0x154 (0 consumable, 1 equip, 2 etc) |

**Semantics.** sub_type 8: prints 'In channel %u.' to the chat/system log. sub_type 9: client-side item grant - looks up the item definition; if the id is invalid nothing happens. Depending on itemdef+0x154: type 0 (consumable) is merged/stacked (max 999/slot) into the consumable tab; type 1 (equipment) inserts a single item into the first empty equip slot with zeroed 12-byte attributes (only if equip capacity scene+0x3A9 <= 45); type 2 (etc) is stacked (max 99/slot) into the etc tab; other type values abort. **Trigger.** Server-initiated notice (EN subset of the KR 0x99 GM/admin-notice family): 8 when telling the player which channel they are on, 9 when the server grants an item (quest reward / GM give / event) and wants the client to add it to its inventory.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Inventory is modified client-side only with no ack: if the tab is full (or count==0, or capacity byte > 45) the add fails silently (no message) and server/client inventories diverge; server must mirror the same stacking rules (999 consumable, 99 etc, equip 1-per-slot, 1 item per packet for equip). Invalid item_id (0 or beyond table) -> silently ignored. Unknown sub_types are safe no-ops (trailing bytes ignored).

**References.** KR Hex-Rays case 0x99 is a larger switch (5, 8, 9, 0x13 Superman mode, 0x14 Supermode, 0x2C kick, 0x2D ...); KR sub 8 is identical (u8 channel), KR sub 9 reads a bigger item struct (sub_40A010) - EN reads just u16 id + u16 count. PySlayer opcode_0x99.py only builds sub 0x13/0x14 (+u8), which the EN client ignores. Our server's tab mapping (+0x3a9 equip, +0x3aa consume, +0x3ab other) and items.json type (0 consumable, 1 equip, 2 etc) agree with the add routines. Our server: not implemented.

**Open questions.**
- Which client action (if any) solicits sub_type 8; no C2S request traced
- Exact role of the per-slot u32 array at scene+0x6F4 for consumables (passed 0 here; likely expiry/cooldown time)

```

str[17] target_name
i32 manner_delta
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gm_subcmd` | u8 | GM command selector, constant 0x0A = /manner | literal PUSH 0xA |
| `target_name` | str[17] | target character name: first whitespace-delimited token after "/manner " (sscanf %s into a zeroed 17-byte stack buffer [esp+0x24]), NUL padded | sscanf(text+8,"%s") at 0x444BAA |
| `manner_delta` | i32 | manner points to add/subtract (signed); must be non-zero or nothing is sent | sscanf(text+8+strlen(name)+1,"%d") into [esp+0x20] at 0x444BDA |

**Semantics.** GM chat command "/manner <name> <points>" typed into chat (or a chat macro). Asks the server to change the named character's manner points by the signed amount (manner points are the value at scene+0xEE0 that blocks chat/whisper/trade/room use when low). Client does nothing locally besides clearing the chat input (function returns 0).

**Trigger.** GM (local entity word +0x12 == 1) submits chat text starting with "/manner " and longer than 8 chars, with a non-empty name token and a non-zero integer second token.

**Expected response.** None awaited; fire-and-forget. No client-side follow-up state.

**Gates / hazards.** Gates in order: strlen>=1; ENGINE.DLL Curse_Engine_Clean(text) must pass (else "No cursing please"); scene+0xEE0 (own manner points) > -40 (else "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point."); scene+0xF00 == 6 (else return, nothing sent); word [[scene+0x970]+0x12] == 1 (GM flag of local player entity, filled by the u16 read at 0x44F08D in S2C 0x07) else the text goes to normal chat parsing at 0x445063; strlen > 8. Hazards: name token > 16 chars overflows the 17-byte stack buffer; the i32 local [esp+0x20] is NOT initialized on this path, so if the second token is not a number sscanf leaves stack garbage and it is sent if non-zero. Offset of the second sscanf assumes exactly one space after the name.

**References.** No C2S 0x06 parser in PySlayer (client_packets has only 03,0B,0C,0D,0F,15,1A,2B,2C,7E) and no GM-command references there. Our server's _dispatch (windslayer_server.py ~602-655) has no 0x06 branch. "/manner " string at 0x6F7BF8 is only referenced by this function.

**Open questions.**
- Server-side semantics (whether delta is added or set, and any reply packet) are not observable in the client.
- Exact meaning of scene+0xF00 == 6 (assumed in-world field scene).

```

u8 text_len
bytes[text_len] notice_text
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gm_subcmd` | u8 | GM command selector, constant 0x01 = notice/announcement. Related sites in the same function: 0x0A = /manner (site #15, 0x444C22), 0x00 = /업데이트 'update' (site #16, 0x444C7F) | literal PUSH 0x1 |
| `text_len` | u8 | (L - 4) & 0xFF, the number of text bytes that follow | MOVZX EAX,BL; SUB AL,4; PUSH EAX (EBX = caller-supplied strlen) |
| `notice_text` | bytes[text_len] | The raw line starting at byte index 4, with no NUL terminator and possibly CP949 multibyte text. Only '/not' is checked and exactly 4 bytes are skipped, so '/notice hello' sends 'ice hello' (9 bytes), '/not hello' sends ' hello' (leading space kept) and '/not… | ADD EBX,-4; PUSH EBX (N); ADD EBP,4; PUSH EBP (src = text+4) |

**Semantics.** A GM asks for a server-wide announcement. The client sends [06 01 len text...] and returns 0, which makes the chat-submit caller clear the input line. The client shows nothing locally. The server should broadcast the text as a system notice. The client has an '[Announcement] ' string at 0x6F5710 for display, but this spec does not identify which S2C packet carries it.

**Trigger.** A GM (flag word ==1 at [[scene+0x970]+0x12]) submits a chat or macro line whose first 4 bytes are '/not' and whose length is > 4. The /manner and /업데이트 checks come first.

**Expected response.** None awaited. The server presumably broadcasts an announcement S2C to all players (opcode not determined here).

**Gates / hazards.** Gates, in order: L > 0 (signed); Curse_Engine_Clean(text) passes, so the notice text itself is profanity-filtered (on failure 'No cursing please' and nothing is sent); manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40; [scene+0xF00] == 6; GM word [[scene+0x970]+0x12] == 1; not '/manner ' (8-byte strncmp); not exactly '/업데이트' (10-byte compare including NUL); strncmp(text,'/notice ',4)==0; L > 4 (unsigned JBE). Server hazards: (1) payload keeps the 'ice ' leftover when the full '/notice ' is typed, so strip it if wanted; (2) the prefix is u8 but the appended count is the full L-4. If L-4 >= 256 the prefix would wrap and a server trusting it would desync. Macro callers (L<=36) and the sprintf caller (L<=63) cannot reach that. The IME chat buffer limit was not measured, so a server should read the rest of the packet body rather than trust text_len.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: No real dispute on the wire format. Analyst A (decomp+asm) and Analyst B (asm only) gave the same grammar (u8 sub-command 0x01, u8 length (L-4), then L-4 raw bytes from text+4), the same socket (g_sock_game) and the same gates. The signatures 'u8 u8 bytes[text_len]' and 'u8 u8 bytes[msg_len]' differ only in names. The asm confirms both: 0x444CA4 strncmp(EBP,"/notice ",4); 0x444CB0 CMP EBX,4 / 0x444CB3 JBE; 0x444CC5 PUSH 6 / 0x444CC7 Add(u8); 0x444CCF PUSH 1 / 0x444CD1 Add(u8); 0x444CD9 MOVZX EAX,BL, 0x444CDC SUB AL,4, 0x444CDF Add(u8); 0x444CE7 ADD EBX,-4, 0x444CEA PUSH EBX, 0x444CEB ADD EBP,4, 0x444CEE PUSH EBP, 0x444CEF Add(char*,N) via IAT 0x4A40EC; 0x444CFD Send(1) with ECX=[0x70E6F4]. Their examples also agree: A's '/nothello'->'hello' and B's '/not hello'->' hello' both follow from the 4-byte compare and 4-byte skip. A left the sub-command, length and text Adds out of locations; B listed them. I also resolved B's open question on the length wrap as far as statics allow: EBX is the caller's strlen (0x4449DD, 0x43DBDB, 0x44AE6F), the macro and sprintf callers are bounded at 36 and 63, and only the IME chat buffer bound is still unknown. Other references: the 0x06 opcode is a GM command family in this function (06 0A <17-byte name> i32 = /manner at site #15; 06 00 = /업데이트 at site #16; 06 01 = notice). PySlayer has no client_packets parser for 0x06, and our server (windslayer_server.py) has no handling of C2S 0x06.

**Open questions.**
- Maximum length of the IME chat buffer ([0x70E708]+0x104), which decides whether text_len can wrap past 255 for typed input. Macro and sprintf callers cannot.
- Whether the original server stripped the 'ice ' leftover or GMs typed '/not <text>'. The 4-byte compare of an 8-byte literal looks like a leftover from a Korean command string.
- Which S2C opcode the server used to broadcast the announcement (the '[Announcement] ' prefix at 0x6F5710).

The asm settles the order and widths. Add(u8 0x6E) at 0x473579. Add(uint EDI=FUN_004832b0(0x434)) at 0x473585 through IAT 0x4A40F0. PUSH 0x11 and LEA ECX,[ESP+0x18] (the name at [ESP+0x14] after one push), then Add(char*,17) at 0x473591. MOV EDX,[ESP+0x10] (fee) and Add(uint) at 0x47359F. PUSH MOVZX [ESP+0xC] and LEA EAX,[ESP+0x2C] (content at [ESP+0x28] after one push), then Add(char*,len) at 0x4735C6. The content has no NUL and is not padded, so bytes[content_len] is the accurate DSL. On side details A is more correct than B: category +0xD8 is set to 0 at messenger init (0x46F976), so it is not uninitialised, only stale across reports; and the reply exists as S2C 0x95 (0x471DA3: u8 result, and on 1 a u64 gold into info+0x228), which B marked unknown. game_system is set to admin_gm because this is a GM moderation report, even though CMessenger builds it. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.

```
u16 quest_id
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quest_id` | u16 | Quest index into the client's hs/windslayer.hqi quest table (1-based). 0 or unknown id = packet ignored after the read. | local [esp+0x10]; then written into first empty active slot char+0x256+2*i (char=[ctx+0x18], ctx=game+0xD2C) or into co… |

**Semantics.** Quest-accept result. After reading quest_id the client looks up the quest record (FUN_0040a840). If the record is null, nothing happens (the handler still returns 'handled'). Otherwise: (a) If record.Money(+0xDE8, i32) >= 0 AND record.Demand_id[0](+0xD0C) == 0 AND record.ReqPro(+0xDF8) == 0 (a quest with no requirements), the quest is NOT put in the active log. FUN_004264a0 adds it to the completed-quest list instead (char+0x262 u16[85] plus count bytes char+0x30C: a new entry gets count 1, an existing one gets count+1 capped at 99, and a full list is shifted left before appending). (b) Otherwise the quest goes into the first active slot i (0..2) whose u16 id at char+0x256+2i is 0. The client writes the id and clears the ready flag at char+0x25F+i. The progress byte at char+0x25C+i is NOT reset. There is no duplicate check, and if all 3 slots are full nothing is stored and there is no message. In both cases the client then grants the quest's Send items itself: for i=0..9, stopping at the first zero id at record+0xC94+4i, it calls FUN_00440920(ctx+4, id, 0, count=record+0xD34+4i). That adds the item to the bag and prints "you've received %s. (Count:%u)" (or "You've learned skill(%s)." for type-3 items). Finally it refreshes the quest window (FUN_00478380). Quest record layout (confirmed from hqi loader FUN_00409FE0): +4 name, +0xC94 Send ids[10], +0xCBC Reward ids[20], +0xD0C Demand ids[10], +0xD34 Send_Num[10], +0xD5C Reward_Num[20], +0xDAC Demand_Num[10], +0xDE4 Exp, +0xDE8 Money, +0xDF4 Repeat, +0xDF8 ReqPro, +0xE08 SNPC, +0xE0C ENPC.

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x16 AcceptQuest (u16 quest_id, send site 0x477330). The client sends it only after checking that an active slot is free ("You can only take 3 quests at a time...") and that the bag has room for the Send items. The client does not add the quest optimistically; it waits for this packet.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Returns without reading if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null (the sub-handler chain then continues). Hazards: (1) Sending 0x26 twice for the same quest fills two active slots. (2) The client grants the hqi Send items ITSELF, so a server that also sends S2C 0x18 GetItem for those items (0x18's handler at 0x46DEDE calls the same FUN_00440920) duplicates them in the client bag. (3) A no-requirement quest (Money>=0, no Demand, ReqPro==0) goes straight to the completed list, so the server must not expect it to be active. The client's turn-in code (FUN_00477af0) only turns in quests that are in active slots. (4) The client's slot choice is the first empty slot, so the server's slot numbering for 0x59 must copy that rule exactly. It was NOT reproduced in two later sessions with the identical packet, so treat it as an unexplained termination risk rather than a rule; recovery is a restart.

Live capture: accepting quest 26 got S2C 0x26 with a 2-byte body, with no desync. Disagreement: reference_gamedef_db.md says 'EN client has NO live quest granted opcode'. That is wrong; this is that opcode. ### S2C 0x27 — QuestCompleted

*server → client* · key `0x27` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 2

Locations: `0x0047785C` handler block (case 0x27); `0x0047786E` GetDataFromPacket u16 quest_id (IAT 0x4A4090); `0x004264A0` add/increment completed-quest list entry; `0x004659D0` refresh gold label (%I64u)

```
u16 quest_id
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quest_id` | u16 | Quest being completed. It must exist in the client's quest table or the packet is a no-op. All rewards come from the client's local hqi record, not from the packet. | local [esp+0x10] |

**Semantics.** Quest turn-in result. The client applies all of the completion bookkeeping itself, from its local quest record: 1. Look up the record; if null, return. 2. Clear every active slot whose id == quest_id (id=0, progress byte char+0x25C+i = 0). 3. FUN_004264a0: add quest_id to the completed list char+0x262 (count 1, or count+1 capped at 99). 4. If record.Money (+0xDE8, i32) != 0: gold64 at char+0x228/0x22C += sign-extended Money, and the gold label is refreshed. If Money < 0 the chat shows "Gave %u Gold." (color 0xFFFD4C87); otherwise "You've received %u Gold." (0xFF00C800). 5. For i=0..9 while Demand_id[i] (+0xD0C+4i) != 0: look up the item in the item table at [ctx+4]+0x4D4. If found, call FUN_00467140(type=item+0x154, inv=[ctx+4]+0xD5C, u16 id, 0, u16 count=+0xDAC+4i) to remove it from the bag (types 0/1/2 only). On success, chat "Gave %u item(%s)." and refresh the inventory UI (FUN_00465290). 6. For i=0..19 while Reward_id[i] (+0xCBC+4i) != 0: FUN_00440920(ctx+4, id, 0, count=+0xD5C+4i) grants the item ("you've received %s. (Count:%u)" / skill learned). 7. Refresh the quest window and the NPC quest-dialog list. EXP (+0xDE4) is NOT applied here; the server must send it separately (S2C 0x21).

**Trigger.** Reply to C2S 0x17 TurnInQuest (u16 quest_id), sent by FUN_00477af0 when talking to the quest's ENPC (+0xE0C). The client checks Money/gold, progress >= ReqPro, Demand items present and reward bag space ("There isn't empty space in the inventory.") before sending.

**Expected response.** none (server should follow with S2C 0x21 exp if the quest gives exp)

**Gates / hazards.** Skipped if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null. An unknown quest_id is a silent no-op. The client does NOT check that the quest was active, so sending 0x27 for a non-active quest still adds gold, removes Demand items, grants Rewards and bumps the completion count. Double-sending doubles rewards. Duplication hazard: the client already adds Money and Reward items and removes Demand items locally. A server that also sends S2C 0x18 GetItem for the rewards (the 0x18 handler calls the same FUN_00440920) duplicates reward items in the client bag. Gold can stay consistent if 0x18 carries an absolute gold total. Gold is not clamped, so negative Money can underflow the u64 if the server skips the gold check. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C21, quest_cards_misc#11): live-confirmed that double-sending re-grants the items and gold and bumps the completion count again; the one exception is a type-3 skill reward that is already learned, which prints nothing the second time. Duplicate 0x27s duplicate items, gold and completion count - not skills.

**References.** No PySlayer builder. Our server's _send_quest_complete packs '<H' quest_id, which matches the wire format. However: (a) our server fires it from C2S 0x16 (treated as accept OR turn-in), while the real client sends turn-in as C2S 0x17 (send site 0x477F15), which our _dispatch does not handle, so real NPC turn-ins get no reply; (b) _complete_quest also sends 0x18 per reward item (plus gold_gain), likely duplicating the client-side hqi Reward grant (PLAUSIBLE; depends on EN hqi Reward columns matching the KR gamedef).

**Open questions.**
- Whether EN hqi Reward/Money/Demand values match the KR gamedef.sqlite3 rows (item-id drift like 377->179), which determines what the client grants locally.
- Whether the original server sent 0x18 inventory syncs after 0x27, or relied solely on the client-side grant.

### S2C 0x59 — QuestProgressUpdate

*server → client* · key `0x59` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 2 (1 if slot >= 4, when the rest is ignored)

Locations: `0x004776AF` handler block (case 0x59); `0x004776C7` GetDataFromPacket u8 slot (IAT 0x4A4094 via EBX); `0x004776F2` GetDataFromPacket u8 progress, read directly into char+0x25B+slot; `0x00426500` quest completion-condition check (Money vs gold, ReqPro vs progress, Demand items in bag)

```
u8 slot
if(slot < 4) {
  u8 progress
} else {
  stop
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | u8 | 1-based active-quest slot (1..3), the index into char+0x256 u16[3]. Checked with a SIGNED test slot-1 < 3, so 0 is also accepted (hazard). A value of 4 or more ends reading with no UI refresh. | local [esp+0x10] |
| `progress` | u8 | Absolute progress counter for that slot (e.g. kill count), compared against quest record ReqPro (+0xDF8) and shown in the active-quest tab as progress/ReqPro. | char+0x25B+slot, i.e. char+0x25C..0x25E progress[slot-1] (char=[ctx+0x18]) |

**Semantics.** Updates one active quest's progress counter. The byte goes straight into char+0x25B+slot. Then, if that slot's ready flag at char+0x25E+slot is 0 and the quest record for the slot's quest id (u16 at char+0x254+2*slot) exists, the client calls FUN_00426500(ctx+0x10, record, progress, gold64 at char+0x228, bag arrays...). That function returns 1 when all of these hold: (Money >= 0, or gold >= \|Money\|), (ReqPro == 0, or progress >= ReqPro), and every Demand item (up to 10; types 0 and 2 counted in the bags, type 1 via FUN_00424df0, type 5 skipped) is present in sufficient count. On success the client sets the ready flag to 1 and prints "[<quest name>] You are ready to complete the quest." in green. The message appears once, because the flag suppresses repeats. The quest window is refreshed whenever slot <= 3. The ready flag only controls the message; the turn-in logic re-checks the conditions itself.

**Trigger.** Server sends it whenever a tracked quest counter changes, e.g. a monster kill counted toward ReqPro. It can also be sent with an unchanged value to re-evaluate readiness.

**Expected response.** none (the player then talks to the ENPC, which sends C2S 0x17 turn-in)

**Gates / hazards.** Skipped entirely if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null. slot=0 passes the signed check and writes progress into char+0x25B, the HIGH byte of active slot 3's quest id (u16 at 0x25A). That corrupts the quest log, and the client then reads a garbage quest id from char+0x254. Only send slot 1..3. Progress is a u8 (max 255). The slot must match the client's own placement: 0x26 fills the first empty slot, and 0x27/0x38 empty the slot.

**References.** PySlayer opcode_59: p8(random slot) + p8u(unk), which agrees on 2 bytes. Its comment 'v47 - 1 < 5' suggests the newer KR build has 5 slots; EN checks < 3. Our server's _send_quest_progress packs '<BB' slot(1..3), count, which matches. It assigns slots lowest-free in _quest_assign_slot, the same rule as the client.

**Open questions.**
- Which game events the original server counted into progress: ReqPro with the NPC field at +0xDFC, possibly a target monster id. Not decidable from this handler.

### C2S 0x2E — DeathReviveRequest

*client → server* · key `0x4484CC/0x2E` · confidence **high** · adjudicated · server: **missing** · length: 0

Locations: `0x446ABB` control id == 0 -> ignore (the only check before per-window dispatch); `0x446AE6` window byte table 0x44BA54[0x78] = 24 -> jump table 0x44B9EC -> 0x44A674 (window 0x79); `0x44A67C` Add(u8) opcode 0x2E, JMP 0x4484C4; `0x4484CC` Send(1) on g_sock_game

```
(empty payload)
```

**Semantics.** Bare opcode, no body. It is sent when any control on window 0x79 is clicked. S2C 0x3E opens that window and puts the local player into motion state 0xD. State 0xD is the death state: FUN_0041A230 sets it together with the dying flag and the exp-loss calculation. So window 0x79 is the death dialog and 0x2E asks the server to revive or return the player. The handler never checks which control was clicked, so every button sends the same packet.

**Trigger.** Clicking any nonzero control on window 0x79 (the death dialog opened by S2C 0x3E).

**Expected response.** Probably a map (re)load: S2C 0x08 hides window 0x79 outside arenas, then the spawn/enter sequence. Not verified for EN. This is a different packet from the S2C 0x2E map/channel enter. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, combat_skill#21): the client sends this the moment the death dialog's only button is clicked and closes the dialog itself, so the server MUST answer with the revive sequence (HP via S2C 0x28/0x44 plus the map-enter sequence S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07) - otherwise the player stays dead with no UI and no way to retry.

**Gates / hazards.** No client-side gate beyond control id != 0. The handler ignores the control id, so a multi-button dialog cannot tell the server which choice was made. Window 0x79 stays open until the server sends something that hides it (S2C 0x08 outside arena), so the player can click repeatedly and send duplicates.

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree the body is empty. Add(u8 0x2E) at 0x44A67C goes directly to JMP 0x4484C4 and Send(1), with no other Add. A's grammar "" and B's "stop" both mean zero bytes. The correct grammar is empty (length 0). On naming: A's 'revive request' is supported by more evidence than B's generic 'Window79Confirm'. The value S2C 0x3E writes (+0x94C = 0xD) is also written by FUN_0041A230 @0x41A283, right next to the dying flag (+0x1388 = 1) and the per-level exp-penalty code, so 0x79 is the death dialog. A's cross-reference 'PySlayer answers respawn with S2C 0x2E' is for the other direction and a newer KR build; do not assume a server reply opcode from it. Our server has no C2S 0x2E branch in _dispatch.

**Open questions.**
- Whether the server should revive in place or send the player to town. The client sends no choice.
- Which S2C sequence the original server sent in reply (0x08 map reload is the most likely, since it hides window 0x79).

*server → client* · key `0x28` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 2

```
u16 hp
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hp` | u16 | New ABSOLUTE current HP of the local player (not a delta) | zero-extended into (*(scene+0x970))+0x9C (local-player entity cur HP, i32). scene = [game_state+0x4CC] = [0x70EECC] |

**Semantics.** Reads one u16 (IAT 0x4A4090, stack local [esp+0xE8]). If the local-player entity pointer [scene+0x970] is non-null, writes movzx(hp) to entity+0x9C. Then always calls FUN_00443690 (ESI=game_state): if the local entity exists, sprintf("%d/%d", +0x9C, +0x110C max HP) into HUD text slot 6 (FUN_004838c0(6)); if max HP (+0x110C) != 0 it sets HP globe fill ratio (FUN_004891e0(2, cur/max, 2)) and a HUD state FUN_00489320(2,1, ratio>0.2 ? 3 : 0) (low-HP indicator). No effect, no sound, no reply.

**Expected response.** none

Handler does not trigger death at 0; however the entity-update loop (FUN_00413920, action 2/0x11 end) calls FUN_0041a230 when +0x9C < 1, so hp=0 can start client-side death flow later. HUD ratio skipped if max HP (+0x110C, set by 0x07) is 0.

**References.** PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x28.py (setHp, single p16u) matches EN exactly. The newer KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x28) is DIFFERENT: u8 subtype (1=HP,2=MP,3=...) + u16 + i32 max etc. - do not port that. Our server _send_hp (windslayer_server.py:1566) struct '<H' matches; used at enter-world (732), item use (1180), map change (1265). Memory note 'player needs 0x28/0x44 on spawn' consistent.

### S2C 0x29 — EntityDie

*server → client* · key `0x29` · confidence **medium** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 16 (client consumes only 4 if uid not found)

Locations: `0x00454D46` handler block; `0x00454D5B` GetDataFromPacket u32 uid; `0x00454D6F` entity lookup by uid; `0x00454D8C` action=0x10 dying

```
u32 uid
if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) {
  stop
}
u32 respawn_tick
u32 respawn_x
u32 respawn_y
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | entity (player or monster) that dies; looked up via FUN_004189f0 in scene list; unknown => stop | stack local [esp+0x1FC] |
| `respawn_tick` | u32 | absolute respawn deadline on the client scene clock scene+0xF1C (advanced +0x1E per logic tick in FUN_00417e10, reset to 0 by FUN_0042c360/FUN_00428090). Local player auto-respawns when (int)(respawn_tick - clock) < 0 | read DIRECTLY into entity+0xE5C (ulong&) |
| `respawn_x` | u32 | respawn/home X; converted unsigned->f64 | stack [esp+0x1EC] -> f64 entity+0x1318 |
| `respawn_y` | u32 | respawn/home Y; converted unsigned->f64 | stack [esp+0x20C] -> f64 entity+0x1320 |

**Semantics.** Starts the death sequence for any entity. After a successful lookup and BEFORE reading the rest, the handler sets entity+0x8E2=0, +0x8E4=0, action +0x904=0x10 (dying), action timer +0xE00=0, and +0x8CF=8. Then reads respawn_tick into +0xE5C and x/y (FILD + 2^32 fixup = unsigned) into f64 +0x1318/+0x1320. The entity update loop (FUN_00413920) plays the death animation in action 0x10, then switches to 0x16 (dead). In 0x16, for TYPE-4 TEMPLATE entities (+0x98 == 4) once (int)(+0xE5C - scene+0xF1C) < 0 the client itself respawns: LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C16, combat_skill#00/#16/#19, world_movement_npc#22) - the LOCAL player is type 3, not type 4, so this branch is NOT the local-player path. That client-side revive also clears the WHOLE buff table, including the 0xB3B render entry a monster needs in order to be drawn, and resets HP to the entity TEMPLATE max (5 for a Pupu), not to the value the server last sent. Details of the revive: posX(+0x11F8)=+0x1318, posY(+0x1288)=+0x1320, action=8 idle, HP=max(+0x110C), MP=max(+0x1110), clears buff arrays. For monsters +0x1318 is also the home position used by the leash check (FUN_00417e10: \|posX-homeX\|>600 sets return flag +0xDBC). HP is NOT set to 0 by this packet.

**Trigger.** Server-side death of a monster or player (HP reached 0).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Unknown uid => no-op. Re-sending for an already dead entity restarts the dying animation (action forced to 0x10). For the local player, respawn_tick=0 (or any value that makes the signed difference negative) causes an immediate client-side respawn at (respawn_x, respawn_y) with full HP/MP as soon as the death animation ends - sending x=y=0 teleports the player to (0,0). A large positive value (e.g. 0x7FFFFFFF) should keep the local player dead until the server respawns it (e.g. via 0x07) - inferred from the signed compare. The server cannot observe scene+0xF1C, so precise timed respawn is not possible. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C16b, combat_skill#19): for the LOCAL player the documented self-respawn does NOT fire, even with respawn_tick = 0 - the player plays the death sequence and stays dead indefinitely (input ignored, no auto-revive after 15 s, HP untouched in memory). HAZARD: a 0x29 aimed at the local player is effectively a permanent death. RECOVERY: the server must revive explicitly (HP via 0x28/0x44 plus a map/spawn sequence, or a fresh 0x07); otherwise only a client restart. Re-derive the revive gate before using 0x29 as a revive path.

**References.** Our server _build_opcode_29 (windslayer_server.py:1937) sends u32 uid + 3 u32 (named anim/dx/dz, all 0) = 16 bytes: layout correct, field names wrong (they are respawn_tick / respawn_x / respawn_y); used for monster death (works). PySlayer opcode_0x29.py sends only 3 random u32 (12 bytes) - one u32 short for EN. KR Hex-Rays case 0x29 has same structure (uid, then +1388 timer, then two u32) with different struct offsets and action 23. Memory reference_combat_model.md 'death=0x29' consistent.

**Open questions.**
- Exact tick unit of scene+0xF1C in real time (0x1E per logic tick; tick rate not verified).
- Behaviour of remote-player entities in action 0x16 depends on room/arena globals (scene+0xF88+0x70, scene+0xF24); not needed for wire format.
- Local-player revive gate: with respawn_tick = 0 the documented (int)(+0xE5C - scene+0xF1C) < 0 branch did not fire (combat_skill#19). Is the comparison unsigned, or is there an extra gate (+0x98 == 4, HP == 0, action 0x16 dwell time)? Re-derive before using 0x29 to revive.

**Expected response.** The client sends C2S 0x2E (1 byte, opcode only) when the player clicks a button in the death dialog (window 0x79), most likely return-to-village/revive. The client has a 'Village transfer failed' message box string for a failure reply.

**Gates / hazards.** - There is NO null check on the local player pointer scene+0x970. Sending it before the local player is registered (lobby/login/loading) dereferences null and crashes. - Sending it again re-applies death processing (HP 0, buffs cleared). - It also needs this+0x4CC (scene) to be valid. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, combat_skill#20/#21): the death dialog (window 0x79) has a SINGLE button ("Revived"); clicking it closes the dialog CLIENT-SIDE immediately and sends C2S 0x2E (0 bytes) without waiting for the server. HAZARD: if the server does not answer, the player is left dead with no UI at all and no way to ask again. RECOVERY: the server must answer C2S 0x2E with the revive/warp sequence (HP via 0x28/0x44 plus 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07, or a fresh spawn).

**References.** - The dispatch map lists the KR source file as Packet_handler_4; this opcode is not in the KR main-handler Hex-Rays. - Our server uses S2C 0x29 (_build_opcode_29 / _send_death) for death, which targets a uid and sets state 0x10 on that entity. 0x3E is the local-player-only variant that also opens the death dialog. - The client has the string 'Revival in 20 seconds.' (FUN_00458640), shown when the local player is downed in some modes.

**Open questions.**
- The exact title/buttons of window 0x79. It is inferred to be the death/return dialog from action 0xD = death, map-change closing it, and every button sending C2S 0x2E.
- What C2S 0x2E expects in reply (a village transfer via S2C 0x08/0x03 map change?).

*server → client* · key `0x40` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 4 if uid not found (client stops); else 6 + 2*(has_hp!=0) + 2*(has_mp!=0) (6..10)

Locations: `0x00454AF2` handler block; `0x00454B07` GetDataFromPacket u32 uid; `0x00454B1B` entity lookup by uid; `0x00454B41` GetDataFromPacket bool has_hp

```
u32 uid
if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) {
  stop
}
bool has_hp
bool has_mp
if(has_hp != 0) {
  u16 hp
}
if(has_mp != 0) {
  u16 mp
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | target entity uid (entity+0x84); looked up in scene entity list (scene+0xC) via FUN_004189f0; uid 0 or unknown => handler stops | stack local [esp+0x1E4]; entity ptr saved at [esp+0x20] |
| `has_hp` | bool | nonzero = HP value follows | stack local [esp+0x97] |
| `has_mp` | bool | nonzero = MP value follows | stack local [esp+0x47] |
| `hp` | u16 | new ABSOLUTE HP; APPLIED ONLY if uid == local uid [scene+0x220] (written to (*(scene+0x970))+0x9C + HUD refresh). For any other entity the value is read and DISCARDED (remote entity +0x9C is NOT updated) | (*(scene+0x970))+0x9C when local, else dropped |
| `mp` | u16 | new ABSOLUTE MP; applied only if uid is the local player (+0xA0 + HUD refresh), otherwise discarded | (*(scene+0x970))+0xA0 when local, else dropped |

**Semantics.** Broadcast-style 'entity recovered HP/MP' with visuals. Exact flow: read uid; entity=FUN_004189f0(scene, uid); if null -> stop. Read both bools. (a) if has_hp: read hp; if entity uid == [scene+0x220]: write local +0x9C, FUN_00443690. If has_hp && !has_mp: effect FUN_0042b580(0x37, entity uid, 0,0,0,1,10,0) + positional Play_Sound(0x37, entity+0x15A4, entity+0x15A8, game_state+0x1044..+0x1050, 0) (IAT 0x4A42F8). (b) if has_mp: read mp; if local: write +0xA0, FUN_00443780; effect FUN_0042b580(0x58, uid=[scene+0x220] i.e. the LOCAL player's uid regardless of target - client quirk, identical in the relay copy FUN_00458640), positional Play_Sound(0x58) at the target entity. (c) ALWAYS (entity found, any bool combo incl. both 0): effect FUN_0042b580(0x54, entity uid, ...) + positional Play_Sound(0x54) at the entity. When both bools are set the 0x37 effect is skipped (only 0x58 + 0x54). Effects 0x54+0x37 are exactly what the client plays locally for heal skills 0x1F5..0x1FF (0x453CAA), so 0x40 is a heal/recover visual, not a hurt flinch.

**Trigger.** Server announces that an entity (another player, or the local player) was healed / used a recovery item, so nearby clients show the heal effect; for the local uid it also sets HP/MP.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Unknown uid => only 4 bytes consumed, nothing happens. Remote entity HP/MP are NOT changed by this packet (use 0x54/0x14/0x1A for remote bars). Every packet mallocs 1-2 effect entries and plays 1-2 positional sounds - sending it per combat hit caused the observed hitch. MP branch effect always lands on the local player sprite even when target is remote.

**References.** Our server _build_opcode_40 (windslayer_server.py:1894) byte layout u32\|bool\|bool\|[u16]\|[u16] is CORRECT, but it is never sent; its docstring calls 0x37 a 'got-hit react sound' and omits the unconditional 0x54 effect. Memory reference_combat_model.md calls 0x40 'flinch+sound' / 'hurt' - binary evidence says heal/recover visual (same ids as heal skills), and remote HP is not written. KR Hex-Rays case 0x40 has the same wire layout but writes HP to the TARGET entity and returns without the extra effect; KR effect ids differ (0x2D/0x2F). PySlayer has no opcode_0x40 builder.

**Open questions.**
- Visual/sound asset names for ids 0x37, 0x54, 0x58 unresolved (inferred HP-recover, heal-cast, MP-recover).
- Whether the effect-0x58-on-local-uid quirk is intentional cannot be determined statically.
