The client sends its current input bytes and event state plus the logic time elapsed since the last send; remote clients simulate the movement from these. Position is included only in the interaction-event block. No state is changed from the server side. On the client, after sending, scene+0x24C = scene+0xF1C; the previous-input snapshot (player+0x8B7..0x8BA = 0x8B3..0x8B6) is updated every tick whether or not a packet is sent. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C12, world_movement_npc#00/#01 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): (a) For the LOCAL player a bad (IP-octet) seed in the spawn record does NOT produce a ~28-packet stream: the client resets +0x8B3/+0x8B4/+0x8B5/+0x904 from real input immediately, and only +0x8B6 = 1 survives ~1.5 s after a map-change 0x07 (7 non-idle sends). After a spawn the client emits a burst of about 5 idle 0x0D, so a server sanity check should allow <= 5, not <= 2. The idle-default rule still matters for the REMOTE records in S2C 0x04/0x05/0x07 and for 0x1A. (b) A basic melee swing is lo bits 2-4 (+0x8B4) = 1 with +0x904 = 4 - NOT an action_event: +0x94C stays 0 for a plain attack, so the 22-byte event_source_uid form is never produced by one. +0x8B4 values: 0 idle, 1 basic attack, 3 jump, 4 down/portal/drop-through. Bits 20-21 (+0x8D0) and hi bits 0-11 (+0x958) are live during jumps. (c) The interact tail for interact_event 0xC is confirmed at 45 bytes: u32 target_uid, f64 pos_x, f64 pos_y, f64 dx, f64 dy, bool, bool, u32 timer, u8 action_event (= 9), u16 item_id.

**Trigger.** Checked every 30 ms logic tick from FUN_0042b260 (possibly several times per rendered frame during catch-up), when scene+0xF00 == 6 (in world), [0x70EED8]+0x70 == 0 (not a P2P room), and player (scene+0x970) != 0. (1) Sends at once if any of player+0x8B3..0x8B6 changed since the last tick, or player+0x950 != 0, or player+0x94C != 0 (also sets scene+0x250 = 1). (2) Otherwise nothing if logic_elapsed < 210 ms. (3) If not idle (idle means 0x904 == 8, 0x8B3 == 8, and 0x8B4, 0x8B5, 0x8B6 all 0), sets scene+0x250 = 1 and sends about every 210 ms. (4) If idle and scene+0x250 != 0, clears it and sends one final packet. (5) If idle otherwise, sends only when logic_elapsed >= 15000 (keepalive).

**Expected response.** Nothing to the sender. It must NOT be echoed back: echoing desynced the cipher, per memory. For multiplayer the server should relay to other players on the map as S2C 0x1B (handler 0x4523F9: u32 uid, u32, bytes[8] state, if(ae) u32, if(vb==4 && ae in {9,7}) f64 f64, if(ie) f64 f64). The 0x1B conditional tail is NOT the same as 0x0D's, so the relay must re-encode rather than copy the bytes.

**Gates / hazards.** Variable length: the server must parse the conditional tails using bits of the packet itself. The client tests the full ints (player+0x94C, +0x950, byte +0x8B6), but the packet carries only 4/4/3 bits of them. The equivalence holds only if those values fit (all observed writers use values <= 0xD). The upper 10 bits of state_lo and upper 20 bits of state_hi are stale garbage and must be ignored (capture: 53 40 / 60 64 75). Not sent in P2P room mode ([map]+0x70 == 1), which appears to use a UDP path instead (FUN_0042c450, not traced).

**References.** Capture '00 00 00 00 65 00 1E 00 00 00 00 02 40 53 00 60 64 75' decodes exactly: realtime_delta 0, map 101, elapsed 30, state_lo 0x53400200 (0x8B6=1, other fields 0, garbage high bits), state_hi 0x75646000 (0x958&0xFFF = 0), 18 bytes, no tails. PySlayer parse_0D agrees on offsets (payload[5:7] u16 'sub_opcode' = map code; payload[7:9] == 0xD2 = elapsed 210; keycode payload[0x0B] = first state byte). Our server's _handle_world_sync docstring wrongly says the payload 'begins with two f64 world coords': positions appear only in the interact_event tail. The memory atlas note calling 0x0D a 'heartbeat' is wrong (it is S2C 0x0D in sub_handler_3, a different message).

**Open questions.**
- Exact meaning of player+0x8B4/0x8B5/0x8B6/0x8D0 values and of action_event (0x94C, values 1..13 seen) and interact_event (0x950, values 1, 9, 0xB, 0xC seen).
- Meaning of f64_1338/f64_1340, flag_8db, flag_8e7, timer_dac; appears related to item/PvP contact mechanics.
- Meaning of the second u32 in the S2C 0x1B relay (probably logic_elapsed_ms) and whether the relay should carry the 0x0D realtime_delta.
- Whether scene+0xF1C can be resynced by the server (FUN_0042c360 writes it at 0x42C3BF), which would affect logic_elapsed.
- Which action actually produces the 22-byte event_source_uid tail? Live (world_movement_npc#00) proved +0x94C stays 0 for a basic attack, so the tail must come from skills or grabs; the 45-byte interact-0xC tail is already confirmed.

### S2C 0x1B — EntityActionCommand

*server → client* · key `0x1B` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 16 base (uid 4 + hold 4 + blob 8); +4 if action!=0; +16 more if action in {7,9} and sub_b==4; +16 if move_flag!=0. Max 52. Only 4 bytes are consumed if the uid is unknown.

Locations: `0x004523F9` handler block; `0x00452422` FUN_004189f0(uid, scene): find entity in scene list; break if not found; `0x0045248D` GetDataFromPacket(char*,8) into scene+0xEF8 state blob, then bit-decoded into cmd; `0x0045263E` FUN_00459df0: append the 0x58-byte cmd to the entity+0x1350 command queue

```
u32 uid
if(no entity with uid in scene list) {
  stop
}
u32 hold_ms
bytes[8] state_blob
if(((state_blob_u32_0 >> 12) & 0xF) != 0) {
  u32 target_uid
  if((((state_blob_u32_0 >> 9) & 0x7) == 4) && ((((state_blob_u32_0 >> 12) & 0xF) == 7) || (((state_blob_u32_0 >> 12) & 0xF) == 9))) {
    f64 target_x
    f64 target_y
  }
}
if(((state_blob_u32_0 >> 16) & 0xF) != 0) {
  f64 pos_x
  f64 pos_y
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | Target entity uid (remote player or monster). If no entity in the scene+0xC list has it, the handler stops reading. | stack [base+0x210] -> FUN_004189f0 lookup |
| `hold_ms` | u32 | Command timing. Monsters (+0x98==4): when dequeued it goes into entity+0xE48 and counts down 30 per tick before the next queued command is popped, so it's how long this action lasts. Remote players (+0x98==3): it's a delay before the command applies (0 means … | cmd+0x00 -> entity+0xE48 |
| `state_blob` | bytes[8] | Packed state, read as u32 b0 (bytes 0-3) and u32 b1 (bytes 4-7), little-endian. b0 bits 0-1 facing: 1->2, 2->6, 0/3->8 (cmd+0x4A -> entity+0x8B3). b0 bits 2-4 motion (cmd+0x4B -> +0x8B4). b0 bits 5-8 motion_8b5 (cmd+0x4C -> +0x8B5, players only). b0 bits 9-11… | scene(game_state+0x4CC)+0xEF8..0xEFF, decoded to cmd+0x44/+0x4A..+0x50 |
| `target_uid` | u32 | Present only if action!=0. Uid of the action target. | cmd+0x08 -> entity+0xD80 (0 when absent) |
| `target_x` | f64 | Present only if action!=0 and sub_b==4 and action is 7 or 9. Target point X (e.g. a ground-targeted skill). | cmd+0x30 -> entity+0x1338 (players) |
| `target_y` | f64 | Target point Y (same condition as target_x). | cmd+0x38 -> entity+0x1340 (players) |
| `pos_x` | f64 | Present only if move_flag!=0. Position X the entity snaps to when the command is applied (non-monster entities only). | cmd+0x10 -> entity+0x11F8 |
| `pos_y` | f64 | Position Y (same condition). | cmd+0x18 -> entity+0x1288 |

**Semantics.** Queues a movement/action command on an existing entity. The client allocates a zeroed 0x58-byte command, sets entity+0x8D7=1, reads hold_ms and the 8-byte state blob, bit-decodes the blob into the command, and reads the optional target and position fields. It forces cmd+0x04=0 and appends the command to the entity's FIFO at +0x1350 (FUN_00459df0). FUN_00412100 consumes the queue once per tick for entities with +0x98>2 and uid != local uid (and only while scene+0xF88+0x70==0). When +0xE48 reaches 0 it pops the head. Monsters (type 4): +0xE48 = hold_ms. Other entities: if move_flag is set, pos goes to +0x11F8/+0x1288 and cmd+0x40 to +0xDAC. Then for everyone: +0x8B4 = motion, +0x8B3 = facing. Players only (type 3): +0x8B5, +0x8B6, +0x8EA/+0x950 = move_flag, +0xD78 = 0, +0x1328/+0x1330 = 0, +0x1338/+0x1340 = target point, +0x8DB, +0x8E8, +0x8D4 and +0x8E7 from unset cmd bytes (0). Finally for everyone: +0x94C = action, +0xD80 = target_uid, +0x958 = param12, +0x8FF = 0, +0x8D0 = facing2. This is the server-side echo of another client's C2S 0x0D movement packet (FUN_0042c940 packs the same blob from the same entity fields), and it's also the way to drive monster actions from the server. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#23/#24): a type-3 remote entity advances physics ONLY while entity+0xE48 > 0, i.e. while a node is pending. A single walk node with nothing queued behind it sets +0x8B3 2 but does not move the entity; each new node moves it for ~210 ms using the PREVIOUS node's facing. A relay must therefore STREAM 0x1B continuously - one node per received C2S 0x0D with hold_ms = that packet's logic_elapsed_ms. Measured stop-node latency behind a pending walk: 1.08 s. For an immediate stop use 0x2A.

**Trigger.** The server relays another player's C2S 0x0D movement/action to nearby clients (turning its state into uid + hold + blob + optional target/pos), and sends server-driven monster AI actions (move/attack) for mobs spawned with server_controlled=1.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Unknown uid: only the 4-byte uid is consumed and the rest is ignored (safe). Commands sent for the LOCAL player's uid are queued but never consumed (FUN_00412100 skips uid==scene+0x220), so they leak memory. Commands for monsters don't apply pos_x/pos_y directly (type-4 branch only sets +0xE48). Movement must come from motion/facing plus the client's physics, or the position is ignored. The blob overwrites scene+0xEF8, which the local client reuses for its own 0x0D. The bits the client doesn't recompute (b0 bits 22-31, b1 bits 12-31) will echo back in the next C2S 0x0D. If you queue many commands with large hold_ms, the backlog stays until the entity is removed. The client needs entity+0xE48==0 before it pops a command. A monster spawned with server_controlled=1 and a big cmd_hold_ms delays its first command. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C29, world_movement_npc#24): monster motion codes (lo bits 2-4 -> +0x904): 0 -> action 7 then walk 12 (82.5 px/s); 1 -> 4 (melee attack loop); 3 -> jump 10/9/11; 5 -> 1 (attack loop); 6 -> 5 wind-up then 6 dash. With server_controlled = 1 the physics STOPS when the hold expires, EVEN MID-AIR, so a server-driven monster needs a follow-up command before its hold runs out.

**References.** C2S 0x0D (FUN_0042c940 @0x42CAAF..) uses the identical blob encoding: +0x8B3->bits0-1 (2->1, 6->2), +0x8B4<<2 (mask 0x1C), +0x8B5<<5 (0x1E0), +0x8B6<<9 (0xE00), +0x94C<<12 (0xF000), +0x950<<16 (0xF0000), +0x8D0->bits20-21, +0x958&0xFFF in the second dword. It likewise sends target uid if +0x94C!=0 and f64 x2 if +0x8B6==4 and action is 7/9. The C2S form carries extra fields (u32 time delta, u16, u32 tick delta, and when move_flag is set u32 +0xD78, f64 x4, bool...) that the S2C form drops. The captured C2S 0x0D blob '00 02 40 53 00 60 64 75' decodes to facing 8, action 0, move_flag 0 plus garbage high bits, which is consistent. KR Hex-Rays case 0x1B has the same structure (uid lookup, 0x58 alloc, u32, 8-byte blob, the same conditionals) but DIFFERENT bit widths (KR: 2-5, 6-10, 11-13, 14-17, 18-21, 22-23). Use the EN widths above. Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py. The memory notes say monster movement is unsolved; this opcode is the likely candidate.

**Open questions.**
- Exact meaning of action codes (+0x94C values 5,6,7,9,0xA,0xD,0x10 seen) and motion/sub_b values. They need a trace of FUN_00413920/FUN_004158d0 state machines.
- [RESOLVED by live verification world_movement_npc#24, 2026-09-17] Live: a monster under server_controlled = 1 does move from motion + facing plus client-side physics while its hold (+0xE48) is non-zero; walk code 0 gives 82.5 px/s. Physics stops the moment the hold expires, even in mid-air, so continuous commands are required. Original question: "How a monster actually moves under server control: FUN_00412100 doesn't apply pos for type 4. Does motion/facing plus per-frame physics move it, or is there another move opcode? Needs dynamic verification."
- Whether hold_ms units are ms (30 subtracted per ~30ms tick is assumed).
- The consumer's gate scene+0xF88+0x70==0 (a map/mode flag); when it is nonzero no queued commands are applied.

| `move_bits` | bytes[8] | Same bit packing as the 8 bytes inside C2S 0x0D, so the server can relay them verbatim. Read as move_bits_lo = u32 LE of bytes 0-3 and move_bits_hi = u32 LE of bytes 4-7. | copied raw into scene(this+0x4CC)+0xEF8..0xEFF. This 8-byte scratch area is the same buffer the C2S 0x0D packer FUN_004… |
| `move_bits_lo[1:0] horiz_input` | bitfield | horizontal key/direction state; 8 = neutral. The C2S packer maps 8B3: 2 to 1, 6 to 2, anything else to 0. | node+0x4A: 1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, 0 or 3 gives 8. Applied later to entity+0x8B3. |

When consumed it goes to entity+0x950 if scene+0xF24 != 0, otherwi… |
| `move_bits_lo[21:20] facing` | bitfield(2) | facing direction used for the action | node+0x50: 1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, anything else gives 8. Later entity+0x8D0. |

| `target_uid` | u32 | Target/victim uid of the action. The C2S 0x0D packer only sends entity+0xD80 when action != 0, so the server should write 0 when there is no action. | node+0x08, later entity+0xD80. If it equals scene+0x220 (the local uid), the handler zeroes node+0x08, +0x4E, +0x4F and… |
| `action_flag` | u8 | only present when the action nibble is 9 or 10 (grab/throw). FUN_00412360 case 9 checks it to trigger a buff/effect. | node+0x52, later entity+0x8FF |

**Semantics.** Server-to-client counterpart of C2S 0x0D: it syncs another entity's input and action state. After the entity is found, the handler: - Sets entity+0x8E4 = 1 (it is 0 only for 0x9E) and entity+0x8D7 = 1. - Mallocs and zeroes a 0x58-byte node and sets node[0] = 0x3DE (990). - Decodes the 8 bits into the node, zeroes node+0x30/+0x38/+0x08/+0x04, then reads the target, the optional u8 and the optional position block. Only 0x2A then does these steps: - Frees every pending node in the entity's move queue (entity+0x1350; head at +0x1354) and sets entity+0xE48 (hold timer) = 0. - Sets node[0] = 960, or 0 if it was 30 or less. - If target_uid == local uid, clears the action fields as described above and sets node[0] to 960 minus max(entity+0xDAC, action_time), clamped at 0. The node is then appended to the queue with FUN_00459df0. FUN_00412100 consumes the queue each tick, only for entities with state byte +0x98 > 2 whose uid != local uid: - node[0] is the longest time (in 30 ms steps) the node waits. - The node applies at once if the entity is idle (904 == 8, 8B3 == 8, 8B4/8B5/8B6 == 0, 950 == 0, 94C == 0). - Applying it copies the node into entity 8B3/8B4/8B5/8B6/94C/950/D80/958/8FF/8D0 and D78/1328/1330/8DB/8E8/1338/1340/8D4/8E7. The EN 0x2A leaves all of those except the decoded bits, target and 8FF at 0.

**Trigger.** Send to the other players on the same map when a player's C2S 0x0D arrives. This is the correct relay: echoing 0x0D is known to desync. Use 0x2A for an authoritative state (it flushes the queue and carries target and position); use 0x9F/0x9E for buffered updates.

**Expected response.** none LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#26/#27/#28): 0x2A applies within one sample (<17 ms measured) because it flushes the pending queue and sets +0xE48 = 0, so it is the only "apply now" relay. 0x9E / 0x9F / 0x1B all append BEHIND the pending nodes (0x9E measured 750 ms, 0x9F 1.81 s, 0x1B stop 1.08 s). Use 0x2A for authoritative keyframes and stops, 0x1B for the streamed relay.

**Gates / hazards.** - An unknown uid or uid 0 is silently ignored and nothing more is read. - NEVER send it with mover_uid == the receiver's own uid. The local entity would be found, its position overwritten (a teleport), and nodes queued for the local uid are never consumed (FUN_00412100 skips the local uid), so memory leaks. - The position block depends on client-only state (mover state 0x10 = dead) and on target_uid == receiver uid. Nothing is read after it, so always appending the 17 bytes should be harmless because trailing bytes are ignored. Omitting it is only safe when target_uid == receiver uid. - A nonzero reaction nibble (bits 16-19) snaps the remote entity to (0,0) when the node is consumed, because the node x/y at +0x10/+0x18 stay 0. - Needs a valid scene (this+0x4CC), so send it in-world only. - Bits 22-31 of lo and 12-31 of hi are ignored. Live C2S captures carry stale garbage there.

**References.** - Bit mapping matches the C2S 0x0D packer FUN_0042c940 exactly: 8B3 in bits 0-1, 8B4 in 2-4, 8B5 in 5-8, 8B6 in 9-11, 94C in 12-15, 950 in 16-19, 8D0 in 20-21, 958 in hi bits 0-11. - Live C2S 0x0D captures decode consistently: walking bits_lo 0x53400200 gives 8B6 = 1; jumping 0x7240000C gives 8B4 = 3; bits_hi & 0xFFF = 0 in both. - KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c, case 0x2A/0x9E/0x9F) has the same skeleton but a DIFFERENT layout. It adds a u16 before the target uid and a u16 after it, uses wider bitfields (action at bits 14-17, facing at 22-23), adds action 14 to the u8 condition, and uses a state check of 23. Do not port the KR layout. - windslayer_server.py has no builder. The project memory confirms that echoing 0x0D broke the cipher.

**Open questions.**
- Which opcode the original server chose for normal walking versus actions (0x2A, 0x9F or 0x9E). The client semantics suggest 0x2A for authoritative/action states and 0x9F/0x9E for buffered input changes.
- C2S 0x0D carries no x/y unless the reaction state is nonzero, so it is unclear where the original server got pos_x/pos_y for 0x2A (server-side simulation, or the last known spawn/position).
- Exact meaning of entity bytes 8B5/8B6 and of the 12-bit action_time value.
- Whether the (0,0) snap for a nonzero reaction nibble is real in practice or is masked by other state (not verified at runtime).

### S2C 0x9E — RemoteEntityMoveStateQueued (short delay, clears flag 8E4)

*server → client* · key `0x9E` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 12 bytes

Locations: `0x00454E6D` shared S2C handler block; `0x00454EA7` opcode==0x9E check that sets entity+0x8E4; `0x00455197` opcode==0x9E sets node[0]=0x1E; `0x00412100` queue consumer

```
u32 mover_uid
if(find_entity(mover_uid) == null) { stop }
bytes[8] move_bits
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mover_uid` | u32 | uid of the entity being synced | stack [esp+0x1D4]; matched against entity+0x84 through FUN_004189f0 |
| `move_bits` | bytes[8] | Same 8-byte bitfield as C2S 0x0D / S2C 0x2A: lo[1:0] horizontal input (1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, else 8), lo[4:2] 8B4, lo[8:5] 8B5, lo[11:9] 8B6, lo[15:12] action 94C, lo[19:16] reaction 950, lo[21:20] facing (1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, else 8), hi[11:0] 958. | scene+0xEF8..0xEFF, decoded into a queue node exactly as in 0x2A |

**Semantics.** Uses the same handler block as 0x2A. It sets: - entity+0x8E4 = 0 (the SETNZ on opcode != 0x9E) - entity+0x8D7 = 1 It builds a queue node from the bits with node+0x08 (target) = 0 and node+0x52 = 0. The node's delay is set to node[0] = 0x1E (30 ms, about one tick), and the node is appended to the entity move queue (+0x1350). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#29 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): 0x9E is NOT an immediate stop. The 30 ms is the node's OWN hold, counted only after every node already queued ahead of it has finished, so the real latency is the remaining hold of the queue (measured 750 ms behind one pending walk node); the queue drains at about 2x speed while >= 2 nodes are queued. entity+0x8E4 = 0 is written AT RECEIPT, not on dequeue. For 'stop now' use 0x2A (it flushes the queue and carries a position) or relay the stop as the next 0x1B. The queue is NOT flushed, entity+0xE48 is not reset, and no position is read. FUN_00412100 applies the node on the next ticks, which sets 94C/D80/958/8FF/8D0 etc. on the entity.

**Trigger.** Relay a buffered movement/input change for another entity when it should apply almost immediately. The exact use by the original server is unknown.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** - An unknown uid or uid 0 is ignored after 4 bytes. - Do not send it for the receiver's own uid: FUN_00412100 never consumes the local uid's queue, so nodes leak. - A nonzero reaction nibble (bits 16-19) makes the consumer copy the zeroed node x/y into the entity, snapping it to (0,0). - Clearing entity+0x8E4 changes interpolation checks in FUN_00413920/FUN_004158d0/FUN_00416380.

**References.** - KR Hex-Rays groups 0x9E with 0x2A/0x9F and likewise sets the delay to a global (dword_6375BC) for 0x9E, but its bitfield layout differs. - Not implemented in windslayer_server.py or in PySlayer's Python.

**Open questions.**
- When the original server used 0x9E instead of 0x9F (for example stop/idle transitions, since it clears flag 8E4).

### C2S 0x0F — EquipItem

*client → server* · key `0x44C481/0x0F` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 5 + 2*stone_count (5..15)

Locations: `0x44C2C0` EquipItem: ECX=item def, EAX=game_state, args u16 item_id, ptr to 12-byte option record (…; `0x44C402` Add(u8 0x0F) opcode; `0x44C415` Add(u16) item_id; `0x44C445` Add(u8) stone_count (loop 0x44C420 counts leading non-zero words, max 5)

```
u16 item_id
u8 stone_count
repeat(stone_count) {
  u16 stone_id
}
u16 extra_option
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_id` | u16 | Item-table idx of the Type 1 equipment piece to equip | stack arg 1: quick-slot id game_state+0x10BE[slot] or inventory UI record +0x00 |
| `stone_count` | u8 | Number of socketed stones/options that follow (quick-slot registry calls these 'QuickSlotStone%d%d') | computed: number of leading non-zero u16 in record[0..4] (stops at first zero, max 5) |
| `stone_id` | u16 | Socketed stone/option item id i. Words after the first zero are never sent. | record[i] (record = game_state+0x10DE+slot*12 or UI slot record +0x02) |
| `extra_option` | u16 | Unknown 6th per-item option word. It is not saved to the registry with the quick slots. S2C 0x1D echoes it. | record+10 (6th u16; UI slot record +0x0C) |

**Semantics.** Asks the server to equip the bag item <item_id> with its stone list. Sending changes no client state. The equip is applied when the server sends S2C 0x1D (u32 uid, u16 item, u8 n, u16[n], u16; handler 0x45298C writes equip grid entity+0x13C/+0x16E and recomposes the sprite). The bag entry is removed by a bag-remove packet (our server uses S2C 0x23). Live capture matches: double-clicking Wooden Stick 179 sent 'B3 00 00 00 00' = item 179, stone_count 0, extra 0.

**Trigger.** Double-clicking/activating an equipment item in the inventory window (window 9) with no NPC-shop/storage/stall context active. Also pressing a quick-slot hotkey (or HUD quick-slot button) that holds an equipment item, at most once per 1000 ms per slot.

**Expected response.** S2C 0x1D equip (same body layout prefixed by u32 uid) plus a bag removal (0x23). Also error chat on failure (server-defined).

**Gates / hazards.** All client-side, each showing a message and not sending on failure. scene+0x970 local entity non-null (silent). def+0x1D4 gender: ==1 requires scene+0x130 != 0 and ==2 requires scene+0x130 == 0, else 'You can not equip other gender's item.'. scene+0x979 (level byte) >= def+0x1D8 (Lv), else 'You need higher level'. entity+0x904 not in {1,4,0xE,0xF} and < 0x18, entity+0x15B4 not in {1,4,0xE,0xF} and < 0x18, and scene+0x258 (pending skill) == 0, else 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.'. def+0x168+entity.class(+0x110)*4 (Job[class]) != 0 or def+0x168 (Job[0]) != 0, else 'You can't equip other class items.'. Hazard: an unanswered C2S 0x15 skill leaves scene+0x258 set and blocks this packet permanently. The quick-slot path updates its 1000 ms timestamp even when a gate rejects.

**References.** This is the only 0x0F send site in the client. Our server's _handle_equip_item reads only u16 item_id and ignores stone_count/stones/extra. That is safe for parsing but loses stone data, and its 0x1D reply does not echo stones. The docstring 'u16 item [, u8, u16]' is correct only for stone_count == 0. PySlayer parse_0F has the same n==0-only layout and wrongly asserts payload[0]==0x0D. It matches the captured 5-byte payload.

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of the 6th option word (record+10 / extra_option) - maybe refine/enchant level or durability.
- Whether unequip uses a different C2S opcode (not in this batch).
- Identity of entity+0x904 / +0x15B4 state values 1,4,0xE,0xF,>=0x18 (attack/skill animation states).

### S2C 0x1E — UnequipItemToBag

*server → client* · key `0x1E` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 9 + 2*option_count (normally 19 with option_count=5)

Locations: `0x00454090` handler block start (shared 0x1E/0x24); `0x4540A5` read u32 uid; `0x4540C0` read u16 item_id; `0x4540FA` read u8 option_count

```
u32 uid
u16 item_id
u8 option_count
repeat(option_count) { u16 option_value }
u16 option_extra
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | uid of the entity whose equipment changes. If it equals scene+0x220 (local player), the item is also put back into the local equipment bag tab | stack [base+0x160]; entity lookup; compared to scene+0x220 at 0x454243 |
| `item_id` | u16 | item id of the equipped item to remove (1-based item table scene+0xF84). The def must have def+0x154 == 1 (equipment category) or the whole packet is ignored | stack [base+0xdc] |
| `option_count` | u8 | number of option/enchant u16 values that follow. The client's 12-byte item-option record holds 5 option slots (bytes 0..9) plus option_extra (bytes 10..11), so send <= 5. The record is zeroed first, so fewer than 5 leaves zeros. No bounds check: a 6th value l… | stack [base+0x4e] |
| `option_value` | u16 | item option/enchant value i (PySlayer calls these 'enchant'); fills record bytes 2*i | 12-byte record at stack [base+0x23c + 2*i] |
| `option_extra` | u16 | trailing u16 of the 12-byte item record (record bytes 10..11); meaning unknown (PySlayer 0x03 sends it unnamed) | stack [base+0x246] = record+10 |

**Semantics.** Removes an equipped item from an entity and, for the local player, returns it to the bag. Steps: (1) Look up item_id in the item table; it must exist with def+0x154 == 1, otherwise nothing happens. (2) If the entity is found: FUN_004269a0(entity+0x13C equip id grid [25 u16], entity+0x16E option records [25 x 12 bytes], item_id, &record) finds the slot whose id == item_id AND whose 12-byte record matches exactly (memcmp) and zeroes it. Then FUN_00426d50 rebuilds the body sprite, FUN_0041ace0 recalculates stats, FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recalculates max HP (clamping current HP), and if level != 0 FUN_00427f40(0) does the same for max MP. (3) If uid == scene+0x220 (checked even when the entity lookup failed): for opcode 0x1E, if bag capacity byte scene+0x3A9 <= 45, FUN_00423FF0 (mode EAX=1 'add') puts item_id plus the 12-byte record into the first empty slot of the equipment bag tab (u16 ids at scene+0x3C8, records at scene+0x422; the same arrays the 0x13 pickup path writes). If the item is a cash item (def+0x1F0 != 0), FUN_0045d170(game_state+0x700, item_id) updates the cash-item list. For both 0x1E and 0x24 it then refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290 on game_state+0xD5C) and the equipment window (FUN_00441a10).

**Trigger.** Server confirmation that an item was unequipped (moved from the equipment grid back into the inventory), sent to the owner and to observers so the sprite updates.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** DUPLICATION HAZARD: the return value of the removal (FUN_004269a0) is ignored. If item_id or ANY of the 12 record bytes (5 options + option_extra) differ from what was stored at equip time, the equip slot is NOT cleared, but the local player still gets a copy added to the bag. The server must echo exactly the option values it used when equipping (e.g. 0x1D / 0x07). If the bag is full, FUN_00423ff0 silently adds nothing. Equipment-category gate def+0x154 == 1. The local-bag branch needs uid == scene+0x220. option_count > 5 corrupts the record (see field notes). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C10, item_inventory#04): a block mismatch produces a THREE-WAY desync, not just a bag duplicate: (1) the bag gains a duplicate carrying the WIRE block, (2) the equip grid and the Equipment window KEEP the item, and (3) the sprite recompose still drops the item's visual (the character is drawn with an empty hand). Echo exactly the 12 option bytes used at equip time. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.

**References.** Wire layout matches the 0x1D handler at 0x45298C (u32, u16, u8 N, N*u16 into a zeroed 12-byte record, trailing u16) and PySlayer opcode_0x03's item record (u16 id, u8 5, 5*u16 enchant, u16). windslayer_server.py defines _build_en_opcode_1E (line ~2189) but NEVER calls it. Its docstring ('persistent in-place equip merge', u16 skinSelector/class, 14 apparences + weapon) is WRONG: the handler REMOVES the item via 0x4269a0, and sending 14 values would corrupt the record. The 0x1D docstring in the same file ('0x1E is the REMOVE/unequip opcode') is right. reference_combat_model.md's 'combat damage' reading and its '+0x3c8 float-number pool' claim are wrong: scene+0x3C8 is the equipment bag tab's item-id array (confirmed by the 0x13 pickup code FUN_00440e50 at 0x440F70/0x440F99). Newer KR build: case 0x1E/0x24 reads u32 + an item-record helper (sub_40A010).

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of option_extra (record bytes 10..11) and of the 5 option values (enchant / refine / socket?) not resolved from tooltip code.
- Which C2S request (unequip double-click) the retail server answers with 0x1E was not traced here.

### S2C 0x23 — InventoryItemRemove (silent)

*server → client* · key `0x23` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **implemented** · length: 7 + 2*opt_count (opt_count must be <= 5)

Locations: `0x0046DD4B` handler block; `0x0046DE06` FUN_00404210 item definition lookup; `0x0046DE2A` FUN_00467140(type, item_id, &opts, count) remove; `0x0046DE39` jmp 0x46D968 -> FUN_00465290 inventory UI refresh, return 1

```
u16 item_id
u16 count
u8 opt_count
repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt }
u16 opt_extra
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_id` | u16 | Item id to remove (1-based catalog index) | local [frame+0x24] -> FUN_00404210, FUN_00467140 arg1 |
| `count` | u16 | Number to remove from type-0/type-2 stacks; ignored for equipment (always 1) | local [frame+0x28] -> FUN_00467140 arg3 (read as a word) |
| `opt_count` | u8 | How many option words follow (0..5) | local [frame+0x0C] |
| `opt` | u16 | Option words 0..opt_count-1 of the 12-byte option block (starts zeroed) | local opts[i] at [frame+0x34+2*i] |
| `opt_extra` | u16 | Word 5 of the option block | local opts[5] at [frame+0x3E] |

**Semantics.** Same as 0x19 but with no leading gold field and no chat message. Reads item_id, count and the option block (u8 n, n u16 words into words 0.., u16 into word 5). Looks up the item definition (none -> stop, handled). Removes the item with FUN_00467140 using the same type rules as 0x19: type 0 subtract from u16 stacks, type 1 remove the matching equipment slot (option bytes must match), type 2 subtract from u8 stacks. On success refreshes the inventory UI; on failure nothing visible happens.

**Trigger.** Whenever the server takes an item out of the bag without selling it: consumed, used by a quest, destroyed, moved to storage or equipped (our server sends it after the 0x1D equip).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Same stack overflow as 0x19: opt_count must be <= 5 (>= 63 corrupts the /GS cookie and kills the client). Equipment is removed only when all 12 option bytes match the stored slot; items granted by 0x18 have zero options, so send opt_count=0 and opt_extra=0. Fails if the tab capacity byte (player_info+0x361/+0x362/+0x363) > 45, if count=0 for stack items, if fewer than count are owned (types 0/2), or if the type is 3 or higher.

**References.** Our server's _build_opcode_23 (u16 item, u16 count, u8 0, u16 0 = 7 B) has the right format. One correction to its comment: FUN_00404210 does not look up a bag element. It returns the item definition from the global catalog [scene+0xF84] (name at +0, type at +0x154), and is NULL only for item_id 0 or an id past the catalog. Whether the item is actually in the bag is decided later by FUN_00467140 against player_info's tab arrays. The memory note '0x23 didn't remove bag in test' fits the item not being in the matching tab array (or an option mismatch), not a catalog miss.

**Open questions.**
- Which C2S requests the original server answered with 0x23 (item use, storage deposit, etc.).

### S2C 0x24 — UnequipItemRemove

*server → client* · key `0x24` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 9 + 2*option_count (normally 19 with option_count=5)

Locations: `0x00454090` handler block start (shared 0x1E/0x24); `0x4540A5` read u32 uid; `0x4540C0` read u16 item_id; `0x4540FA` read u8 option_count

```
u32 uid
u16 item_id
u8 option_count
repeat(option_count) { u16 option_value }
u16 option_extra
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | u32 | uid of the entity whose equipped item is removed | stack [base+0x160] |
| `item_id` | u16 | equipped item id to remove; def must exist with def+0x154 == 1 | stack [base+0xdc] |
| `option_count` | u8 | number of option u16s (send <= 5; same record-overflow behaviour as 0x1E) | stack [base+0x4e] |
| `option_value` | u16 | option/enchant value i of the equipped item; must match the stored record exactly for removal | record [base+0x23c + 2*i] |
| `option_extra` | u16 | record bytes 10..11 (unknown meaning); must match stored record | record [base+0x246] |

**Semantics.** Same handler as 0x1E: removes item_id (with a matching 12-byte option record) from the entity's equip grid +0x13C/+0x16E, rebuilds the sprite, recalculates stats and max HP/MP. For the local player (uid == scene+0x220) it refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290) and the equipment window (FUN_00441a10). Unlike 0x1E it does NOT add the item back to the bag and does NOT update the cash-item list (FUN_0045d170): the opcode check at 0x45424F skips both. So the item simply disappears from the equipment.

**Trigger.** Server removes an equipped item without returning it to the inventory (likely item destroyed, expired or broken, or moved elsewhere).

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Same gates as 0x1E (item def exists with def+0x154 == 1; the removal needs an exact id + 12-byte record match, otherwise nothing changes and there is no error). The window refresh only runs for the local uid. No bag add, so no duplication hazard. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C33, item_inventory#05): removal from the equip tab COMPACTS the list - later slots shift down - so slot indices the server cached before the removal are stale afterwards.

**References.** Shares its wire layout with 0x1D and 0x1E. The newer KR Hex-Rays groups case 0x1E/0x24 together too. Not sent by windslayer_server.py. Memory note 'Equip: 0x23=silent-remove' refers to a different opcode.

**Open questions.**
- Retail use case for 0x24 (destroy / expire / trade) is inferred, not traced.

## card_deck

### C2S 0x63 — CardDeckListRequest

*client → server* · key `0x44EF67/0x63` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **partial** · length: 0

Locations: `0x44DF8F` in the S2C 0x02 login-result==1 branch: FUN_0045a130(EAX=app+0xDC4) initializes the card-…; `0x45A141` MOV [cardobj+0xC], g_sock_game (app+0xDD0); also +0x0 = app, +0x4 = ui root, +0x8 = playe…; `0x44EF55` ECX = [app+0xDD0]; `0x44EF5D` Add(u8 0x63) via EDI = IAT 0x4A40FC

```
(empty payload)
```

**Semantics.** Opcode-only request that asks the server for the card deck ('dictionary') contents. The send is unconditional and comes right after the messenger 0x2F send, at the very end of the S2C 0x03 handler. It goes through the card-deck object's socket pointer (app+0xDC4, the same object passed to SubHandler5). That object only handles S2C 0x8A: u8 count stored at (player+0x48)+0xE30, then u16 ids. It then refreshes the Card Deck UI ('%u / %u (%u%%)'). S2C 0x8B error code 2 says 'Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again.', which ties this data to the login/world-entry fetch. No other Adds; the only Add(0x63) in the binary is this one. Fire-and-forget.

**Trigger.** Automatic, at the end of every S2C 0x03 (world/map info) handler, i.e. after each map load, immediately after C2S 0x2F (or in its place when the messenger gate fails).

**Expected response.** Probably S2C 0x8A card deck list: u8 count, repeat(count){ u16 card_id }. It is stored at player+0x48+0xE30/+0xE32 and handled in SubHandler5_ifelse. The client does not require a reply.

**Gates / hazards.** No gate. [app+0xDD0] is only set by FUN_0045a130 in the S2C 0x02 success path (result==1). If a server sends S2C 0x03 without a prior successful 0x02 on this connection, ECX may be NULL or stale and CSNSocket::Add would fault (crash). SubHandler5 ignores 0x8A/0x8B unless cardobj+0x0 (app) and +0x4 (ui) are non-null, which is also set in that 0x02 path.

**References.** The live capture shows 0x63 with 0 bytes after a map load, which agrees. windslayer_server.py _dispatch answers C2S 0x63 by sending S2C 0x63 with an EMPTY body. That looks wrong: the client's S2C 0x63 handler (0x4577A8) is unrelated. It reads u16 + u8 and formats '%s(%u/%u)' / '%u Players' (a player-count display), so an empty body means reading past the end. The natural reply is S2C 0x8A. PySlayer has no C2S 0x63 parser; its server_packets list has no 0x8A either.

**Open questions.**
- Name and reply are inferred from the owning object (card-deck/dictionary object at app+0xDC4, its S2C 0x8A/0x8B handlers and strings); wire format (0 bytes) is certain, semantic name is medium confidence.
- S2C 0x03 already reads a u8 into player+0xE78 (= player+0x48+0xE30, the card count slot) at 0x44E629; it is unclear whether 0x8A is still needed to fill the u16 id array or whether 0x03's byte is an unrelated field sharing that offset.
- Whether the current server's empty S2C 0x63 reply causes visible side effects (a garbage player-count label) was not verified statically.

*client → server* · key `0x45A4F8/0x64` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 2

Locations: `0x44B82B` caller: the UI event dispatcher calls the card-deck handler with EAX=control id, EDI=main…; `0x45A4B3` gate: control id must be 0x292 (id 8 returns 1 and does nothing); `0x45A4BA` gate: notification code must be 2 (likely the confirm/OK button); `0x45A4C3` FUN_004830f0 looks up control 0x292 in g_ui_root+0x5C0; the send happens only if +0x134 !…

```
u16 card_item_id
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card_item_id` | u16 | Item template id (1-based index into the item DB at charmgr+0xF84) of the card item to register in the Card Deck. Never 0, because the client skips the send when it is 0. | control 0x292 +0x134 (MOVZX word). Set at 0x45A457 from DI, which is the u16 in the selected inventory (control 9) cell… |

**Semantics.** Asks the server to register a card item in the character's Card Deck (a collection book). Client flow: (1) inventory action case 0x65 in FUN_00469090 on a selected inventory item calls FUN_0045a3c0. That function checks that the item def has +0x154==2 and +0x14C!=0; otherwise it shows 'This item cannot be registered.'. It also scans the local deck list (byte count at charData+0xE30, u16 ids from +0xE32; charData = main+0x4CC+0x48); a duplicate shows 'This card is already registered . You can't register it again.'. If both checks pass, it stores the id in control 0x292 +0x134 and opens dialog 0x292. (2) When the user confirms dialog 0x292 (notification code 2), FUN_0045a4a0 sends [0x64][u16 card_item_id] and shows the modal 'Waiting for the server to response.'.

**Trigger.** The player uses the card-register action on a card item in the inventory (FUN_00469090 case 0x65), then confirms dialog control 0x292 (notification 2). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C47, quest_cards_misc#07): the user gesture behind FUN_00469090 case 0x65 is DRAGGING a card from the bag (Miscellanies tab) onto the Card Deck window (window 8, hotkey B) - neither a right-click nor a double-click is involved. The confirm dialog 0x292 then reads "Once the card is registered to the Card Deck, it cannot be returned back to your inventory."

**Expected response.** S2C 0x8B (handled in SubHandler5 @0x45A520). Its grammar is: u8 result; if(result==1){ u8 new_count u16 card_item_id }. On result 1 the client sets charData+0xE30=new_count and writes card_item_id at charData+0xE30+new_count*2, so new_count is the 1-based slot and equals the new total. This happens only if the item lookup and FUN_00467140(card_item_id,0,1) both succeed (probably consumes the card from the inventory). The client then refreshes the deck UI and prints 'Registered %s in the Card Deck.'. result 2 = 'Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again.', result 6 = 'Already registered.', anything else = 'Failure to register card. Please try again in a few minutes.'. The 0x8B handler first calls FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1), which probably dismisses the waiting box. S2C 0x8A (u8 count; repeat(count){u16 card_item_id}) replaces the whole deck list. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x8B CardDeckRegisterResult - this one box does have an OK button, so an unanswered 0x64 is not a soft-lock, but nothing is registered.

**Gates / hazards.** Needs [main+0xDC4+4] (g_ui_root copy) != 0, which FUN_0045a130 sets during the S2C 0x02 handler. FUN_00446300 only reaches this handler if [main+0xDC4] != 0 and the item-mall handler FUN_0045f2e0 returned 0. The socket pointer is not null-checked here. After sending, the client shows a blocking 'Waiting for the server to response.' message box. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C47, quest_cards_misc#07): the waiting box (dialog 0x16) HAS an OK button, so an unanswered 0x64 does NOT soft-lock the client - the player closes the box, nothing is registered and the card stays in the bag. (Drop "soft-locks" from the design-doc note.) control0x292+0x134 is not cleared after the send, so confirming the dialog again would re-send the same id. The duplicate check runs only against the client's local deck list, so the server must also reject duplicates (result 6).

**References.** No C2S parser in PySlayer (its client_packets only cover 0x03,0x0B,0x0C,0x0D,0x0F,0x15,0x1A,0x2B,0x2C,0x7E). PySlayer has server builders opcode_0x8A/0x8B in __init__ (KR). Not handled by our windslayer_server.py _dispatch (no 0x64 branch). The UI strings in FUN_0045a3c0 and SubHandler5 confirm the Card Deck meaning.

**Open questions.**
- [RESOLVED by live verification quest_cards_misc#07, 2026-09-17] Live: notification 2 on control 0x292 is the OK button of the register confirmation dialog, reached by dragging a card from the bag onto the Card Deck window (window 8). Original question: "Exact meaning of notification code 2 on control 0x292 (assumed to be the OK/Yes button of the register confirmation dialog)"
- Whether FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) at the start of the 0x8B handler is what closes the 'Waiting for the server to response.' box
- What FUN_00467140(card_item_id,0,1) does in the 0x8B success path (likely removes one card from the inventory); whether the server must also send an inventory update

### S2C 0x8A — CardDeckList

*server → client* · key `0x8A` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 1 + 2*deck_count

Locations: `0x45A520` sub-handler 5 (if/else) entry; gate [obj+0]!=0 && [obj+4]!=0, obj = game_state+0xDC4 = 0x…; `0x45A69D` 0x8A handler block; `0x458350` call site of SubHandler5 in the unclaimed-opcode chain (ECX = game_state+0xDC4); `0x45A130` handler-object init, run from the S2C 0x02 login-response handler @0x44DF8F: [+0]=game_st…

```
u8 deck_count
repeat(deck_count) {
  u16 card_item_id
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_count` | u8 | number of cards registered in the Card Deck (dictionary). Also the loop count. | read straight into charinfo+0xE30 (= *(0x70EECC)+0x78... i.e. scene+0xE78; charinfo pointer cached at 0x70F7D4) |
| `card_item_id` | u16 | item id (1-based index into the item table) of the i-th registered card | read straight into charinfo+0xE32+2*i (scene+0xE7A+2*i) |

**Semantics.** Replaces the whole local Card Deck list. The u8 count is read directly into charinfo+0xE30, then deck_count u16 item ids are read directly into charinfo+0xE32.. (no bounds check). Then FUN_0045a160: finds dialog id 8 (Card Deck window) and clears its list (FUN_0047d700), adds one 0x38-byte list entry per id (the loop stops early at the first id == 0), picks page/scroll state, and if the item table's u16 total-card count at [itemtable+0x24] is non-zero, formats "%u / %u (%u%%)" = deck_count / total / percent into control 0x29 (FUN_004838c0). The stored list is also what the client checks before registering a card (FUN_0045a3c0 says "This card is already registered ." if the id is already in the list, so it sends no C2S 0x64 for it). No reply is sent. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C22, quest_cards_misc#13/#14): [itemtable+0x24] - the "%u / %u (%u%%)" label's TOTAL - is 880 in the EN client, not 64. In the decoded EN hii (4248 items) exactly 880 entries have CardNpc != 0, while only 64 have CardSpr != 0, so +0x24 counts CardNpc != 0 entries. The label reads n / 880 with floor(n*100/880)%, so 1 or 2 registered cards both show 0%. Before any 0x8A/0x8B the label shows the untouched template text "000/000 (000%)".

**Trigger.** Server-pushed; no C2S request in the EN client asks for it. Send after a successful login (S2C 0x02 success), and before or at world entry, so the deck window and the duplicate check have data. The 0x8B result-2 text "Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again." suggests the original server sent this list at login.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** Ignored (no bytes consumed) until the handler object is initialized by a successful S2C 0x02 login response: SubHandler5 checks [0x70F7C4]!=0 and [0x70F7C8]!=0. CAPACITY HAZARD: ids are written in place with no bounds check. charinfo+0xE98 holds an i32 field (compared with 100/30 at 0x469189, updated by SubHandler3), so at most 51 entries fit (0xE32..0xE97). Keep deck_count <= 50/51. At about 133 or more entries the writes reach the item-table pointer at scene+0xF84 (charinfo+0xF3C), which other code dereferences. An id of 0 ends the UI list early (the count label still shows deck_count). Ids should be real item ids (category 2 card items); unknown ids just produce empty list entries.

**References.** PySlayer: no opcode_0x8A.py exists (server_packets/__init__.py only has a try/except import stub); the KR Hex-Rays doc has no card-deck strings. Our server (windslayer_server.py): no builder and never sends 0x8A. The opcode atlas lists 0x8A only as a SubHandler5 route. The format comes from asm alone and matches the decomp.

**Open questions.**
- Exact deck capacity: 51 slots fit before the i32 at charinfo+0xE98, but the design limit could be 50 (the struct may have 2 alignment bytes). No explicit constant was found.
- Is charinfo+0xE30 zeroed on login or character load? If not, a missing 0x8A may leave stale data from an earlier session.
- Does dialog 8 (Card Deck window) always exist when 0x8A arrives? If it does not, FUN_0045a160 adds entries to whatever dialog ui_root+0x5F0 points at. Probably harmless because the UI is built at startup, but this was not verified.
- [RESOLVED by live verification quest_cards_misc#13, 2026-09-17] Live: [itemtable+0x24] = 880 in EN, which is exactly the number of decoded EN items with CardNpc != 0 (only 64 have CardSpr != 0). It is the card-dictionary total, not the count of registrable Monster Card items. Original question: "What the item table's u16 at +0x24 is: presumably the total number of collectible cards, loaded from client data."

### S2C 0x8B — CardDeckRegisterResult

*server → client* · key `0x8B` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 4 if result == 1, else 1

Locations: `0x45A572` 0x8B handler block (opcode-0x8A-1 branch); `0x45A578` dismisses message-box dialog 0x16 ('Waiting for the server to response.') before reading; `0x45A60E` item record lookup: itemtable[card_item_id-1]; `0x45A634` removes 1 of the card item from the client inventory by category (2 = etc tab @inv+0x760/…

```
u8 result
if(result == 1) {
  u8 new_deck_count
  u16 card_item_id
} else {
  stop
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | u8 | 1 = registered OK; 2 = 'Failed to receive dictionary\r\ninformation.Please log in again.'; 6 = 'Already registered.'; any other value = 'Failure to register card. \r\nPlease try again in a few minutes.' (message box type 3) | stack local [esp+0x13] |
| `new_deck_count` | u8 | deck count after adding this card (normally old count + 1). The new card is stored as the last entry. | stack local [esp+0x12]; on success written to charinfo+0xE30 (deck count). Also used as the 1-based slot: the id goes t… |
| `card_item_id` | u16 | item id of the card that was registered (same id the client sent in C2S 0x64) | stack local [esp+0x14]; on success written as u16 to charinfo+0xE30+2*new_deck_count |

**Semantics.** Reply to C2S 0x64 (card register). Before reading anything, the handler calls FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) on ui_root, which closes the 'Waiting for the server to response.' message box (dialog 0x16). It then reads result. result==1: reads new_deck_count (u8) and card_item_id (u16). It looks up the item record (itemtable[card_item_id-1]); if there is none, it stops silently. Otherwise it calls FUN_00467140(category=[rec+0x154], inventory object game_state+0xD5C, id, 0, qty 1) to take one of that item out of the client's own inventory (category 0 = equip, 1 = consumable, 2 = etc; other categories fail). If the client does not hold the item, it stops silently and the deck is NOT updated. On success it writes charinfo+0xE30 = new_deck_count and u16 charinfo+0xE32+2*(new_deck_count-1) = card_item_id, rebuilds the deck list and the 'n / total (pct%)' label (FUN_0045a160), prints "Registered <item name> in the Card Deck." to the chat log (colour 0xFFFFFFFF; the name is the null-terminated string at item record +0), and refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290). result 2, 6 or anything else: shows the matching message box; no more bytes are read. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C22, quest_cards_misc#13/#14): [itemtable+0x24] - the "%u / %u (%u%%)" label's TOTAL - is 880 in the EN client, not 64. In the decoded EN hii (4248 items) exactly 880 entries have CardNpc != 0, while only 64 have CardSpr != 0, so +0x24 counts CardNpc != 0 entries. The label reads n / 880 with floor(n*100/880)%, so 1 or 2 registered cards both show 0%. Before any 0x8A/0x8B the label shows the untouched template text "000/000 (000%)".

**Trigger.** Send in reply to C2S 0x64 [u16 card_item_id]. The client sends 0x64 when the player confirms dialog 0x292 (button 2) after choosing to register a card item. The item must be category 2 with the card flag [rec+0x14C] set, and not already in the 0x8A deck list. After sending, the client shows 'Waiting for the server to response.' and waits for this packet. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x64 (card register). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).

**Expected response.** none (the client consumes the card item locally on success)

**Gates / hazards.** Ignored (no bytes read) before the handler object is initialized by a successful S2C 0x02 login response. The waiting box is dismissed for every result. On success the client removes one card from its own inventory, so the server must NOT also send an inventory-removal packet (the card would be removed twice), but it must update its own inventory and deck records. If the client has no such item, nothing is registered client-side and no message appears, so client and server go out of sync. new_deck_count must be >= 1: with 0 the u16 id is written over charinfo+0xE30/0xE31, corrupting the count. Keep new_deck_count <= 50/51 (no bounds check; an i32 field sits at charinfo+0xE98). If new_deck_count is not old_count+1, the client's list gains gaps (a 0 id ends the UI list early) or overwrites existing entries. Category-1 items fail when inv+0x361 > 45. The chat string buffer is 64 bytes (sprintf_s).

**References.** PySlayer: no opcode_0x8B.py and no parse for C2S 0x64 (only a try/except import stub in server_packets/__init__.py). Our server: _dispatch has no C2S 0x64 branch and there is no 0x8B builder. The UI strings (strings.tsv 0x6F5190, 0x6F517C, 0x6F5FAC, 0x6F7F50, 0x6F5FF0) confirm this is the card-deck/dictionary system. No live capture exists.

**Open questions.**
- Values other than 1/2/6 all show the generic failure text; whether the original server used other codes (e.g. 3/4/5) with separate meanings is unknown.
- Whether the original server sent new_deck_count = old+1 or reused the slot some other way cannot be told from the client. Appending (old+1) is the only safe choice.
- Whether a separate inventory-sync packet is needed if the card stack was not in the client's inventory is untested.

| `message` | str[91] | Reply text typed by the player, NUL padded (buffer zeroed before copy). Same 91-byte size as the message field (+0x11..+0x6B) of the 0x7E-byte gift record. | window(0x3EF).control[8]+0xD1 edit text |

**Semantics.** Received-gift popup 0x3EF (shown for each gift record from S2C 0x6D whose item is giftable or a WS Gift Card 0xCFF..0xD04) lets the player type a thank-you note. Pressing control 2 sends a Note (0x4B) addressed to the gift sender with item id 9999, provided the message is non-empty, then removes the gift from the queue and shows the next one. No 'Waiting for the server' box is shown on this path.

**Trigger.** Gift-received popup (window 0x3EF) OK button (param_3 == 2) with non-empty reply text.

**Expected response.** Probably S2C 0x77 (SubHandler4 0x462ADD): closes box 0x16, u8 ok; if ok==1 { clears/closes Note window 0x3FD, u32 x -> FUN_00464380(ctx,x,1,0) (cash-item count update), 'You successfully sent the message.' } else 'Failed to send the message .' (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x77 SendMessageItemResult (echoing the real serial - serial 0 consumes nothing).

**Gates / hazards.** Sent only if FUN_0043df40(sender_name,0) passes (non-empty, no spaces) and message strlen > 0; an empty message silently skips the send but still dequeues. If name validation fails an error box is shown and the gift stays queued. Name copy is an unbounded strcpy into 17 bytes. No ResetBuffer before Adds. Server should NOT consume a note item when note_item_id == 9999; the 0x77 success path calls FUN_00464380 with the returned u32, so the value the server returns for a 9999 reply matters (unverified). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x77.

**References.** Opcode 0x4B also sent at site #55 (0x460F58? no: 0x46104? - Note window 0x3FD, u16 from window+0x40 = Note item id) with the identical layout. Item names from server/data/en/items_en.json: 1894 'Note (x1)', 3320 'Notes x11', 3327-3332 'WS Gift Card'. Not in PySlayer client parsers; not handled by windslayer_server.py _dispatch.

**Open questions.**
- What u32 should the server return in S2C 0x77 for a 9999 (free reply) note so that FUN_00464380 does not decrement a real item.
- Is 9999 treated by the original server as 'no item' or does it map to a special template?

### S2C 0x6D — GiftInboxList

*server → client* · key `0x6D` · confidence **high** · agreed (independent asm-only derivation matched) · server: **missing** · length: 1 + 126*gift_count

Locations: `0x00462E42` handler block start (case 0x6D); `0x00462E50` GetDataFromPacket u8 gift_count (IAT 0x4A4094); `0x00462E80` GetDataFromPacket char buffer, N=0x7E (126) per gift record (IAT 0x4A4098); `0x00462E8D` FUN_00459df0: append record to CPList at ctx+0x5F4

```
u8 gift_count
repeat(gift_count) {
  str[17] sender_name
  str[91] message
  u16 item_id
  bytes[16] unk_6e
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gift_count` | u8 | number of 126-byte gift records that follow | stack local [esp+0x13]; loop count (unsigned; 0 skips the loop but the HUD step still runs) |
| `sender_name` | str[17] | name of the character who sent the gift. It is sent back as the recipient name in the C2S 0x4B reply. | record+0x00 (heap block new(0x7E) appended to CPList ctx+0x5F4, ctx=game_state+0x700). FUN_004838c0(6) at 0x45E39A strc… |
| `message` | str[91] | gift message text (91 bytes, same size as the message field in C2S 0x4B) | record+0x11; FUN_0048a060(4) at 0x45E3DB strcpy's it into dialog 0x3EF control 4 (+0xD1) |
| `item_id` | u16 | gifted item id (for example 3327..3332 = WS Gift Card 1000..50000) | record+0x6C; read at 0x45E2BF/0x45E361, looked up in the item table ([ctx+0x1C], index id-1); the item name goes to dia… |
| `unk_6e` | bytes[16] | unknown trailing 16 bytes (possibly a serial or timestamp); send zeros | record+0x6E..+0x7D; stored but no reader found in the EN client |

**Semantics.** Adds pending received gifts to a client-side queue. For each record the client allocates 126 bytes (operator new, NOT zeroed), reads exactly 126 raw bytes into it and appends it to the CPList at cash-shop ctx+0x5F4 (ctx = game_state+0x700). The list is only cleared by FUN_0045B0F0 (session reset). After the loop, even when gift_count==0, it walks UI root ([ctx+0x18]) window list +0x5C0 for the window with id 3, sets UI+0x5F0 to that window, steps 5 nodes along its control list +0x8C and sets control+0x18 = 0 on the 6th control. +0x18 is the button state (0 = normal/enabled, 3 = disabled, per FUN_00489c50), so this enables a HUD gift icon. S2C 0x78 in SubHandler3 does the same with control 8. No popup comes from 0x6D itself. The gift dialog (window 0x3EF) is opened by FUN_0045E260, which runs at the end of the S2C 0x6A handler (cash shop list) and again after the user confirms a gift dialog. FUN_0045E260 takes the head record, looks up item_id and shows the dialog only if itemdef+0x1F0 != 0 or item_id is in 0xCFF..0xD04. Dialog contents: control 1 = item name, control 6 = sender_name, control 4 = message, control 8 = empty reply box (string at 0x6F2118).

**Trigger.** Send when the player has pending cash-shop gifts from other players, e.g. on entering the world or right after another player's C2S 0x4B gift. For the popup to appear, send it before S2C 0x6A (cash shop list).

**Expected response.** None directly. When the dialog's button 2 is pressed, the sender name passes FUN_0043df40 and the reply text is non-empty, the client sends C2S 0x4B: u16 9999, str[17] sender_name, str[91] reply_text (send site #51 @0x46098E). It then pops and frees the head gift and shows the next one. With empty text it only pops.

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler4 runs only when [ctx+0x14] (game_state ptr) and [ctx+0x18] (UI root) are non-null; otherwise it returns 0 and the opcode goes unhandled. Records are allocated with new and not memset: a short packet leaves heap garbage. sender_name and message are later copied with unbounded strcpy (loops at 0x483937 / 0x48A0E0), so both MUST be NUL-terminated inside their fields (name <=16 chars, message <=90 chars) or the copy overruns the 126-byte block and the controls. Queue-stall hazard: if the head record's item_id is not in the item table, or itemdef+0x1F0==0 and item_id is outside 3327..3332, the dialog never opens. Only the dialog pops the queue, so every later gift is blocked. Button 2 aborts without popping if sender_name fails FUN_0043df40 (empty, contains a space or a forbidden word such as 'gamemaster'/'yahoo'), so the gift cannot be dismissed. If UI window 3 or its 6th control is missing, the HUD step returns early (harmless). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C20, chat_mail_gm#11, chat_mail_gm#09): the map-change sequence RESETS the Gift HUD button (window 3 control 6) back to disabled even though the queue itself survives S2C 0x03. To relight the button after a map change or an 0x2F resync, send this packet again with count = 0 - that runs the HUD step without adding queue entries (records are append-only and would otherwise duplicate).

**References.** No PySlayer builder or parser for 0x6D (its doc only lists 0x6D under Packet_handler_4). Not in windslayer_server.py. The 126-byte layout matches S2C 0x78 (SubHandler3 @0x471A42: u8 count + 126-byte records into another list, enabling HUD window 3 control 8). The sender/message sizes (17/91) match both C2S 0x4B send sites (#51 @0x46098E with u16 9999; #55 @0x461064 with a real item id), so C2S 0x4B is 'send gift/note to player' and this record is its received side with item_id moved to +0x6C. Item names from server/data/en/items_en.json: 3327..3332 = WS Gift Card 1000/3000/5000/10000/30000/50000.

**Open questions.**
- Meaning of record bytes +0x6E..+0x7D (16 bytes): no reader found in the EN client (the list is only touched by FUN_00459df0, FUN_0045B0F0, FUN_0045E260 and FUN_00459f90).
- Meaning of itemdef+0x1F0 (the flag that lets non-gift-card items open the dialog); probably a 'giftable cash item' flag.
- Which UI element window id 3 / control #6 is (probably the HUD gift/present icon), and whether clicking it asks the server to open the cash shop (which would lead to 0x6A and the popup). Not traced.
- Whether the server should resend 0x6D after gifts are consumed: the client never removes records except through the dialog or a session reset, so resending duplicates them.

|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | u8 | Number of 126-byte memo records that follow (0..255; unsigned JBE / movzx loop bound). | stack local [ESP+0x12] |

Must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (<=16 chars). Part of… | memo record +0x00 |
| `text` | str[93] | Record +0x11..+0x6D. Memo body, drawn with CIME::DrawMultiText (controls 0x10/0x11, 0x47F304). NUL-terminate within 93 bytes (<=92 chars). | memo record +0x11 |
| `year` | u16 | Record +0x6E. First %u of '%u/%u/%u %u:%u' (SYSTEMTIME.wYear position). | memo record +0x6E |
| `month` | u16 | Record +0x70. Second %u (wMonth). | memo record +0x70 |
| `day_of_week` | u16 | Record +0x72. Not displayed (renderer skips it); SYSTEMTIME.wDayOfWeek position. | memo record +0x72 |
| `day` | u16 | Record +0x74. Third %u (wDay). | memo record +0x74 |
| `hour` | u16 | Record +0x76. Fourth %u (wHour). | memo record +0x76 |
| `minute` | u16 | Record +0x78. Fifth %u (wMinute). | memo record +0x78 |

| `millisecond` | u16 | Record +0x7C. Not referenced (wMilliseconds position). | memo record +0x7C |

**Semantics.** Delivers stored memos (offline messages). The handler reads a u8 count, then for each record mallocs 0x7E bytes, reads exactly 126 bytes into it with one GetDataFromPacket(char*, 0x7E) call, and appends the pointer to the messenger memo list (messenger+0x34; FUN_00459df0 keeps head +0x38, tail +0x3C, count +0x40). The list is NOT cleared first, and the memo window is not redrawn here. After the loop (also when count==0) it finds UI window id 3 in the UI root list (messenger+0x70 -> +0x5C0), sets it as current (+0x5F0), walks to its 8th control (+0x8C list, index 7) and sets control+0x18 = 0, which shows/enables the HUD memo button. When that is used, FUN_00470640 opens window 0x3FE, adds every record pointer to the window's item list (+0xAC) and shows the count. The window renderer FUN_0047db10 then draws record+0x00 as the sender name, record+0x11 as the multi-line body, and u16s at +0x6E/+0x70/+0x74/+0x76/+0x78 as 'Y/M/D h:m'. The 16 bytes at +0x6E..+0x7D match a Win32 SYSTEMTIME exactly: wDayOfWeek at +0x72 is skipped, and wSecond/wMilliseconds are unused. Selecting a row copies 17 bytes of the name into messenger+0xA4 (reply target). Closing the window asks 'All the messages will be deleted when closing the window. Will you continue?'. On OK the client sends C2S 0x44 (no body), sets window 3 control 8 to state 3, closes 0x3FE and frees the list.

**Trigger.** Server sends when the player has stored memos, typically after login/world entry (after S2C 0x03, which resets the list), and presumably with count=1 when a new memo arrives (append-only behaviour supports this). FUN_00483470 (world-entry UI setup) also checks the list count at +0x40 before touching window 3.

**Expected response.** None directly. Later, when the user confirms deleting memos on closing window 0x3FE, the client sends C2S 0x44 with 0 bytes (send site 0x47295F).

**Gates / hazards.** SubHandler3 gate: messenger+0x68/+0x70 must be non-null, otherwise the packet is dropped. The records accumulate: they are cleared only by the messenger reset on S2C 0x03 (FUN_0046f860 -> FUN_0046fc40) or by the C2S 0x44 confirm path, so resending the full list without a reset duplicates memos. count==0 still lights the window-3 control-8 memo button, so skip 0x78 entirely when there are no memos. sender_name must contain a NUL within its 17 bytes, or both Draw_Text and the strncpy to +0xA4 run on into the body. text must contain a NUL within its 93 bytes, or DrawMultiText runs into the date bytes. A truncated packet leaves the malloc'd (non-zeroed) record partly uninitialized. If window 3 or its 8th control is missing, the UI step is silently skipped. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C20, chat_mail_gm#11, chat_mail_gm#09): the map-change sequence RESETS the Msg HUD button (window 3 control 8) back to disabled even though the queue itself survives S2C 0x03. To relight the button after a map change or an 0x2F resync, send this packet again with count = 0 - that runs the HUD step without adding queue entries (records are append-only and would otherwise duplicate).

**References.** ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the wire at the call sites: u8 count at 0x471A50 (IAT 0x4A4094), then a loop (JL back-edge 0x471AA1) of malloc(0x7E) plus ONE GetDataFromPacket char-buffer read with N=0x7E (PUSH 0x7e at 0x471A7D, IAT 0x4A4098 at 0x471A80). The byte count 1+126*count is therefore identical. They disagree only on the 126-byte record: B gave an opaque str[126] 'text', A gave name[17] + text[93] + 8 u16. A is correct. FUN_00470640 (0x4706A6) passes each list record pointer (node+8) in EDX to FUN_00489a80, which appends it to window 0x3FE's item list at +0xAC (0x489ABB/0x489ACA). The window-0x3FE renderer in FUN_0047db10 fetches items from that same +0xAC list via FUN_00459fd0 and splits the record by control (jump table 0x481670 = {0x47E4E6, 0x47E4E6, 0x47E54F, 0x47E54F} for controls 0x0C..0x0F). Controls 0x0C/0x0D draw record+0x00 as a string (Draw_Text, PUSH EAX at 0x47E3F3). Controls 0x0E/0x0F do movzx word [EAX+0x78], [EAX+0x76], [EAX+0x74], [EAX+0x70], [EAX+0x6E] into sprintf '%u/%u/%u %u:%u' (0x47E584..0x47E5A7). Controls 0x10/0x11 do ADD EAX,0x11 then DrawMultiText (0x47F304/0x47F31D). FUN_00472900 strncpy's exactly 0x11 bytes from record+0 into messenger+0xA4 (0x4732B8..0x4732C2). So the record is a 17-byte name, a body at +0x11 running to +0x6D (93 bytes), and a 16-byte SYSTEMTIME at +0x6E, which fits the 0x7E size exactly. B's 'displayed as a single string' is wrong: +0 is drawn only up to the name's NUL, and the body and date come from fixed offsets. B's other observations (0x44 send on confirm, window 3 control 8 indicator, FUN_00483470 count check) are consistent with the code. Cross-refs: no PySlayer builder exists (opcode_0x78 import present, file missing). The opcode atlas lists 0x78 under Packet_handler_3 with no format. Our server has no builder. B notes the sibling S2C 0x6D (SubHandler4 0x462E42) has the same u8 + repeat 126-byte shape, but its record sub-layout was not re-verified here.

**Open questions.**
- The date field names are inferred from the SYSTEMTIME-shaped layout. The client prints +0x6E/+0x70/+0x74 as the first three numbers, so year/month/day is the natural order, but the server's original fill convention is unverified. +0x72, +0x7A and +0x7C are never read.
- Which C2S action creates a memo server-side (the send-memo request) was not identified in this batch.
- The initial visibility of window 3 control 8 before any 0x78 comes from UI resources, not from code seen here.
- Is 0x6D (same wire shape, list +0x5F4, window 3 control 6) a different message category with the same record layout? Not verified in this adjudication.

| `pos_y` | f64 | Current world Y. | entity+0x1288 |
| `elapsed_e50` | i32 | Second elapsed-time counter (+30 per tick while +0x8DF==0). Default 0. | entity+0xE50 |
| `facing` | u8 | Horizontal facing: 2 and 6 are opposite directions (confusion effects swap 2<->6), 8 = neutral/default. Same field as bits 0-1 of the 0x1B/0x0D state blob. | entity+0x8B3 |
| `motion` | u8 | Motion/stance code (0 idle; AI writes 1,3,4,5,6). Same field as bits 2-4 of the 0x1B blob. | entity+0x8B4 |
| `motion_8b5` | u8 | Motion sub-field (bits 5-8 of the 0x1B blob). Default 0. | entity+0x8B5 |
| `motion_8b6` | u8 | Motion sub-field (bits 9-11 of the 0x1B blob; value 3 and 4 are tested). Default 0. | entity+0x8B6 |
| `unk_8da` | bool | Flag, default 0. | entity+0x8DA |
| `unk_8df` | bool | Flag, default 0; while it's 0, +0xE50 keeps counting. | entity+0x8DF |
| `unk_8dc` | bool | Flag, default 0. | entity+0x8DC |
| `unk_8dd` | bool | Flag, default 0. | entity+0x8DD |
| `unk_8de` | bool | Flag, default 0. | entity+0x8DE |
| `cur_hp` | u16 | Current HP, zero-extended into the u32 at +0x9C. It overwrites the max-HP default RegisterLocalPlayer copies from +0x110C. 0 = corpse (live-verified: unhittable). | stack [base+0x110] -> entity+0x9C |
| `timer_d94` | u32 | Counter that grows by 30 per tick up to 500 while motion==6 (FUN_00413920). Default 0. | entity+0xD94 |
| `server_controlled` | bool | Aggro / server-driven flag (PySlayer comment: 어그로 'aggro'). When nonzero the client wander AI is off (FUN_00417e10 needs it ==0) and the monster follows queued 0x1B commands. Also gates the next field. | entity+0x8E4 |
| `cmd_hold_ms` | u32 | Present only if server_controlled!=0. Initial command hold timer (the same field 0x1B's hold_ms feeds; -30 per tick). | entity+0xE48 |

**Semantics.** Creates one NPC/monster entity per block. For each block the client: (1) allocates a 0x15F0-byte entity, runs the ctor, then memsets it to 0. (2) Reads template_index (+0xE60) and uid (+0x84), sets alive/type byte +0x98=4 (template NPC/monster) and clears name[17]. (3) Looks up the template list at game_state+0x4E0 by template_index. On a hit it copies the template name into entity+0 and sets +0x11DC=record (nameplate). It copies record+0x644 (type/class) to +0xE64, +0x660 to +0xE68, +0x63C to +0xE6C, +0x648 (max HP) to +0x110C, +0x650 to +0x119C, +0x658 to +0x1130, +0x654 to +0x1134, +0x680 to +0xDE8, +0x67C to +0xDEC and +0x65C to +0x1140. Float +0x664 goes to f64 +0x11E0. For type 4..7 it sets +0x1150=1..4 and puts record+0x66C in +0x1160/+0x1164/+0x1168/+0x116C. It also copies +0x668 to +0x1154, 10 dwords from +0x250 to +0xDC0, and level byte +0x640 to +0x99. (4) Reads effect_count and applies each effect via FUN_00424e20. (5) Calls RegisterLocalPlayer. For type 4 that stamps timeGetTime into +0xE54, applies defaults (0x8B3=8, 0x8BD=2, 0x8CF=8, 0x904=8, HP=max) and adds the entity to the scene list. If uid==scene+0x220 it also becomes scene+0x970 (local player). (6) Reads the remaining fields, which overwrite those defaults. (7) Reopens the template sprite file. (8) Seeds the per-entity RNG table. The handler never looks for an existing entity with the same uid.

**Trigger.** When a monster/NPC enters the player's view: on map entry for every mob in the map, and on monster respawn.

**Expected response.** none

**Gates / hazards.** template_index must resolve (1..count of game_state+0x4E0 list). If it doesn't, +0x11DC stays NULL. Memory notes report a NULL-deref crash at 0x43C4C2 (nameplate strlen) for alive==4 entities without +0x11DC, and at minimum the body/name won't render. uid must NOT equal scene+0x220 (the local player uid, 1 on our server), or the monster is registered as the local player. There is no uid dedup: resending 0x1A for an existing uid seems to add a second entity with the same uid (FUN_004189f0 lookups return the first match). That fits the observed 'snap back to spawn' jitter, and it leaks entities. Every 0x1A also calls CSpriteControl::OpenFromFile again for the template (record+0x678 is overwritten), which may cost time or memory when spawning in bulk. The memset after the ctor zeroes the CPList vftables at +0x1350/+0x1360/+0x1370/+0x1588 (client bug; the lists still work because FUN_00459df0 doesn't use the vftable). cur_hp=0 gives a corpse. effect entries whose id has no definition are silently dropped.

**References.** The field order and widths match windslayer_server.py _build_opcode_1A (line 1494) byte for byte, so the layout is correct. Disagreements about values: (a) The server sends +0x8B3..+0x8B6 as 127,0,0,1 ('ip'). These are facing/motion bytes; 127 isn't a valid facing, so 8 (or 2/6),0,0,0 is recommended. (b) The server sends action_state(+0x904)=0; the client's idle is 8. (c) unk_8cf=1, unk_954=32 and action_elapsed(+0xE00)=501 were copied from 0x07. The client's own defaults are 8, 0 and 0. (d) The server's 'inner loop = action 0xB3B idle' is really a status-effect entry (FUN_00424e20, skill table scene+0xF84). The live finding that count=0 leaves the body invisible is recorded but not explained statically. Matches memory project_local_player_spawn.md's 88-byte layout (83 bytes + opcode = 84 with no hold field; 88 includes the optional u32), but that note calls 0x1A the LOCAL player spawn. In fact 0x1A is a generic template (monster/NPC) spawn that becomes local only when uid==scene+0x220, which agrees with reference_combat_render.md. PySlayer opcode_0x1A.py targets the newer KR layout (different order: second loop, f64 pos early, 6 base-pos u32s, 7 bools) and must NOT be used for EN. The KR Hex-Rays case 0x1A has the same field families.

**Open questions.**
- The meanings of unk_954, unk_8cf, unk_8bd, unk_8d9, unk_8da/8dc/8dd/8de and timer_d94 are only partly known (defaults are from RegisterLocalPlayer).
- Whether a duplicate uid from a resent 0x1A really leaves two entities (no dedup in the handler or RegisterLocalPlayer was seen, but a dedup elsewhere in the per-frame code wasn't ruled out).
- Why effect_count=0 made the body invisible in the live test (the memory note says an effect 0xB3B is needed). Statically the effect list is a status-effect array; the render dependency wasn't traced.
- The client-side wander AI (FUN_00417e10) needs type(+0xE64)>2, server_controlled==0, an empty 0x1B queue and +0xE48==0. Why mobs were observed static in-client wasn't resolved (possibly scene+0xF88+0x70 or the caller FUN_0042b260's gates).
